children.translated_text: <s>Sātvatatantra</s>, First Chapter
The blessed <s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ya eko bahudhā kṛṣṇaḥ sṛṣṭyādau bahudheyate /
children.translated_text: He who is one, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who at the beginning of creation becomes manifold in many ways —

children.text: tam ahaṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmi paramānandavigraham // SatvT_1.1
children.translated_text: I take refuge in Him, whose form is supreme bliss. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.1
Seated on the summit of <s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme bestower of auspiciousness,
Was questioned by <s>Nārada</s>, who was devoted to the welfare of all beings: // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.2
'O Blessed One, I wish to hear of <s>Hari</s>, the performer of wondrous deeds,
The various playful forms (<s>līlā-tanu</s>) of the immeasurable Lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the all-pervading one. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.3

children.text: yadarthaṃ yatsvarūpaṃ ca yadyat kāle yathā rataḥ /
children.translated_text: For what purpose, in what form, in which [form] at which time, and how the Lord, self-abiding,

children.text: gṛhṇāti bhagavān svasthas tan mamākhyātum arhasi // SatvT_1.4
children.translated_text: Assumes [these forms] — please narrate this to me. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.4
The cause of the incarnations, and the long-standing origin of [His] embodiment —

children.text: prathamaṃ tattvato brūhi tvaṃ parāparavittamaḥ // SatvT_1.5
children.translated_text: First tell me this in truth, O you who are the greatest knower of the higher and the lower.' // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.5
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:
'O greatly fortunate one, O best of devotees of the Lord, you have asked
That by which I am rightly impelled to describe the glories of the Lord. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.6
Of the incarnations and the splendor (<s>virāj</s>) of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>, O great-minded one,

children.text: kathane naiva paśyāmi pāraṃ varṣaśatair api /
children.translated_text: In their narration, I see no end even in a hundred years.

children.text: tathāpi sāram uddhṛtya tantrarūpeṇa nārada // SatvT_1.7
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, extracting the essence, in the form of a <s>tantra</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.7
I shall describe just as it was spoken by the compassionate Lord Himself,
Having first offered salutations, preceded by 'Victory!', to the Lord in the form of the Cowherd (<s>Gopāla</s>). // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.8
I shall expound the [text] called <s>Sātvatatantra</s>, which increases devotion to the Lord.

children.text: yadāsīd ekam avyaktaṃ nityaṃ cidrūpam avyayam // SatvT_1.9
children.translated_text: When there was the One, unmanifest, eternal, of the nature of consciousness, imperishable, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.9

children.text: brahmeti yad vidur vijñā bhagavān iti sātvatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Which the wise call <s>Brahman</s> and the <s>Sātvatās</s> [call] <s>Bhagavān</s> —

children.text: tadāsantam ivātmānaṃ matvā dṛśya vinā vibhuḥ // SatvT_1.10
children.translated_text: Then the all-pervading Lord, considering Himself as though non-existent without [anything] visible, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.10

children.text: dviprakāram abhūt satyaṃ sattābhūtvā svayaṃ svayam /
children.translated_text: Became twofold in reality, having become existence by Himself, of Himself.

children.text: tac cicchaktisvarūpeṇa prakṛtiḥ puruṣo mahān // SatvT_1.11
children.translated_text: That [twofold reality], in the form of the power of consciousness (<s>cit-śakti</s>), [became] <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and the great <s>Puruṣa</s> (supreme Person). // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.11
The sole abode of all worlds is called <s>Bhagavān</s>.
His power is <s>Prakṛti</s>, having the form of cause and effect, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.12
Which divides itself again in the form of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).

children.text: yaḥ kālas taṃ vadanty eke hareś ceṣṭāṃ duranvayām // SatvT_1.13
children.translated_text: What some call <s>Kāla</s> (Time) — the action of <s>Hari</s>, difficult to trace — // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.13
Because of the disturbance of the three <s>guṇas</s> from which [creation] formerly came into separate existence,
And because of which the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) obtains the fruits of good and evil — // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.14
That is <s>karma</s> (action), the cause of the birth of the great [cosmic egg], having an unmanifest form.

children.text: bhāvānāṃ pariṇāmo hi yato bhavati sarvadā // SatvT_1.15
children.translated_text: For the transformation of all entities always arises from it. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.15
The knowers of the <s>Veda</s> call that very [principle], which is subtle in form, <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature).

children.text: ukto 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ sākṣād īśvaro bhagavattanuḥ // SatvT_1.16
children.translated_text: This <s>Puruṣa</s> is declared to be directly the Lord, the body of <s>Bhagavān</s>. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.16
Established in <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Karma</s>, and <s>Svabhāva</s>, He impels <s>Prakṛti</s>.
<s>Prakṛti</s>, the divine goddess, presided over by <s>Puruṣa</s>, containing the [three] <s>guṇas</s>, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.17
Became the <s>Mahat-tattva</s> (great principle), whose nature is comprehensive knowledge and action.

children.text: tasmāj jāto hy ahaṃkāras trividho daivanoditāt // SatvT_1.18
children.translated_text: From that, impelled by the divine [will], <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) arose, threefold: // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.18

children.text: vaikārikas taijasaś ca tāmasaś ceti yaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaikārika</s> (sattvic), the <s>Taijasa</s> (rajasic), and the <s>Tāmasa</s> (tamasic) — so they know it.
From the <s>Vaikārika</s> arose the mind and the gods, lords of knowledge and action: // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.19
<s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) and <s>Keśa</s> (?), the Directions, <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), and the <s>Nāsatyas</s> (Aśvins) — the impellers of knowledge;
<s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Kopa</s> (?) — these are the impellers of action. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.20
From the <s>Rājasa</s> (rajasic <s>ahaṅkāra</s>) arose [the faculties] whose nature is the grasping of sense-objects, knowledge, and action.

children.text: tvagrasajñā śrutiś cakṣur ghrāṇaṃ buddhiś ca tanmayāḥ // SatvT_1.21
children.translated_text: Skin, tongue, hearing, sight, and smell, and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — these are constituted of knowledge; // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.21
Speech, hands, the organ of excretion, the generative organ, and locomotion — these are constituted of action.

children.text: tāmasāt pañcabhūtāni tanmātrāṇi ca bhāgaśaḥ // SatvT_1.22
children.translated_text: From the <s>Tāmasa</s> (tamasic <s>ahaṅkāra</s>) arose the five gross elements and the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>), each in part. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.22

children.text: prathamaṃ tāmasāj jajñe śabdas tasmād abhūn nabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: First, from the <s>Tāmasa</s> arose sound (<s>śabda</s>); from that came space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: śabdarūpāt tu nabhasaḥ sparśas tasmād abhūn marut // SatvT_1.23
children.translated_text: From space, possessing the quality of sound, arose touch (<s>sparśa</s>); from that came wind (<s>vāyu</s>). // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.23

children.text: maruto 'bhūt tatas tejas tejaso rūpam uttamam /
children.translated_text: From wind arose fire (<s>tejas</s>); from fire, the supreme [quality of] form (<s>rūpa</s>).

children.text: rūpamātrād raso jajñe tasmād āpo 'bhavan śucīḥ // SatvT_1.24
children.translated_text: From the subtle element of form arose taste (<s>rasa</s>); from that, the pure waters came into being. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.24

children.text: adbhyo jāto gandhaguṇo gandhād bhūmir ajāyata /
children.translated_text: From water arose the quality of smell (<s>gandha</s>); from smell, earth was born.
<s>Mahat-tattva</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, together with sound, touch, and fire, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.25
Taste and smell — all these are remembered as modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s>,

children.text: śabdasya prakṛter eva saṃdṛśyante yato budhaiḥ // SatvT_1.26
children.translated_text: Since they are seen by the wise as [arising] from the <s>Prakṛti</s> of sound [i.e., from the primordial <s>Prakṛti</s>]. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.26
Therefore, those that are <s>prakṛtis</s> (primary causes) [in one context] are known as <s>vikāras</s> (modifications) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (transformations) [in another].

children.text: ākāśe śabdamātraṃ syād vāyau sparśaḥ saśabdakaḥ // SatvT_1.27
children.translated_text: In space there is only the subtle element of sound; in wind there is touch together with sound. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.27

children.text: rūpaṃ tejasi śabdaś ca sparśaś caiva jale tathā /
children.translated_text: In fire there is form, sound, and touch; in water likewise,

children.text: rasaśabdasparśarūpaṃ pṛthivyāṃ sarvam eva hi // SatvT_1.28
children.translated_text: Taste, sound, touch, and form; in earth, indeed, all [five qualities are present]. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.28
Because the qualities of the causes are present in the effects, therefore

children.text: dṛśyate tv adhikas tatra guṇo yāvati kaś ca ha // SatvT_1.29
children.translated_text: Each additional quality is seen in each successive [element]. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.29
The <s>Mahat</s> and other principles, belonging to the great <s>Puruṣa</s>,
Are the forms [taken by Him for] the descent into effects — know this, O best of the twice-born. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.30
Having gathered all these [principles], by the will of <s>Puruṣa</s>,
[The principles], with their respective portions, produced <s>Virāj</s> (the cosmic being), whose nature is the universe. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.31
His internal cavity extended fifty <s>koṭis</s> (five hundred million [yojanas]).

children.text: daśottarādhikair etaiḥ saptabhir bahir āvṛtam // SatvT_1.32
children.translated_text: He was enveloped externally by these seven [sheaths], each ten times greater [than the previous]. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.32

children.text: tam āhuḥ puruṣasyaiva gehaṃ yatrāviśat svayam /
children.translated_text: They call that the abode of <s>Puruṣa</s> Himself, into which He Himself entered,
Since [without Him] the entire expanse was merely inert. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.33
Since the principles arose from <s>Nara</s> (the Supreme Person), in the aggregate called <s>Nāra</s>,

children.text: ayanaṃ tasya yad abhūt tasmān nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // SatvT_1.34
children.translated_text: His dwelling (<s>ayana</s>) being in that — therefore He is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.34
Since the Lord dwelt in the <s>Virāj</s> body, [which is] called a 'city' (<s>pura</s>),

children.text: ataḥ puruṣanāmānam avāpa puruṣaḥ paraḥ // SatvT_1.35
children.translated_text: Therefore the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> obtained the name '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (dweller in the city). // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.35
When the Lord, the divine one, the expansion of the primordial <s>Prakṛti</s>,

children.text: nārāyaṇena rūpeṇa virajam aviśat svayam // SatvT_1.36
children.translated_text: In the form of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, Himself entered the <s>Virāj</s>, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.36

children.text: tadā cetanam āpādya cirād vigraha utthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having bestowed consciousness, [the <s>Virāj</s>] arose from its long [dormancy] as an embodied [being],
Designated by the term 'aggregate' (<s>samaṣṭi</s>), the support of the fourteen worlds. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.37

children.text: yasmin carācaraṃ bhūtaṃ sraṣṭā brahmāhares tanūḥ /
children.translated_text: In whom exists all that is moving and unmoving — the creator <s>Brahmā</s>, a body of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: tatra lokamayaṃ yāvat taṃ virājaṃ vido viduḥ // SatvT_1.38
children.translated_text: Inasmuch as He comprises the worlds — that <s>Virāj</s>, the knowers know. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.38
The individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) who presides over it [the <s>Virāj</s>] is called <s>Vairāja</s>, designated as <s>Puruṣa</s>;
And the God who is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) within it is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, free from affliction, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.39
The sole abode of all individual souls — Him they declare to be <s>Bhagavān</s>,
The treasury, the seed, the imperishable [source] of thousands of incarnations. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.40
From whose portion, endowed with <s>rajas</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> was born for [the task of] creation,

children.text: viṣṇuḥ sattvaguṇādhīśaḥ sthitau sthāpayituṃ jagat // SatvT_1.41
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of the <s>sattva</s> quality, [was born] for preservation, to sustain the world; // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.41
Through <s>tamas</s>, the all-pervading Lord became <s>Rudra</s> in form, for dissolution.

children.text: ete viṣṇor guṇamayā avatārāḥ kriyākṛtāḥ // SatvT_1.42
children.translated_text: These are the incarnations of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, brought about by [His] action. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.42

children.text: eṣām aṃśāvatārān me nibodha gadato mama /
children.translated_text: Hear from me as I tell you the partial incarnations (<s>aṃśāvatāra</s>) of these.

children.text: brahmaṇo 'ṃśena samabhūn marīcir atrir aṅgirāḥ // SatvT_1.43
children.translated_text: From a portion of <s>Brahmā</s> arose <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.43

children.text: pulastyaḥ pulahaś caiva kratur dakṣo dvijottama /
children.translated_text: <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, O best of the twice-born,

children.text: bhṛgur vasiṣṭho 'tharvā ca kardamādyāḥ prajeśvarāḥ // SatvT_1.44
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Vasiṣ���ha</s>, <s>Atharvā</s>, and <s>Kardama</s> and others, the lords of creation. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.44

children.text: eṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca prapautrāś ca mahaujasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons, of great vigor,
All arose for the purpose of creation, endowed with the power of <s>Bhagavān</s>. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.45

children.text: viṣṇor aṃśena samabhūd dharmo yajño bṛhattrivṛt /
children.translated_text: From a portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s> arose <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Yajña</s> (Sacrifice), and <s>Bṛhattrivṛt</s>;
The fourteen <s>Manus</s>, beginning with <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, renowned throughout the worlds. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.46

children.text: eṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca tathendrādyāś ca devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their sons and grandsons, and likewise <s>Indra</s> and the other deities,

children.text: viṣṇvaṃśayuktā lokānāṃ pālakāḥ kathitā mayā // SatvT_1.47
children.translated_text: Endowed with <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s portion, have been described by me as the protectors of the worlds. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.47
From a portion of <s>Rudra</s>, the hosts of <s>Rudras</s> were born by the hundreds, separately;

children.text: sarpāś ca śataśo jātā ye ca hiṃsrāḥ svabhāvataḥ // SatvT_1.48
children.translated_text: And serpents were born by the hundreds, and those who are violent by nature. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.48
These have been briefly described as the portions of <s>Rudra</s>, abiding in <s>tamas</s>,
Destroyers of this world, of terrible form and extraordinary nature. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.49

children.text: atha te sampravakṣyāmi līlādehān hareḥ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell you separately of the sport-bodies (<s>līlā-deha</s>) of <s>Hari</s>.
Hear of those [forms] made of pure <s>sattva</s>, peaceful, the abodes of the love of the world. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.50

children.text: ya īśa eko bhagavān ananto brahmasvarūpī puruṣo 'dhiyajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is the one Lord, <s>Bhagavān</s>, infinite, of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Person, the Lord of sacrifice,

children.text: pātuṃ punar viśvam asau svakāryaṃ bheje tanūs taṃ praṇamāmi kṛṣṇam // SatvT_1.51
children.translated_text: To protect this universe, His own creation, He assumed bodies — to that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> I bow. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.51

body.text: iti śrīsātvatatantre śivanāradasaṃvāde prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ // SatvT_1.52
body.translated_text: Thus ends the First Chapter in the <s>Sātvatatantra</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Nārada</s>. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 1.52

children.translated_text: <s>Sātvatatantra</s>, Second Chapter
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: sākṣād babhūva bhagavān paripātum īśo vedān yugādisamaye hayaśīrṣanāmā /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself appeared, the Lord, named <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> (Horse-headed), to protect the <s>Vedas</s> at the beginning of the cosmic age;

children.text: hatvā suretaravarau madhukaiṭabhākhyau nastaś cakāra viśrutīḥ śrutibhir vimṛgyaḥ // SatvT_2.1
children.translated_text: Having slain the two chief demons called <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, He restored the renowned scriptures — He who is sought through the <s>śrutis</s>. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.1

children.text: lokān nivṛttiparatāṃ pracikīrṣur ādau bhūtvā catuḥsanatayā bhagavān vimuktyai /
children.translated_text: Intending to turn the worlds toward cessation [of worldly activity], in the beginning, having become fourfold as the <s>Sanaka</s> [brothers], <s>Bhagavān</s> [appeared] for liberation;

children.text: provāca yogam amalaṃ viśadāśayebhyo bhogān viraktiparatāṃ svayam ācacāra // SatvT_2.2
children.translated_text: He taught pure <s>yoga</s> to those of clear understanding, and Himself practiced renunciation and detachment from enjoyments. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.2

children.text: deveṣu nāradatanur bhagavān viśuddhaṃ naiṣkarmyayogam avahat khalu pāñcarātram /
children.translated_text: Among the gods, <s>Bhagavān</s> in the body of <s>Nārada</s> bore the pure <s>naiṣkarmya-yoga</s> (yoga of actionlessness), namely <s>Pāñcarātra</s>;

children.text: dharmaṃ tathā bhagavatā kathitaṃ viśeṣaśiṣyeṣv asau paramanirvṛtim ādadhānam // SatvT_2.3
children.translated_text: Likewise, he proclaimed the <s>dharma</s> taught by <s>Bhagavān</s> to special disciples — [the <s>dharma</s>] that bestows supreme bliss. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.3

children.text: ādau dadhāra dharaṇīdharaṇāya dhātuḥ svāyambhuvoktiparipālakakāla eva /
children.translated_text: In the beginning, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the teacher of all, assumed the body of a great boar (<s>Varāha</s>) for the purpose of supporting the earth, at the very time of fulfilling the command of <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Manu];

children.text: nārāyaṇo 'khilagurur gurukoladehaṃ tenāhanad ditisutaṃ daśanāgraghātaiḥ // SatvT_2.4
children.translated_text: With that [form], He slew the son of <s>Diti</s> [the demon <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>] with the blows of the tips of His tusks. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.4

children.text: bhūmer adho dharaṇimaṇḍalam aprameyaḥ śeṣākhya āsa jagataḥ sthitaye nitāntam /
children.translated_text: Below the earth, the immeasurable one named <s>Śeṣa</s> existed to hold the sphere of the earth, for the stability of the world;

children.text: yasmin kalārpitam idaṃ likhivac cakāsti nāgādhipair munigaṇaiḥ parisevitāṅghriḥ // SatvT_2.5
children.translated_text: On whom this [universe] rests, placed [there] as a [mere] part, shining like a [small] mark, whose feet are worshipped by the serpent-kings and the hosts of sages. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.5

children.text: tasmād adhaḥ kamaṭha āsa viśālarūpī brahmāṇḍabhāṇḍaparivistṛtādivyakāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Below him, the Tortoise (<s>Kamaṭha</s>) existed, vast in form, with a divine body spread across the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg);

children.text: śeṣo 'pi yatra paribhāti sutantutulyo yaṃ cāryamā pitṛpatiḥ samupāsate vai // SatvT_2.6
children.translated_text: Upon whom even <s>Śeṣa</s> appears like a fine thread, and whom <s>Aryaman</s>, the lord of the ancestors, worships. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.6

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dṛśārdhavayasāpi vihāya mātur dehaṃ dhruvaṃ madhuvane tapasābhitaptam /
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Dhruva</s>, though but half his age, who had left his mother's body and was performing austerity in the <s>Madhuvana</s> forest,

children.text: bhūtvā kṛpāmayavapur bhagavān svalokaṃ prādāt stuvanti yatayo munayo 'pi yaṃ vai // SatvT_2.7
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān</s>, having become a body of compassion, granted him His own world — whom even ascetics and sages praise. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.7

children.text: ālokya kardamatapo bhagavān vibhūtyai saṃśuddhadivyavapuṣāvirabhūt saśuklaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beholding the austerity of <s>Kardama</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for [granting] prosperity, manifested with a pure divine form, resplendent;

children.text: tasmā adād varamajātmajaputrarūpam ānandabindupayasā ca cakāra tīrtham // SatvT_2.8
children.translated_text: To him He gave as a boon a son in the form of His own unborn Self, and made a holy site (<s>tīrtha</s>) with the waters of the bliss-drop (<s>ānanda-bindu</s>). // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.8

children.text: yajñe sa eva rucinā manuputriputra āhūtisūtir asurāraṇivahnikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: In sacrifice, He Himself [appeared] as <s>Ruci</s>'s [son], a grandson of <s>Manu</s> — the one born from the oblation, like a sacrificial fire against demons;

children.text: trailokyagopanavidhau suranātha īśa nāmnā suyajña iti viśrutakīrtir āśiḥ // SatvT_2.9
children.translated_text: For the protection of the three worlds, O lord of the gods, He [appeared] with the name <s>Suyajña</s>, of renowned fame — a blessing! // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.9

children.text: siddheśvaraś ca samabhūt kapilākhya īśaḥ śrīdevahūtitanayo vitatāna tasyai /
children.translated_text: And the Lord of <s>Siddhas</s> appeared, the Lord named <s>Kapila</s>, the son of <s>Devahūti</s>; to her He expounded

children.text: yogaṃ svaśaktisahitaṃ cidacidvibhāgaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ tathā svabhimukheṣu jagāda śuddham // SatvT_2.10
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> together with His own power, the discrimination of conscious and unconscious (<s>cit-acit-vibhāga</s>), and likewise pure <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, to those devoted to Him. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.10

children.text: yogeśvaro 'tritanayo bhagavān ananto dattākhya āsa samatāvavadat svacaryām /
children.translated_text: The Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, the son of <s>Atri</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the infinite one named <s>Datta</s> (<s>Dattātreya</s>), declared the discipline of equanimity as His own practice,

children.text: prahlādahaihayayaduṣv aparāyaṇeṣu śiṣyeṣu śikṣitakathāṃ kathayan gurubhyaḥ // SatvT_2.11
children.translated_text: Teaching the well-instructed discourse to <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Haihaya</s>, <s>Yadu</s>, and other devoted disciples, [and transmitting it] to teachers. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.11

children.text: nārāyaṇo nara ṛṣipravarāvabhūtāṃ dharmasya dakṣaduhitary adhimūrtipatnyām /
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Nara</s>, the foremost of sages, were born to <s>Dharma</s> [from his wife], the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, [who was] the spouse of the supreme embodiment;

children.text: dhīropakārakaruṇāśayakāyaśuddhaṃ tīvraṃ tapaḥ pracaratāṃ surarājatāpam // SatvT_2.12
children.translated_text: They practiced intense austerity, heroic, beneficent, compassionate in intent, pure in body — [their austerity] causing distress to the king of the gods. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.12

children.text: nābher abhūd ṛṣabhasaṃjñasadāptakāmo yogeśvaraḥ sutaśatair avadat prajābhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: From [the womb of] <s>Nābhi</s> was born the one named <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, ever fulfilled in desires, the Lord of <s>Yoga</s>; He taught <s>dharma</s> to His hundred sons and to the people,

children.text: dharmaṃ tataḥ paramayogijanāvacaryāṃ naiṣkarmyalakṣaṇaparāṃ svayam ācacāra // SatvT_2.13
children.translated_text: Then the supreme practice followed by yogis, characterized by <s>naiṣkarmya</s> (actionlessness) — that He Himself practiced. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.13

children.text: dhātrantike susanakādibhir īryamāṇe cetoguṇān vigalituṃ bhagavān sa haṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the presence of the Creator (<s>Dhātṛ</s>), when <s>Sanaka</s> and the others were striving to dissolve the qualities of the mind, <s>Bhagavān</s> [appeared] as the <s>Haṃsa</s> (Swan);

children.text: provāca tattvam amalaṃ sadayārdracittā yasmād guṇāguṇavibhāgam abhūn munīnām // SatvT_2.14
children.translated_text: He taught the pure truth with compassionate and tender heart — from which arose the discrimination of <s>guṇas</s> and non-<s>guṇas</s> among the sages. // <s>Sātvatatantra</s> 2.14

children.text: vene mṛte dvijajanair anu bāhuyugmaṃ saṃmathyamānasamaye pṛthurūpa āsīt /
children.translated_text: When <s>Vena</s> had died, as the twice-born people were churning the pair of arms [of the corpse], at that time [He appeared] in the form of <s>Pṛthu</s>.

children.text: lokakṣudhāṃ praśamayan pṛthivīṃ dudoha sarvāṇi bhūtikaraṇāni ca sarvabhūtyai // SatvT_2.15
children.translated_text: appeasing the hunger of the world, he milked the earth and [milked] all means of prosperity for the welfare of all beings. // SatvT_2.15

children.text: dakṣasya yajñavihite śivaśaktihetoḥ prāptājyabhāmam adhikaṃ bhṛguṇābhidattam /
children.translated_text: At the sacrifice arranged by <s>Dakṣa</s>, for the sake of <s>Śiva</s>'s power, having obtained excessive anger, being struck by <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: tatrāṣṭabāhur abhavad bhagavān bhavāya prāptā nutiḥ suranarādikṛtāpi tena // SatvT_2.16
children.translated_text: there the Lord became eight-armed for the welfare [of all]; praise was offered to him by gods, men, and others. // SatvT_2.16

children.text: jātaḥ priyavratakule gaya ity udārakīrtiṃ tatāna bhagavān tanuvāṅmanobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Born in the family of <s>Priyavrata</s>, the Lord, known as <s>Gaya</s>, spread noble fame through body, speech, and mind;

children.text: tenāpi yajñatanur īśvara indrarūpī spardhāṃ cakāra mahatāṃ madam ādadhānaḥ // SatvT_2.17
children.translated_text: with him too, the Lord in the form of <s>Indra</s>, the sacrifice-bodied ruler, competed, bearing great pride. // SatvT_2.17

children.text: saṃvatsarasya tanayaḥ sa ha yāminīnām ālokanādivividhaṃ mudam ācikīrṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: He, the son of <s>Saṃvatsara</s>, of the nights, desiring to create various delights such as sight and so forth,

children.text: śrīkāmadevavapuṣā hy avatīrya devo devyomayā madanakelibhir ārarāma // SatvT_2.18
children.translated_text: the Lord descended in the beautiful form of <s>Kāmadeva</s> and sported with the goddess <s>Ūrmayā</s> in amorous play. // SatvT_2.18

children.text: prācīnabarhitanayāṃs tapasā sutaptān dṛṣṭvā svaśāntavapuṣāvirabhūd anantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the sons of <s>Prācīnabarhi</s> scorched by intense austerity, <s>Ananta</s> manifested in his own tranquil form;

children.text: dattvā svapādabhajanaṃ vasatāṃ gṛheṣu kanyāṃ ca vṛkṣajanitām adiśad dayāluḥ // SatvT_2.19
children.translated_text: granting them worship of his own feet while dwelling in their homes, the compassionate one also bestowed upon them a maiden born from a tree. // SatvT_2.19

children.text: svārociṣe tuṣitayā dvijavedaśīrṣāj jāto vibhuḥ sakaladharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Svārociṣa</s> [<s>manvantara</s>], born from the head of the twice-born Vedas through <s>Tuṣitā</s>, <s>Vibhu</s> was the foremost among all upholders of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: yad brahmacaryāniyamān ṛṣayo 'py aśikṣan sākṣāj jagadgurutayāvacacāra śuddhān // SatvT_2.20
children.translated_text: from whom even the sages learned the rules of <s>brahmacarya</s> — he practiced them purely, being directly the teacher of the world. // SatvT_2.20

children.text: dharmād abhūt sutatayā bhagavāṃs tṛtīye manvantare trijagataḥ sthitaye kṛpāluḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Dharma</s>, in the third <s>manvantara</s>, the compassionate Lord was born as a son for the sustenance of the three worlds;

children.text: śrīsatyasena iti durjanayakṣarakṣān yas tān apāharad asau suranāthamitraḥ // SatvT_2.21
children.translated_text: named <s>Śrī Satyasena</s>, he who removed the wicked <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> — he was the friend of <s>Indra</s>. // SatvT_2.21

children.text: turye 'ntare sarasi vāraṇarājarājaṃ grāheṇa tīvrabalinā parikarṣayantam /
children.translated_text: In the fourth age, in a lake, the king of elephant-kings being dragged by a mighty crocodile of terrible strength —

children.text: nārāyaṇety abhihite harir uddadhāra tasmād bhavārṇavajalād api devarājaḥ // SatvT_2.22
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> rescued him when [the elephant] cried out '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!' — from that ocean of existence too [he rescues], the king of gods. // SatvT_2.22

children.text: vaikuṇṭha āsa bhagavān dvijavarya mudrā devyā mayā tadanurūpajayābhidhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord was <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, O best of twice-born, by name corresponding to his consort <s>Jayā</s>, with the <s>mudrā</s> [and] the goddess <s>Māyā</s>;

children.text: vaikuṇṭhadarśanam akārayad aprameyas tasyāu pañcamamanoḥ samaye prasiddham // SatvT_2.23
children.translated_text: the immeasurable one caused the vision of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — this was celebrated in the time of the fifth <s>Manu</s>. // SatvT_2.23

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe 'ntare tu bhagavān dvijaśāpakhinnadehān surān avanatān avalokya sannaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the sixth age, the Lord, seeing the gods humbled, their bodies afflicted by a brāhmaṇa's curse, became compassionate;

children.text: vairājavipratanayo 'jitasaṃjña īśo devāsurair amathayat sahasā payodhim // SatvT_2.24
children.translated_text: born as the son of <s>Vairāja</s> brāhmaṇa, the Lord named <s>Ajita</s> swiftly churned the ocean together with gods and demons. // SatvT_2.24

children.text: devāsure jalanidher mathanād viṣaṣṇe hastāc cyute girivare sahasārdracittaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the battle between gods and demons, when the great mountain slipped from the hand during the churning of the ocean, being suddenly moved with compassion,

children.text: bhūtvā tu kūrmavapur adbhutam uddadhāra mene ca parvatavivartanagātrakaṇḍūm // SatvT_2.25
children.translated_text: becoming the wondrous tortoise-form, he lifted it up, and considered the turning of the mountain upon his back as mere scratching. // SatvT_2.25

children.text: dugdhāmbudhāv ururujāṃ pracikīrṣur īśa ādāya pūrṇakalaśaṃ sudhayā nitāntam /
children.translated_text: Desiring to heal the great diseases in the ocean of milk, the Lord, the enjoyer of sacrifice, taking a vessel filled to the brim with nectar,

children.text: āyurvidhānanigamaṃ khalu yajñabhoktā dhanvantariḥ samabhavad bhagavān narāṇām // SatvT_2.26
children.translated_text: along with the scripture of longevity (<s>Āyurveda</s>), manifested as the Lord <s>Dhanvantari</s> for mankind. // SatvT_2.26

children.text: dhanvantarer amṛtapūrṇaghaṭe svavārā cūrṇīyamāna amare śaraṇaṃ praviṣṭe /
children.translated_text: When the nectar-filled vessel of <s>Dhanvantari</s> was being snatched away, [and] the immortals, their share being crushed, took refuge,

children.text: mohiny abhūt sa bhagavān asurāsurāṇāṃ mohāya tāpaviramāya sadāptakāmaḥ // SatvT_2.27
children.translated_text: the Lord became <s>Mohinī</s>, for the delusion of demons and gods alike, and for the cessation of their suffering — he who is eternally fulfilled. // SatvT_2.27

children.text: satyavratāya janatarpaṇataḥ svarūpaṃ mātsyaṃ mahākaruṇayā pravitatya sadyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>Satyavrata</s>, out of great compassion for the nourishment of people, extending his fish form immediately,

children.text: kalpārṇave 'py avadad acyuta ātmatattvaṃ bhūrūpanāvivasate viharan dvijebhyaḥ // SatvT_2.28
children.translated_text: even in the ocean of dissolution, the imperishable one taught the truth of the Self to the twice-born, sporting while resting in the earth-shaped boat. // SatvT_2.28

children.text: trailokyaduḥkhadalanāya nṛsiṃharūpaṃ kṛtvā svabhaktam avituṃ kila lāṅgalāgraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Assuming the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> for the destruction of the three worlds' suffering, to protect his own devotee, with the tips of his plough-[like claws],

children.text: dhṛtvāsurendram asurendraviśālatīvravakṣaḥsthalaṃ sthalam ivāgranakhair dadāra // SatvT_2.29
children.translated_text: holding the lord of demons, he tore open the broad and terrible chest of the great demon-lord as if it were [mere] ground, with his foremost claws. // SatvT_2.29

children.text: yasmin prapaśyati baliḥ sagaṇaṃ trilokaṃ tenāpi vāmanatanuṃ bhagavān gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: He in whom <s>Bali</s> beheld the three worlds with their retinues — the Lord, assuming the form of a dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>),

children.text: saṃyācya sammitapadatritayaṃ baleḥ svaṃ kṛtvā triviṣṭapam adād aditeḥ sutebhyaḥ // SatvT_2.30
children.translated_text: begging from <s>Bali</s> ground measured by three steps, making <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (heaven) his own, gave it to the sons of <s>Aditi</s>. // SatvT_2.30

children.text: bhaktān ahaṃ samanuvarta iti svavācaṃ sākṣāt prakartum iva bhūvivare praviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I follow my devotees' — as if to fulfill his own word directly, he entered the excellent abode of the earth;

children.text: vairocaner gṛham arakṣayad aprameyo nāmnā gadādhara iti kṣapayan dayāvān // SatvT_2.31
children.translated_text: the immeasurable one protected the house of <s>Vairocana</s>'s [son], the compassionate one known as <s>Gadādhara</s>, destroying [enemies]. // SatvT_2.31

children.text: bhūtvā tu bhārgavakule nijatātanāśād rāmo mahāparaśukaṃ parigṛhya tīkṣṇam /
children.translated_text: Born in the <s>Bhārgava</s> lineage, due to the killing of his own father, <s>Rāma</s>, taking up the sharp great battle-axe,

children.text: kṣatraṃ nivārya kṣititalaṃ parihṛtya bhūyo dattvā dvijāya hy avasat sa mahendrapṛṣṭhe // SatvT_2.32
children.translated_text: having removed the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> from the surface of the earth and then giving [the earth] to the twice-born, he dwelt on the peak of <s>Mahendra</s>. // SatvT_2.32
<s>Śrī Rāmacandra</s>, whose lotus feet were served by the gods, born in the ocean of the solar dynasty,

children.text: devārināśanavidhau kuśikānvayena nīto maheśadhanur ājagavaṃ babhañja // SatvT_2.33
children.translated_text: was led by one of the lineage of <s>Kuśika</s> for the purpose of destroying the enemies of the gods, and broke the bow <s>Ājagava</s> of <s>Maheśa</s>. // SatvT_2.33

children.text: jñātvā tato bhṛgukulodbhavadhīravīraṃ rāmaṃ sugaurarucirāṃ pariṇīya sītām /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing <s>Rāma</s> of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> lineage — the steadfast hero — and marrying <s>Sītā</s> of very fair complexion,

children.text: gatvā gṛhān gṛhapateḥ pitur āptajāyāvācaṃ niśamya vanavāsam agāt sabhāryaḥ // SatvT_2.34
children.translated_text: going to the homes of the householder, hearing the word of his father's trusted wife, he went to forest exile with his consort. // SatvT_2.34

children.text: tīrtvā gāṅgapayo 'nujānugamanāc chrīcitrakūṭaṃ giriṃ tyaktvā duṣṭavirādharādhadamano dhāvan dhanur dhārayan /
children.translated_text: Crossing the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, followed by his brother, [reaching] the beautiful mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, leaving it, slaying the wicked <s>Virādha</s> and other base ones, running while wielding his bow,

children.text: hatvā krūrasurendravairihariṇaṃ mārīcasaṃjñaṃ tato laṅkeśāhṛtasītayā khalu punaḥ prāpto dṛśām īdṛśām // SatvT_2.35
children.translated_text: having killed the cruel deer-form of the great enemy named <s>Mārīca</s>, then, with <s>Sītā</s> stolen by the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, he was reduced to such a state. // SatvT_2.35

children.text: candraṃ caṇḍakaraṃ pracaṇḍapavanaṃ mene sumandānilaṃ mālāṃ mālatimallikāṃ śucikalāṃ gītaṃ sphuliṅgāyitam /
children.translated_text: He considered the moon as fierce-rayed, the fierce wind as a gentle breeze, the garland of <s>mālatī</s> and <s>mallikā</s> as pure digits, and song as mere sparks;

children.text: ity evaṃ vanitāparāyaṇanaraṃ hāsyann ivālokayan ṛkṣaṃ manmathasāyakāhṛtamano reme priyāśaṅkayā // SatvT_2.36
children.translated_text: thus, looking as if laughing at a man devoted to his woman, the bear [<s>Jāmbavān</s>], his mind struck by <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows, rejoiced thinking of his beloved. // SatvT_2.36

children.text: gatvā vānararājavālinamahāmitreṇa setuṃ tato baddhvā vāridhim ātarat taratamaṃ sākaṃ plavaṃgair mudā /
children.translated_text: Going with the great friend, the monkey-king <s>Vālin</s>'s [slayer], building a bridge, he then crossed the ocean swiftly together with the monkeys joyfully;

children.text: chittvā rākṣasayakṣalakṣam amalā sītā saputrānujaṃ laṅkeśaṃ jvaladagninā bhagavatā cāptā punaḥ sā purī // SatvT_2.37
children.translated_text: having cut down the host of <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Yakṣas</s>, the stainless <s>Sītā</s>, along with sons and brother, [was recovered]; the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> was [slain] by the Lord with blazing fire, and that city was obtained again. // SatvT_2.37
Without diminishing the power of <s>Sūrya</s> and others, he ruled the earth, [maintaining] all <s>dharmas</s> of serving cows, brāhmaṇas, and the wise;

children.text: udriktabhaktinamitān anayat svanāthān sarvān vanādhivasataḥ svapadaṃ suśāntam // SatvT_2.38
children.translated_text: he led all his lords, bowed with overflowing devotion, dwelling in the forest, to his own peaceful abode. // SatvT_2.38

children.text: tasyānujo bharatasaṃjña udārabuddhī rāmājñayā nijagṛhe nivasann api śrīm /
children.translated_text: His younger brother named <s>Bharata</s>, of noble intellect, by <s>Rāma</s>'s command, though dwelling in his own home, [abandoned] prosperity,

children.text: tyaktvā vanasthavratavān abhavat tato vai gandharvakoṭimathanaṃ viharaṃś cakāra // SatvT_2.39
children.translated_text: renouncing [it], he became one observing the vow of a forest-dweller; then he performed the destruction of ten million <s>Gandharvas</s> while sporting. // SatvT_2.39

children.text: śrīlakṣmaṇas tadavaro vanam etya rāmaṃ sītāṃ niṣecya bahukaṣṭa āsīt /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his next younger, having come to the forest with <s>Rāma</s>, and having sprinkled <s>Sītā</s> [with protection], endured much hardship;

children.text: bāhye 'pi cāsya vacasā vanam etya dehaṃ saṃtyajya tatpadam agād arisainyavahniḥ // SatvT_2.40
children.translated_text: and outwardly too, by his [<s>Rāma</s>'s] word, having come to the forest and abandoning his body, he went to his [Lord's] abode — he who was fire to enemy armies. // SatvT_2.40

children.text: śatrughnasaṃjña uruvikramaśuddhabuddhiḥ śauryeṇa darpadalano dviṣatāṃ dayāluḥ /
children.translated_text: The one named <s>Śatrughna</s>, of great valor and pure intellect, crusher of enemies' pride through his heroism, compassionate;

children.text: dīneṣu daityalavaṇāntaka āryasevī svānyeṣu sāmyamatirājanatābhirāmaḥ // SatvT_2.41
children.translated_text: toward the afflicted, the destroyer of the demon <s>Lavaṇa</s>, servant of the noble, having equanimity toward his own kin, delightful through humility before elders. // SatvT_2.41

children.text: mārkaṇḍanāmamunaye bhuvanāni deṣṭuṃ māyālaye tanutare jaṭhare mukundaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the sage named <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, to show him the worlds, <s>Mukunda</s> in the abode of <s>māyā</s>, in his tiny belly,

children.text: nyagrodhapattrapuṭakośaśayāna āsīd aṅguṣṭhapānaparamaḥ śiśur aprameyaḥ // SatvT_2.42
children.translated_text: lay sleeping in the cup-like hollow of a banyan leaf — the immeasurable infant, absorbed in sucking his toe. // SatvT_2.42

children.text: vṛtrasya ghoravapuṣā paritāpitānāṃ saṃrakṣaṇāya bhagavān yudhi nirjarāṇām /
children.translated_text: For the protection of the immortals tormented by the terrible form of <s>Vṛtra</s> in battle, the Lord,

children.text: ādyo hy abhūd garuḍakiṃnaragītakīrtis teṣāṃ suduḥkhabhayaśokavināśaśīlaḥ // SatvT_2.43
children.translated_text: was the first [helper], whose glory was sung by <s>Garuḍa</s> and <s>Kinnaras</s> — he whose nature is to destroy their great suffering, fear, and sorrow. // SatvT_2.43

children.text: aṅguṣṭhaparvasumitān śramaṇān dvijāgryān dṛṣṭvā tu goṣpadapayogatasarvadehān /
children.translated_text: Seeing the ascetics — the best of twice-born — measuring [only] the joint of a thumb, their entire bodies submerged in the water of a cow's hoofprint,

children.text: brahmaṇya indrahasitān samidaṃśuhastān gurvarcanāya kṛpayāvad amūn prapannān // SatvT_2.44
children.translated_text: the Lord, devoted to brāhmaṇas, [seeing them] laughed at by <s>Indra</s>, with <s>samidh</s>-fuel in hand [going] for worship of their teacher, out of compassion protected those who had taken refuge. // SatvT_2.44

children.text: duṣyantabījam adhigamya śakuntalāyāṃ jāto hy ajo 'pi bhagavān adhiyajñakart
children.translated_text: Having obtained the seed of <s>Duṣyanta</s> in <s>Śakuntalā</s>, though unborn, the Lord, the performer of the supreme sacrifice, was born;

children.text: vismāpayan bahunṛpān bahuvājimedhān sākṣād iyāja bahu dānam adād ameyaḥ // SatvT_2.45
children.translated_text: amazing many kings, he directly performed many horse-sacrifices and gave immeasurable gifts. // SatvT_2.45

children.text: sarvān janān kaliyuge balabuddhihīnān dṛṣṭvā kṛpāparavaśo vasuvīryajāyām /
children.translated_text: Seeing all people in <s>Kali Yuga</s> as bereft of strength and intelligence, overcome with compassion, in the wife of <s>Vasuvīrya</s>,

children.text: jātaḥ parāśarasakāśata ādidevo vedān samāhitatayā vibhajiṣyati sma // SatvT_2.46
children.translated_text: the primeval Lord was born from <s>Parāśara</s>, and with concentrated mind would divide the <s>Vedas</s>. // SatvT_2.46

children.text: vṛṣṇeḥ kule tu bhagavān baladevanāmā yasmād balān atibalān adalat surārīn /
children.translated_text: In the family of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, the Lord named <s>Baladeva</s>, because by his strength he crushed the exceedingly mighty enemies of the gods;

children.text: yal lāṅgalāgrakalanāt kururājadhānī dhāneva dhāmasahitā calitātibhītā // SatvT_2.47
children.translated_text: by the point of whose plough, the capital of the <s>Kuru</s> king trembled greatly in fear, shaking like grain together with its splendor. // SatvT_2.47

children.text: bhūmer janasya nijapādaparāyaṇasya vṛṣṇer ajo 'pi bhagavān sukham ādadhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the earth, for the people devoted to his feet, though unborn, the Lord in <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>'s [line], bestowing happiness,

children.text: jāto bhaviṣyati yaśo vipulaṃ prakartuṃ śrīkṛṣṇa ity abhihito 'khilaśaktipūrṇaḥ // SatvT_2.48
children.translated_text: will be born to spread vast fame — called <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, filled with all powers. // SatvT_2.48

children.text: jāto nijena vapuṣā vasudevagehe gatvā tu gokulam atho viharan vinodaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Born in his own form in the house of <s>Vasudeva</s>, going to <s>Gokula</s>, sporting with playful amusements,

children.text: bālākṛtir viśadabālakabhāṣāhāsair gogopagopavanitāmudam āśu kartā // SatvT_2.49
children.translated_text: in a child's form, with the bright speech, laughter, and ways of a child, he will quickly bring delight to the cows, cowherds, and cowherd women. // SatvT_2.49
He will slay the hosts of enemies of the gods sent by <s>Kaṃsa</s>, led by <s>Ulūkī</s> [<s>Pūtanā</s>]; for the protection of <s>Vraja</s>, the great mountain —

children.text: dhṛtvocchilīndhram iva sapta dināni vāmahaste pragṛhya suranāthamadaṃ pramārṣṭā // SatvT_2.50
children.translated_text: holding up <s>Govardhana</s> as if it were an uprooted mushroom for seven days in his left hand, he will crush the pride of <s>Indra</s>. // SatvT_2.50

children.text: dhātrā yadā sapaśugopaśiśau praṇīte buddher bhramo halabhṛto 'bhavad aprameyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the Creator took away the calves, cowherds, and children, the immeasurable confusion of <s>Baladeva</s>'s intellect arose;

children.text: tat saṃharan sapaśupālakulasvarūpaṃ kṛtvā vidhiṃ vividhamohamalāt sa dhartā // SatvT_2.51
children.translated_text: dispelling that, he will sustain [them] by assuming the forms of the calves and cowherd families himself, delivering <s>Brahmā</s> from the impurity of his various delusions. // SatvT_2.51
In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, with fragrant music, playful songs, bearing the speed of <s>Kāma</s> in the minds of the cowherd women who milked the cows,
he will perform the great amorous festival-play, astonishing the <s>Rākṣasas</s> and sky-dwellers by night. // SatvT_2.52

children.text: kaṃsasya raṅgasadanaṃ sabale praṇīte svāphalkinā bhavadhanus tarasā vibhajya /
children.translated_text: When brought with <s>Bala</s> to the arena of <s>Kaṃsa</s> by <s>Akrūra</s>, swiftly breaking the bow of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: cāṇūraśūraśamanaṃ sahakaṃsamājau kartā dvipaṃ kuvalayaṃ sahasā nihatya // SatvT_2.53
children.translated_text: he will perform the slaying of the mighty <s>Cāṇūra</s> along with <s>Kaṃsa</s> in battle, having suddenly killed the elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>. // SatvT_2.53

children.text: sāṃdīpanaṃ mṛtasutaṃ gurudakṣiṇārthī dattvā jarāsutabalaṃ yavanaṃ ca hatvā /
children.translated_text: Desiring to give <s>guru-dakṣiṇā</s>, having restored the dead son of [his teacher] <s>Sāndīpani</s>, and slaying the <s>Yavana</s> force of <s>Jarāsandha</s>,

children.text: śrīrukmiṇīprabhṛtidāraśataṃ vivāhya tābhyaḥ sutān daśadaśānu janiṣyati sma // SatvT_2.54
children.translated_text: marrying a hundred wives beginning with <s>Śrī Rukmiṇī</s>, from them he will beget ten sons each. // SatvT_2.54

children.text: bhaumaṃ nihatya sagaṇaṃ divi devamātur dātuṃ tadīyamaṇikuṇḍalam ādidevaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having slain <s>Bhauma</s> [<s>Naraka</s>] with his retinue, the primeval Lord, to give back to the divine mother her own jeweled earrings in heaven,

children.text: gatvā surendratarurājavaraṃ priyāyāḥ prītau samuddharaṇato ditijān sa jetā // SatvT_2.55
children.translated_text: going [there] and obtaining the best of divine trees for his beloved, from [its] uprooting — through [the ensuing fight] he will conquer the <s>Daityas</s>. // SatvT_2.55

children.text: bāṇāsurasya samare mama vīryanāśāl labdhāmaratvam adhikaṃ yudhi bhūpabandhūn /
children.translated_text: In the battle with <s>Bāṇāsura</s>, having destroyed the immortality obtained through my [<s>Śiva</s>'s] power, in war, the kinsmen of kings —

children.text: jitvā yudhiṣṭhiranṛpakratunā vivāhabījaṃ nipātya gurubhārataraṃ prahartā // SatvT_2.56
children.translated_text: having defeated them, through the sacrifice of king <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, he will strike down the seed of the marriage [dispute], the heavy [burden] of the <s>Bhārata</s>. // SatvT_2.56

children.text: loke pradarśya sutarāṃ dvijadevapūjāṃ svasyāpy apārakaruṇāṃ nijasevakebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Displaying to the world supremely the worship of brāhmaṇas and gods, and his own boundless compassion toward his servants,

children.text: trātvā parīkṣitanṛpaṃ paramāstradagdhaṃ pārthāya bhūtim avalokayitā dvijārthe // SatvT_2.57
children.translated_text: having saved king <s>Parīkṣit</s> burnt by the supreme weapon, he will show prosperity to <s>Arjuna</s> for the sake of the twice-born. // SatvT_2.57

children.text: kāmena snehabhayarāgakuṭubasaṃdhe yasmin mano nivasataḥ śamalaṃ nirasya /
children.translated_text: For one in whose [mind abides] attachment through desire, affection, fear, passion, or family bond — casting out the impurity of the mind dwelling [thus],

children.text: dātā svarūpam amalaṃ pariśuddhabhāvaḥ sākṣāt svarūpaniratasya ca kiṃ nu vakṣye // SatvT_2.58
children.translated_text: he gives his own stainless form, being of purified nature — and what shall I say of one who is directly absorbed in his own nature? // SatvT_2.58

children.text: yat pādapaṅkajaparāgaparāyaṇānām agre cakāsti na ca muktisukhaṃ nitāntam /
children.translated_text: Before those who are devoted to the pollen of his lotus feet, neither the bliss of liberation shines supremely,

children.text: kiṃ vānyadarpitabhayaṃ khalu kālavegaiḥ sākṣān mahāsukhasamudragatāntarāṇām // SatvT_2.59
children.translated_text: nor is there any fear caused by the force of time — for those who have entered the great ocean of bliss directly. // SatvT_2.59

children.text: gaṅgāditīrthatapahomavratādikebhyaḥ kīrtiṃ svakīyam adhikāṃ samudīrya loke /
children.translated_text: Having proclaimed in the world his own fame as greater than [that from] <s>Gaṅgā</s> and other sacred places, austerity, fire-offerings, vows, and the like,

children.text: atyunnataṃ dvijakulaṃ dvijaśāpavyājād dhatvā svalokam amalaṃ tanunābhigantā // SatvT_2.60
children.translated_text: having elevated the twice-born community exceedingly, under the pretext of a brāhmaṇa's curse, he will go to his own stainless abode, abandoning the body. // SatvT_2.60

body.text: tasmād bhaviṣyati sutaḥ sukhado janānāṃ pradyumnasaṃjña urugāyaguṇānurūpaḥ // SatvT_2.61
body.translated_text: From him will be born a son who gives happiness to people, named <s>Pradyumna</s>, corresponding to the qualities of the widely-praised one. // SatvT_2.61

children.text: kartā mudaṃ muditavaktrasucārugātraiḥ pātrair ivāmṛtapayo manujān pracchan /
children.translated_text: He will create delight, showering upon people with vessels as if of nectar-milk, through his joyful face and beautiful limbs;
and from him too, though unborn, one named <s>Aniruddha</s> will be born — the lord in the mind, by being the propagator of the sacred texts. // SatvT_2.62

children.text: yasmād uṣāharaṇato bhujavīryanāśād bāṇo bhaviṣyati śivānugaśāntadehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the abduction of <s>Uṣā</s>, from the destruction of [his] arm-strength, <s>Bāṇa</s> will become one whose body is pacified, a follower of <s>Śiva</s>. /

children.text: vyāsād bhaviṣyati [... au2 ṇeichenjh] bhagavān araṇyāṃ yogī janān prati gadiṣyati vedasāram // SatvT_2.63
children.translated_text: From <s>Vyāsa</s>, there will arise [... text corrupt ...] the Blessed Lord, a yogin in the forest, who will declare the essence of the <s>Veda</s> to the people. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.63

children.text: śrīmatsuśāntam amalaṃ bhagavatpraṇītaṃ yac chraddhayā kalijanā api yānti śāntim /
children.translated_text: The glorious, perfectly tranquil, and stainless [teaching] set forth by the Blessed Lord—through faith in it, even people of the <s>Kali</s> age attain peace.

children.text: buddhāvatāram adhigamya kalāvalakṣair veṣair mater ativimohakaraṃ pralobham // SatvT_2.64
children.translated_text: Having assumed the <s>Buddha</s> <s>avatāra</s>, [he creates] an exceedingly deluding allurement of the intellect, through guises distinguishable by [various] arts. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.64

children.text: pākhaṇḍaśāstram adhikalpya suradviṣāṇāṃ kartā jinasya tanayo bhagavān gayāyām /
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord, son of <s>Jina</s>, at <s>Gayā</s>, will be the author [of teachings], having devised a heterodox scripture (<s>pākhaṇḍa-śāstra</s>) for the enemies of the gods;

children.text: pākhaṇḍaśāstrabahule nijavedamārge naṣṭe dvijātibhir asatpathi vartamāne // SatvT_2.65
children.translated_text: When heterodox scriptures abound, when the proper Vedic path is lost, and when the twice-born walk on the wrong path— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.65
The sun of the <s>Kalki</s> <s>avatāra</s>, striking down the host of kings equal to the darkness of youth, the protector of established <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sākṣād bhaviṣyati sarasvatisaṃjñitāyāṃ śrīsārvabhauma iti vedagupo dvijāgryāt // SatvT_2.66
children.translated_text: Will manifest directly in the [town] named <s>Sarasvatī</s>, as '<s>Śrī Sārvabhauma</s>,' the protector of the <s>Vedas</s>, from a foremost <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.66

children.text: kṛtvā puraṃdaraśriyaṃ balaye 'tidāsyan goptāṣṭame manuyuge viditānubhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having bestowed the glory of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) upon <s>Bali</s> through extreme servitude, the protector—of renowned power—in the eighth <s>Manu</s>-age,

children.text: āyuḥ karo navamanoḥ samaye janānāṃ nītiṃ vidhātum amarārivināśanāya // SatvT_2.67
children.translated_text: Will be the giver of longevity and, in the time of the ninth <s>Manu</s>, [will appear] to establish moral conduct (<s>nīti</s>) for the people and to destroy the enemies of the gods. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.67

children.text: goptā bhaviṣyati jagajjanadhārayāsau bhūtvā śrutendrasahito bhagavān apāraḥ /
children.translated_text: He, the Blessed Lord, boundless, accompanied by <s>Śrutendra</s>, will be the protector of the world's people, having become [an avatāra] bearing the world;

children.text: bhūtvā viśūcisadane dvijarājaśambhoḥ sāhityakarmaparavān daśame 'ntare saḥ // SatvT_2.68
children.translated_text: Having been born in the house of <s>Viśūci</s>, of the twice-born king <s>Śambhu</s>, devoted to the works of learning, in the tenth interval [<s>Manvantara</s>]. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.68

children.text: pātāmarān [... au3 ṇeichenjh] viśvak [... au1 ṇeichenjh] senasaṃjño yat sainyapūgasamarād amarārināśaḥ /
children.translated_text: [He will] subdue the demons [... text corrupt ...] everywhere [... text corrupt ...] named <s>Sena</s>, [through] whose army-hosts the enemies of the gods are destroyed in battle;

children.text: manvantaraikadaśame 'rthakariprapautraḥ śrīdharmasetur iti viśruta ādidevaḥ // SatvT_2.69
children.translated_text: In the eleventh <s>Manvantara</s>, the great-grandson of <s>Arthakari</s>, the primeval deity renowned as '<s>Śrī Dharmasetu</s>.' // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.69

children.text: hatvāsurān surapatau vidhṛter apatye dātā tṛtīyabhavanaṃ bhagavān svayambhūḥ /
children.translated_text: Having slain the demons, when <s>Surapati</s> (<s>Indra</s>) is the offspring of <s>Vidhṛti</s>, the self-born Blessed Lord will give the third abode;

children.text: jāto dviṣaṇmanuyuge yugapālanāya viprāt svaśaktimahasaḥ sunṛtākhyato vai // SatvT_2.70
children.translated_text: Born in the second <s>Manu</s>-age for the protection of the age, from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [manifesting] the greatness of his own power, [he is] named <s>Sunṛtā</s> indeed. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.70

children.text: khyāto bhaviṣyati tato bhagavān svadhāmā yasmāj janā jagati saukhyam apāram āpuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thereafter the Blessed Lord, Self-luminous (<s>Svadhāman</s>), will become renowned—he from whom people in the world attain boundless happiness;

children.text: bhāvye trayodaśayuge bhavitādidevaḥ śrīdevahotratanayo bhagavān bṛhatyām // SatvT_2.71
children.translated_text: In the future thirteenth age, the primeval deity will be the Blessed Lord, son of <s>Devahotra</s>, in [the city of] <s>Bṛhatī</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.71

children.text: yogeśvaro divi divaspatiśakramitro yogād ameyavapuṣā sa vitānatulyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord of Yoga (<s>Yogeśvara</s>), in heaven, friend of <s>Indra</s> the lord of heaven, through yoga, with an immeasurable form equal to the cosmic canopy;

children.text: satrāyaṇasya sadane bhagavān anādidevo 'pi devavanitātanayo 'bhijātaḥ // SatvT_2.72
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord, the beginningless deity, though the son of divine women, born in the house of <s>Satrāyaṇa</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.72
At the end of that interval, [he] will spread the threads of the canopy of ritual action, being of a nature that desires the welfare of the world.

children.text: ete mayā bhagavataḥ kathitā dvijāte śuddhāvatāranicayā jagato hitārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: These pure collections of <s>avatāras</s> of the Blessed Lord, for the benefit of the world, have been recounted to you by me, O twice-born one;
They are to be contemplated as [having] completeness, portions, and fractions, and are manifested through knowledge, action, power, <s>samādhi</s>, and the like. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.73
He by whose playful forms (<s>līlā-tanu</s>) the entire world of moving and unmoving beings is always protected—

children.text: tam ahaṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmi kṛṣṇaṃ brahmāṇḍanāyakam // SatvT_2.74
children.translated_text: To Him I go for refuge, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lord of the universe (<s>brahmāṇḍa-nāyaka</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 2.74
<s>Sātvata Tantra</s>, Third Chapter (<s>Paṭala</s>).
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
The <s>avatāras</s> of the great-souled Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> have been described [by you],
To be contemplated in their distinctions of complete (<s>sampūrṇa</s>), portion (<s>aṃśa</s>), and fraction (<s>kalā</s>), O Lord. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.1
Of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is without distinctions (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), [who is] <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>)—

children.text: katham aṃśakalābhāga etad varṇaya no vibho // SatvT_3.2
children.translated_text: How can there be a division into portions and fractions? Explain this to us, O all-pervading Lord. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.2
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: satyam uktaṃ tvayā brahman kṛṣṇasya jagadātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truly spoken by you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Soul of the world,

children.text: avatāreṣu sarveṣu bhedād aṃśakalāḥ svataḥ // SatvT_3.3
children.translated_text: In all his <s>avatāras</s>, the portions and fractions, [arising] from the [apparent] division, of themselves— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.3
The skillful ones, the knowers devoted to the Blessed Lord, do not describe [real divisions],

children.text: avikārād acyutāc ca nirbhedād brahmarūpiṇaḥ // SatvT_3.4
children.translated_text: Since he is unchangeable, infallible (<s>Acyuta</s>), without distinctions, and of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.4
However, on the basis of the manifestation of the power of knowledge and the like, from the observation of complete, portion, and sub-portion,
They speak of the complete, the portion, and the fractional division of the Lord of the world. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.5
Although knowledge, valor, qualities, and the like exist everywhere [in all avatāras],

children.text: tathāpi kāryataḥ kecid dṛśyante na hi sarvataḥ // SatvT_3.6
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, from the standpoint of [their specific] function, some are seen [manifest] but not all [in every case]. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.6

children.text: aiśvaryajñānadharmāś ca vairāgyaṃ śrīr yaśas tathā /
children.translated_text: Sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), righteousness (<s>dharma</s>), detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>), splendor (<s>śrī</s>), and fame (<s>yaśas</s>)—

children.text: eṣāṃ saṃdarśanāt sākṣāt pūrṇo vidvadbhir ucyate // SatvT_3.7
children.translated_text: From the direct manifestation of these, [an avatāra] is called 'complete' (<s>pūrṇa</s>) by the learned. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.7
From the lesser manifestation of even portions of these,
The Blessed Lord appears with a division into portions (<s>aṃśa</s>) and fractions (<s>kalā</s>), bearing the distinctions of divine attributes (<s>bhaga</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.8

children.text: aṃśas turīyo bhāgaḥ syāt kalā tu ṣoḍaśī matā /
children.translated_text: A portion (<s>aṃśa</s>) is a fourth part; a fraction (<s>kalā</s>) is considered a sixteenth;

children.text: śatabhāgo vibhūtiś ca varṇyate kavibhiḥ pṛthak // SatvT_3.9
children.translated_text: And a hundredth part is [called] a manifestation (<s>vibhūti</s>)—so the poets describe, severally. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.9
Therefore, of knowledge, righteousness, detachment, sovereignty, splendor,

children.text: yaśasaḥ pṛthagbhedaṃ mattaḥ śṛṇu dvijottama // SatvT_3.10
children.translated_text: And fame—hear from me the individual divisions, O best of the twice-born. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.10
Creation, dissolution, [knowledge of] the learned and the unlearned (<s>vidyā-avidyā</s>), and [knowledge of] going and coming [of beings]—

children.text: eṣāṃ jñānaṃ vadanty aṅga jñānaṃ ṣaḍvidham uttamam // SatvT_3.11
children.translated_text: These, O dear one, they call knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>)—knowledge of six kinds, supreme. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.11

children.text: satyaṃ śaucaṃ dayā maunaṃ dharmaś cāturvidhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truth, purity, compassion, and silence—<s>dharma</s> is remembered as fourfold.

children.text: amāno vyatirekaś ca aindriyas tu vaśīkṛtaḥ // SatvT_3.12
children.translated_text: Absence of pride, [power of] discrimination, and the subjugation of the senses— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.12
Thus, O blessed one, detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>) is declared to be fourfold.

children.text: aṇimā laghimā caiva mahimā tadanantaram // SatvT_3.13
children.translated_text: <s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), and <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), and then— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.13

children.text: prākāmyaṃ caiva prāptiś ca īśitā vaśitā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>īśitā</s> (lordship), <s>vaśitā</s> (dominion), likewise

children.text: kāmasyāvasitā hy ete aṣṭaiśvaryāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // SatvT_3.14
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmasyāvasitā</s> (fulfillment of desire)—these eight sovereign powers (<s>aiśvarya</s>) are declared. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.14
Servants, ministers, friends, kinsmen, sons, grandsons, and wives,
Garments, ornaments, treasure-houses, and a fourfold army— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.15

children.text: gṛhā bhūr astraśastre ca durgādyāḥ śriya īritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Houses, land, weapons and arms, fortresses, and the like—these are called splendor (<s>śrī</s>).

children.text: yaśas tu puṃso bhavati karmato guṇatas tathā // SatvT_3.16
children.translated_text: Fame (<s>yaśas</s>) accrues to a person through action and through qualities. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.16
Action (<s>karma</s>) is said to be fourfold: consisting of creation, sustenance, and dissolution;
Through that [action], the deeds of the playful <s>avatāras</s> are supremely wondrous. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.17
The qualities [of the Lord] are immeasurable, as proclaimed by the wise;

children.text: tathāpy ahaṃ dviṣaṣṭhīṃ te varṇayāmy anupūrvaśaḥ // SatvT_3.18
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, I shall describe sixty-two of them to you in order. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.18

children.text: brahmaṇyaś ca śaraṇyaś ca bhaktavātsalyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Devotion to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>brahmaṇya</s>), being a refuge (<s>śaraṇya</s>), tender affection for devotees (<s>bhakta-vātsalya</s>),
Generosity (<s>dātṛtva</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya-saṃdhatva</s>), valor (<s>vikrāntatva</s>), self-restraint (<s>niyamyatā</s>); // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.19
Invincibility (<s>durjayatva</s>), irresistibility (<s>duḥsaratva</s>), being worthy of worship (<s>niṣevyatva</s>), forbearance (<s>sahiṣṇutā</s>),
Imperturbability (<s>akṣobhyatva</s>), independence (<s>svatantratva</s>), self-sufficiency (<s>nairapekṣya</s>), gracefulness of form (<s>sva-sauṣṭhava</s>); // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.20

children.text: śauryam audāryam āstikyaṃ sthairyaṃ dhairyaṃ prasannatā /
children.translated_text: Heroism (<s>śaurya</s>), magnanimity (<s>audārya</s>), piety (<s>āstikya</s>), steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>), fortitude (<s>dhairya</s>), graciousness (<s>prasannatā</s>),

children.text: gāmbhīryaṃ praśrayaḥ śīlaṃ prāgalbhyam ṛtamaṅgalam // SatvT_3.21
children.translated_text: Profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>), modesty (<s>praśraya</s>), virtue (<s>śīla</s>), boldness (<s>prāgalbhya</s>), and auspicious truth (<s>ṛta-maṅgala</s>); // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.21

children.text: śamo damo balaṃ dākṣyaṃ kṣemaṃ harṣo 'nahaṃkṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-control (<s>dama</s>), strength (<s>bala</s>), skill (<s>dākṣya</s>), welfare (<s>kṣema</s>), joy (<s>harṣa</s>), absence of egoism (<s>anahaṃkṛti</s>),

children.text: saṃtoṣa ārjavaṃ sāmyaṃ manobhāgyaṃ śrutaṃ sukham // SatvT_3.22
children.translated_text: Contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), uprightness (<s>ārjava</s>), equanimity (<s>sāmya</s>), mental fortune (<s>manobhāgya</s>), learning (<s>śruta</s>), happiness (<s>sukha</s>); // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.22

children.text: tyāgo bhayaṃ pāvanaṃ ca tejaḥ kauśalam āśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>), fearfulness [for the wicked] (<s>bhaya</s>), purifying power (<s>pāvana</s>), radiance (<s>tejas</s>), dexterity (<s>kauśala</s>), being a refuge (<s>āśraya</s>),

children.text: dhṛtiḥ kṣamā smṛtir lajjā śraddhā maitrī dayonnatiḥ // SatvT_3.23
children.translated_text: Steadiness (<s>dhṛti</s>), patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), modesty (<s>lajjā</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>dayā</s>), exaltation (<s>unnati</s>); // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.23

children.text: śāntiḥ puṣṭiḥ svavākśuddhir buddhir vidyā svarakṣatā /
children.translated_text: Peace (<s>śānti</s>), nourishment (<s>puṣṭi</s>), purity of speech (<s>sva-vāk-śuddhi</s>), intelligence (<s>buddhi</s>), learning (<s>vidyā</s>), self-protection (<s>sva-rakṣatā</s>)—

children.text: ete te bhagabhedās tu kathitā hy anupūrvaśaḥ // SatvT_3.24
children.translated_text: These divisions of divine attributes (<s>bhaga-bheda</s>) have been declared to you in due order. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.24

children.text: eṣāṃ prakāśo yatrāsīt sa pūrṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where all of these are manifest, that [avatāra] is called 'complete' (<s>pūrṇa</s>);

children.text: aṃśaprakāśād aṃśaḥ syāt kalāyās tu kalā smṛtā // SatvT_3.25
children.translated_text: From partial manifestation, it is a 'portion' (<s>aṃśa</s>); and from [further] fractional [manifestation], it is called a 'fraction' (<s>kalā</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.25

children.text: vibhūtes tu vibhūtiḥ syād eṣa bhedo na hi svataḥ /
children.translated_text: And from [manifestation of] a vibhūti, it is a '<s>vibhūti</s>' (power-manifestation). This division is not inherent [in the Lord himself],
For the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in his own nature is without distinctions (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) and true. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.26
Of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the pure, of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the great-souled—

children.text: yataḥ kṛṣṇāvatāreṇa bhagabhedāḥ pṛthak pṛthak // SatvT_3.27
children.translated_text: Since through the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> <s>avatāra</s>, the divisions of divine attributes (<s>bhaga-bheda</s>) severally— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.27
Were displayed separately for separate purposes, therefore he is called 'complete' (<s>sampūrṇa</s>).
In the <s>Hayagrīva</s> and other <s>avatāras</s>, since lesser— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.28

children.text: darśitā bhagabhedā vai tasmād aṃśāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Divisions of divine attributes were displayed, they are therefore declared to be 'portions' (<s>aṃśa</s>).
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Matsya</s> (the Fish), <s>Kūrma</s> (the Tortoise), <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar), <s>Narakesarin</s> (<s>Narasiṃha</s>), // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.29
The <s>Manvantara</s> <s>avatāras</s> such as <s>Yajña</s> and others, and <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> (Horse-headed One);

children.text: tathā śuklādayo hy āvirbhāvā ṛṣabha ātmavān // SatvT_3.30
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Śukla</s> and others, and the self-realized manifestations (<s>āvirbhāva</s>), and <s>Ṛṣabha</s>; // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.30
<s>Nara-Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Datta</s> (<s>Dattātreya</s>), and in the <s>Kali</s> age, <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Kalki</s>—
Through their power of knowledge, action, and the like, these are declared to be 'portions' (<s>aṃśa</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.31
<s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Brahmarāta</s>, and others are 'fractions' (<s>kalā</s>),
Endowed with a portion of knowledge—<s>avatāras</s> of the great-souled <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.32

children.text: gayaḥ pṛthuś ca bharataḥ śaktiyuktāḥ kalā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Gaya</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, and <s>Bharata</s>, endowed with power, are considered 'fractions' (<s>kalā</s>);

children.text: guṇāvatārā brahmādyās tadaṃśā ye vibhūtayaḥ // SatvT_3.33
children.translated_text: The <s>guṇa-avatāras</s> (<s>avatāras</s> of the qualities) such as <s>Brahmā</s> and others, and those who are their portions, are [called] 'manifestations' (<s>vibhūti</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.33
This designation of 'complete' (<s>sampūrṇa</s>), 'portion' (<s>aṃśa</s>), and 'fraction' (<s>kalā</s>) has been described to you by me,
In accordance with [their respective] functions, O chief of the twice-born, through the demonstration of the divisions of divine attributes. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.34

children.text: na brahmaṇo bhidā vipra śrīkṛṣṇasya ca sattama /
children.translated_text: There is no [real] division of <s>Brahman</s>, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, nor of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, O best one,

children.text: nārāyaṇasya vā saumya hy avatārisvarūpiṇaḥ // SatvT_3.35
children.translated_text: Nor of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, O gentle one—for [he is] of the nature of the source of all <s>avatāras</s> (<s>avatāri-svarūpin</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.35
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
Describe to me the nature of the source of <s>avatāras</s> (<s>avatāri-svarūpa</s>), O <s>Sadāśiva</s>!

children.text: kiṃ brahma paramaṃ sākṣāt kiṃ vā nārāyaṇo vibhuḥ // SatvT_3.36
children.translated_text: Is <s>Brahman</s> itself the Supreme directly, or is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> the all-pervading Lord? // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.36
Or is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>-world?

children.text: kim ekatattvam eteṣām athavā kiṃ pṛthak pṛthak // SatvT_3.37
children.translated_text: Is there one reality among these, or are they each different? // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.37

children.text: śṛṇu tat paramaṃ guhyaṃ brahmadāyāda sattama /
children.translated_text: Hear that supreme secret, O best heir of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: avatārisvarūpaṃ me yathā varṇayato dvija // SatvT_3.39
children.translated_text: As I describe the nature of the source of <s>avatāras</s>, O twice-born. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.39

children.text: ekam eva paraṃ tattvam avatāri sanātanam /
children.translated_text: The Supreme Reality (<s>paraṃ tattva</s>) is one alone, eternal, the source of all <s>avatāras</s>;
It is designated separately by the names '<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,' '<s>Brahman</s>,' and '<s>Puruṣa</s>.' // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.40
Just as the radiance, light, and orb of the sun have no separate existence,

children.text: tathā śrīkṛṣṇadevasya brahmaṇaḥ puruṣasya ca // SatvT_3.41
children.translated_text: So too <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, and <s>Puruṣa</s> [are inseparable]. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.41
Therefore, the knowers of the <s>Sātvata Tantra</s>, established in devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), distinguished [among seekers],

children.text: śrīkṛṣṇākhyaṃ paraṃ dhāma paramānandam uttamam // SatvT_3.42
children.translated_text: [Declare] the supreme abode named <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the supreme bliss, the highest— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.42
Dwelling in the world of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, having a form of pure <s>sattva</s> (<s>śuddha-sattva</s>)—
They declare him eternal, true, served by hosts of his own devotees. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.43
The <s>Vedāntins</s>, established in knowledge, following the scripture of knowledge (<s>jñāna-śāstra</s>),

children.text: vadanti brahma paramaṃ prakāśātmakam avyayam // SatvT_3.44
children.translated_text: Declare the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> as having a nature of pure luminosity, imperishable— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.44
Without hands, feet, eyes, ears, skin, or nose as body,
Endowed with all powers, consisting of radiance, beyond the reach of speech and mind— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.45
Consisting of bliss alone, perfectly pure, manifest as consciousness (<s>cid-vyakta</s>), the cause of all.
The followers of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Vedic ritualists), versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>, [declare] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, free from affliction, // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.46
The thousand-headed deity, of supreme bliss, imperishable,

children.text: anantaśaktiṃ sarveṣāṃ puruṣaṃ prakṛteḥ param // SatvT_3.47
children.translated_text: Of infinite power, the <s>Puruṣa</s> beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.47
Those devoted to ritual action declare him as the cause of creation, sustenance, and dissolution,
The bestower of all bliss, tranquil, the deliverer from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.48

children.text: ataḥ kṛṣṇasya devasya brahmaṇaḥ puruṣasya ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of <s>Brahman</s>, and of <s>Puruṣa</s>—

children.text: vastuto naiva bhedo hi varṇyate tair api dvija // SatvT_3.49
children.translated_text: In reality there is no distinction whatsoever, as even they [the different schools] describe, O twice-born. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.49
Just as an object appears manifold through the operations of the various sense-faculties,

children.text: tathā sa bhagavān kṛṣṇo nāneva paricakṣate // SatvT_3.50
children.translated_text: So too the Blessed Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is spoken of as though manifold. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.50
Therefore, by all this [reasoning] too, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>),
Entered the womb of <s>Devakī</s> in a playful human form (<s>līlā-mānuṣa-rūpa</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.51
Therefore, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is called the cause of all <s>avatāras</s>,
Since creation and numerous other functions were manifested by him of his own accord. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.52
He alone, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), is worthy of worship by all the worlds,

children.text: muktyādyarthaṃ nṛlokasya mānuṣatvaṃ yato gataḥ // SatvT_3.53
children.translated_text: Since he assumed human form for the sake of liberation (<s>mukti</s>) and other goals of the human world. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.53

children.text: atas taṃ puruṣā nityaṃ bhaktibhedena nityadā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, people always worship him, the Lord of liberation (<s>apavarga-īśa</s>), the Supreme Lord,

children.text: bhajanti hy apavargeśaṃ pareśaṃ tadakāmyayā // SatvT_3.54
children.translated_text: With various forms of devotion (<s>bhakti-bheda</s>), desiring nothing else from him. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.54

children.text: mayā te kathitā vipra avatārā mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>avatāras</s> of the great-souled [Lord] have been described to you by me, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: kim anyat kathayāmy adya tvaṃ hi bhāgavatottamaḥ // SatvT_3.55
children.translated_text: What else shall I relate today? For you are the foremost among devotees of the Lord (<s>Bhāgavata</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 3.55
<s>Sātvata Tantra</s>, Fourth Chapter (<s>Paṭala</s>).
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:

children.text: nāsti tṛptiḥ śṛṇvato me tava vāgamṛtaṃ hareḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no satiation for me in hearing the nectar of your words about <s>Hari</s>,
His fame, supremely auspicious, grounded in the narratives of his <s>avatāras</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 4.1

children.text: tathāpi sāmprataṃ hy etac chrutvā kautūhalaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, having heard this, my curiosity now [turns to]:

children.text: bhaktibhedaṃ bhagavato bhāvanīyaṃ sadā nṛbhiḥ // SatvT_4.2
children.translated_text: The varieties of devotion (<s>bhakti-bheda</s>) to the Blessed Lord, which should always be contemplated by people. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 4.2

children.text: brūhi me bhagavan viṣṇor bhaktibhedaṃ sadāśiva /
children.translated_text: Tell me, O Blessed <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the varieties of devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yaj jñātvā hy añjasā viṣṇoḥ sāmyaṃ yāti janaḥ prabho // SatvT_4.3
children.translated_text: By knowing which a person quickly attains equality with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O Lord.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> spoke:

children.text: sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā sādho paraṃ guhyatamaṃ yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Well have you asked, O virtuous one, for this is the most secret of secrets;

children.text: anyasmai na mayā proktaṃ vinā bhāgavatān narāt // SatvT_4.4
children.translated_text: It has not been spoken by me to anyone other than a devotee of the Lord (<s>bhāgavata</s>).

children.text: yadaivāvocaṃ māṃ kṛṣṇo dhyānāt tuṣṭamanā vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: When the all-pervading <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, pleased in mind by [my] meditation, spoke to me,
At that very time the compassionate one forbade me from telling it to a non-devotee.

children.text: tadā cāhaṃ tasya pādapaṅkaje śirasā nataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then I, bowing my head at his lotus feet,

children.text: babhāṣa etad bhagavān bhaktān nirdeṣṭum arhasi // SatvT_4.6
children.translated_text: Said: 'O Lord, please designate the devotees.'

children.text: tadā prītamanā devo mām uvāca satāṃ gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the Lord, pleased in mind, the refuge of the good, said to me:

children.text: śṛṇuṣva śiva bhadraṃ te bhaktān vakṣyāmi sātvatān // SatvT_4.7
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O <s>Śiva</s>, may it be well with you; I will tell you of the <s>Sātvata</s> devotees.'
'Those devoted to meditation on me, who are my very life-breath, eager to hear my fame —

children.text: bhaktān jānīhi me deva sarvalokapraṇāmakān // SatvT_4.8
children.translated_text: Know them as my devotees, O god, who are worshipped by all worlds.'
'Supremely pleased with them, I shall tell you of the varieties of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) along with their means;

children.text: bravīmi śiva te bhaktis tenaiva samprasidhyati // SatvT_4.9
children.translated_text: O <s>Śiva</s>, your devotion succeeds through that very [teaching].'

children.text: yadi tvadvākyaniṣṭhaḥ syād yo 'pi ko 'pi sadāśiva /
children.translated_text: 'If anyone, O <s>Sadāśiva</s>, should be devoted to your word,

children.text: tasmai prītamanā vācyo bhaktibhedaḥ sasādhanaḥ // SatvT_4.10
children.translated_text: To him too, with pleased mind, should the varieties of devotion with their means be told.'

children.text: tad idaṃ te pravakṣyāmi bhaktibhedaṃ sasādhanam /
children.translated_text: 'This I shall tell you — the varieties of devotion with their means,
Since you are the foremost among devotees, delighting in the praise of the Lord.'

children.text: ekaiva bhaktiḥ śrīviṣṇoḥ prītir ity ucyate budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Devotion to <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> is one alone, called by the wise 'love' (<s>prīti</s>),
Because of its being beyond qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), undivided, and consisting of bliss, O best of twice-born.

children.text: kiṃ tu jñānakriyālīlābhedaiḥ sā trividhā matā /
children.translated_text: However, through the divisions of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), action (<s>kriyā</s>), and divine play (<s>līlā</s>), it is regarded as threefold;

children.text: tān śṛṇuṣvānupūrvyeṇa mattaḥ svavahito dvija // SatvT_4.13
children.translated_text: Hear of these from me in order, O attentive twice-born.
Unwavering mental devotion to <s>Hari</s>, who is the inner controller of all —

children.text: sā nirguṇajñānamayī sākṣād api garīyasī // SatvT_4.14
children.translated_text: That is the devotion consisting of pure knowledge (<s>nirguṇa-jñānamayī</s>), the greatest even directly.
The supreme devotion of all the senses toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of all —
That is natural, divine (<s>bhāgavatī</s>), born of [ritual] action, and disdainful of liberation.
That which arises as love-filled (<s>premamayī</s>) upon hearing and uttering the divine plays (<s>līlā</s>) of <s>Hari</s> —

children.text: satsaṅgajānyāsād grāhyā sarvadā sā hy anuttamā // SatvT_4.16
children.translated_text: Born of association with the good (<s>satsaṅga</s>), easily graspable, always supreme.
