Hear in order the complete means of practice for these, O best of beings,

children.text: yām āśritya samāpnoti jano bhaktiṃ janārdane // SatvT_4.17
children.translated_text: By resorting to which a person attains devotion to <s>Janārdana</s>.
Through one's own duty (<s>svadharma</s>) appropriate to oneself, through offering [all actions] to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
Through the practice of non-violence, and toward the images and the like of the Lord,
Through worship, praise, and joyful greeting by hearing, seeing, and touching,
Through dispassion toward sense-objects, through service to one's own teacher,
Through hearing the scriptures of renunciation, through forbearance and the like toward superiors,

children.text: sameṣu mitrabhāvena dīneṣu dayayā tathā // SatvT_4.20
children.translated_text: Through friendliness toward equals, and through compassion toward the wretched,
Through meditation on the form of the Lord, through hearing and chanting his glories,

children.text: bhūteṣu bhagavaddṛṣṭyā nirguṇā bhaktir ucyate // SatvT_4.21
children.translated_text: Through seeing the Lord in all beings — [thus] the <s>nirguṇā</s> (transcendent) devotion is described.

children.text: labdhvā tāṃ nirguṇāṃ bhaktiṃ muktiṃ cāpi na manyate /
children.translated_text: Having attained that <s>nirguṇā</s> devotion, one does not even regard liberation [as important];
That very [devotion] is called liberation, for it brings about the state of the Lord.
Now hear, O best of beings, of the means of <s>bhāgavatī</s> (divine) devotion,

children.text: yat sarvayatnataḥ kāryaṃ puruṣeṇa manīṣiṇā // SatvT_4.23
children.translated_text: Which should be performed with all effort by a wise person.
Through the instruction of the holy teacher, with hearts devoted to the Lord's devotion,
Service at the feet of the Lord should be performed through one's own faculties as appropriate:

children.text: vācoccāro harer nāmnāṃ karṇābhyāṃ karmaṇāṃ śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: With the voice, the utterance of the names of <s>Hari</s>; with the ears, hearing of his deeds;
With the hands, service to the body, images, and the like of the Lord;
With the tongue, joyfully partaking of the food-offerings (<s>naivedya</s>) given by the Lord;
With the nose, smelling the fragrance clinging to the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
With the head, bearing the garland-remnants (<s>nirmālya</s>) of the Lord's body;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā viṣṇujanādīnām īkṣaṇaṃ sādareṇa ca // SatvT_4.27
children.translated_text: With the eyes, respectfully gazing upon the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others;
With the mind, contemplation of the Lord's form; with the head and chest,

children.text: bāhupādādibhir viṣṇor vandanaṃ parayā mudā // SatvT_4.28
children.translated_text: With the arms, feet, and other [limbs], salutation to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with supreme joy;
Bringing of wealth and other [things] entirely for the Lord's purpose —
Through these means of one's own, constant service at the feet of the Lord

children.text: āśu sampadyate bhaktiḥ kṛṣṇe bhāgavatī satī /
children.translated_text: Quickly brings about true <s>bhāgavatī</s> devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
When all the senses naturally develop

children.text: svābhāvikī ratir abhūt sā vai bhāgavatī matā /
children.translated_text: A spontaneous attachment to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Person — that is regarded as <s>bhāgavatī</s> [devotion].

children.text: etadbhaktiparo vipra cāturvargyaṃ na manyate // SatvT_4.31
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> devoted to this devotion does not even regard the four goals of life (<s>cāturvargya</s>);

children.text: tasyām antaḥ sarvasukham adhikaṃ vāpi labhyate /
children.translated_text: Within it, all happiness is found, and even more.
Now, O best of twice-born, [hear] the cause of love-filled (<s>premamayī</s>) devotion;
Listen with a trusting and resolute mind.

children.text: sadguror upadeśena labdhvā satsaṅgam ādṛtaḥ // SatvT_4.33
children.translated_text: Through the instruction of a true teacher, having reverently obtained the company of the good (<s>satsaṅga</s>),
Hearing from the good of the four kinds of deeds of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: teṣv evaṃ kīrtanaṃ teṣāṃ manasā cāpi cintanam // SatvT_4.34
children.translated_text: And likewise, chanting of those [deeds] and also contemplating them with the mind,
Vocal recitation of them, and praising those who are devoted to them;

children.text: yady aśakto bhavet kīrtau smaraṇe cāpi sarvaśaḥ // SatvT_4.35
children.translated_text: If one is unable to [perform] chanting and remembrance in full,

children.text: tadā tu bhagavannāmnām āvṛttau vṛttayet sadā /
children.translated_text: Then one should always engage in the repetition of the Lord's names.

children.text: sadā śaśvat prītiyukto yaḥ kuryād etad anvaham // SatvT_4.36
children.translated_text: One who constantly performs this every day with love —

children.text: tasyāśu bhaktiḥ śrīkṛṣṇe jāyate sadbhir ādṛtā /
children.translated_text: Devotion to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, honored by the good, quickly arises for him.

children.text: evaṃ premamayīṃ labdhvā bhittvā saṃsāram ātmanaḥ // SatvT_4.37
children.translated_text: Having thus obtained love-filled [devotion], having broken through one's own <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth),
One quickly attains peace (<s>śānti</s>) that bestows supreme bliss.
Having attained [it], the devotees [contemplate] the form, character, qualities, and deeds of the Lord —

children.text: nānusaṃdhatta etā vai vinā bhaktiṃ janārdane /
children.translated_text: They do not pursue any of these apart from devotion to <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: yady anyasādhanāny anyabhaktau kuryād atantritaḥ // SatvT_4.39
children.translated_text: If one, without slothfulness, should employ other means for another [type of] devotion,

children.text: na tatra kaścid doṣaḥ syād dharisevā yataḥ kṛtā /
children.translated_text: There is no fault in that, since service to <s>Hari</s> has been performed.

children.text: kiṃ tu yad bhaktiniṣṭhā syāt tām evāpnoti mānavaḥ // SatvT_4.40
children.translated_text: But whatever devotion one is established in, that alone does a person attain.

children.text: phalabhedena bhedaḥ syāt sādhanena na bhidyate /
children.translated_text: The distinction is in the fruit, not in the means.

children.text: pṛthag eṣa mayākhyāto bhaktibhedaḥ sasādhanaḥ // SatvT_4.41
children.translated_text: Thus separately I have told you of the varieties of devotion with their means.
Desireless, consisting of fruit, eternal, surpassing the happiness of liberation —

children.text: sakāmaḥ saguṇo vipra bahudhokto maharṣibhiḥ // SatvT_4.42
children.translated_text: The desire-laden [variety], with qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>), O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, has been described in many ways by the great sages.

children.text: kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmy adya vada māṃ dvijasattama /
children.translated_text: What more shall I tell you today? Speak to me, O best of twice-born.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> spoke:

children.text: vidheyaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tvayā me surasattama /
children.translated_text: You have told me all that is to be done, O best of gods;

children.text: niṣedhanīyaṃ kiṃ cātra bhaktistambhakaraṃ ca yat // SatvT_4.43
children.translated_text: What is to be prohibited here, and what causes obstruction to devotion,
And what causes decline and increase, as well as the chief means of practice —
Tell me [all this], O great god, to me who am devoted to faith and service.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> spoke:
Whatever is external to the devotions and their means, O great sage —

children.text: niṣedhanīyaṃ tat tāsāṃ bhaktānāṃ puruṣottame // SatvT_4.45
children.translated_text: That is to be prohibited for those devotees of the Supreme Person.
Excessive attachment to the course of bodily [existence] and esteem for sense-objects —
These are said to cause obstruction to devotion in one established in devotion, O best of twice-born.
In brief I have told you of prohibitions and obstructions;

children.text: bhaktighnadoṣaṃ śṛṇu taṃ sarvathā varjanaṃ nṛṇām // SatvT_4.47
children.translated_text: Now hear of the faults that destroy devotion — [they are] to be avoided by people in all circumstances.
In the <s>nirguṇā</s> [devotion], violence to living beings; in the <s>bhāgavatī</s>, egoism;

children.text: premamayyāṃ satāṃ dveṣo bhaktināśakarā ime // SatvT_4.48
children.translated_text: In the <s>premamayī</s>, hatred of the good — these destroy devotion.
Transgression of all [types of] devotion [and] disrespect for the teacher's word —

children.text: dveṣeṇa narakaṃ yāti kurvan bhaktim api dvijaḥ // SatvT_4.49
children.translated_text: Through hatred, even a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> performing devotion goes to hell.

children.text: doṣadṛṣṭyā doṣavān syāt tatra doṣaphalaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Through a fault-finding outlook one becomes faulty; for that, the fruit of fault occurs.

children.text: martyadṛṣṭyā kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ bhavet kuñjaraśaucavat // SatvT_4.50
children.translated_text: All that is done with a mortal outlook becomes like the bathing of an elephant.
Service to the teacher, always reverently [performed], is indeed the chief of all means,

children.text: yayā bhaktir bhagavati hy añjasā syāt sukhāvahā // SatvT_4.51
children.translated_text: By which devotion to the Lord easily becomes bliss-bestowing.
Therefore, with all effort, through reverence for the teacher's word,

children.text: kāryā saiva tu tat sarvā bhagavadbhaktivardhinī // SatvT_4.52
children.translated_text: That very [service] should be performed, for it is the increaser of all devotion to the Lord.
One established in <s>nirguṇā</s> devotion should always practice compassion to beings;
In <s>bhāgavatī</s> [devotion], the full engagement of body, mind, and speech [is the means];

children.text: premamayyāṃ satāṃ prītyā śravaṇaṃ yaśasāṃ hareḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>premamayī</s> [devotion], hearing the glories of <s>Hari</s> with love for the good —

children.text: mukhyāḥ sādhanasampattyaḥ kathitās te dvijottama // SatvT_4.54
children.translated_text: These are the chief accomplishments of the means, told to you, O best of twice-born.
Taking refuge at the feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is declared as the root of all,

children.text: yad vinā sravate bhaktir āmabhāṇḍāt payo yathā // SatvT_4.55
children.translated_text: Without which devotion leaks away, as milk from an unbaked vessel.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> spoke:
Tell me, O most knowledgeable one, of taking refuge at the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: vinā yena pumān yāti kurvan bhaktim api śramam // SatvT_4.56
children.translated_text: Without which a person, even performing devotion, comes to [mere] exhaustion.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> spoke:
The complete establishment of body, speech, and mind directly in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Person —

children.text: pariniṣṭhāśrayaṃ yad vai śaraṇaṃ parikīrtitam // SatvT_4.57
children.translated_text: That indeed is declared as taking refuge (<s>śaraṇa</s>).

children.text: etad vai trividhaṃ proktaṃ vedavidbhir dvijottama /
children.translated_text: This is said to be of three kinds by the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, O best of twice-born:

children.text: prathamaṃ madhyamaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kramaśaḥ śṛṇu tan mune // SatvT_4.58
children.translated_text: First, middle, and best — hear of them in order, O sage.
When one's conviction is established in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as the protector from sin in [matters of] <s>dharma</s>, sacred sites, gods, and the like —

children.text: yad buddhiniṣṭhitaṃ kṛṣṇe kṛtaṃ tat prathamaṃ smṛtam // SatvT_4.59
children.translated_text: That is considered the first [level of refuge].
When the sense of 'mine' regarding wife, sons, friends, wealth, house, cattle, and the like

children.text: yan mamatvāśrayaṃ kṛṣṇe kṛtaṃ tan madhyamaṃ smṛtam // SatvT_4.60
children.translated_text: Is established in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — that is considered the middle [level of refuge].
When the self-identification with the body and all else, even the very selfhood of the self,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ kṛṣṇapādābje kṛtaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ prakīrtitam // SatvT_4.61
children.translated_text: Is placed at the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> ��� that is proclaimed as the best [level of refuge].

children.text: īśvaraṃ tadadhīnaṃ ca taddharmaṃ ca sanātanam /
children.translated_text: The Lord, what depends on him, and his eternal <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: hitvānyad āśrayaṃ tasya vastuto naiva dṛśyate // SatvT_4.62
children.translated_text: Apart from that, no other refuge is truly seen for him.
One endowed with this refuge, devoted to the Supreme Person,
With <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) abiding in his heart, purifies all the worlds.

children.text: tasmād bhaktādṛter viṣṇor deho 'pi naiva satpriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, without reverence for the devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, even the body is not dear to the good,
How much less the other things such as splendors, which are [already] of the nature of supreme bliss.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> spoke:

children.text: bhaktānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sākṣād brūhi me surattama /
children.translated_text: Tell me directly, O best of gods, the characteristics of devotees,

children.text: tathaiva teṣv ahaṃ prītiṃ kariṣyāmi samāhitaḥ // SatvT_4.65
children.translated_text: So that I may likewise cultivate affection for them with attentive mind.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> spoke:

children.text: bhaktānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sākṣād durvijñeyaṃ nṛbhir mune /
children.translated_text: The characteristics of devotees are directly hard to discern by [ordinary] people, O sage;

children.text: vaiṣṇavair eva tad vedyaṃ padāny ahir aher iva // SatvT_4.66
children.translated_text: They are to be known by <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> alone — as the tracks [of a serpent are known] by a serpent.

children.text: tathāpi sāratas teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yad alaukikam /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, the essential characteristics of those [devotees], which are extraordinary —

children.text: vakṣye tat te muniśreṣṭha viṣṇubhakto yato bhavān // SatvT_4.67
children.translated_text: I shall tell you, O best of sages, since you are a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Their minds [are fixed] on me, free from egoism, devoid of the sense of 'mine,'
Following the scriptures, tranquil, friends of all embodied beings.

children.text: yadā sarveṣu bhūteṣu hiṃsantam api kaṃcana /
children.translated_text: When they do not harm any being — even one that harms [them] —

children.text: na hiṃsanti tadā muktā nirguṇā bhagavatparāḥ // SatvT_4.69
children.translated_text: Then [they are] liberated, beyond qualities, devoted to the Lord.

children.text: harisevāṃ vinā kiṃcin manyante nātmanaḥ priyam /
children.translated_text: They consider nothing dear to themselves other than service to <s>Hari</s>;
Devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [they direct] the activities of body, home, and senses [toward him].
Free from attachment and aversion, devoid of [concern for] honor and dishonor,

children.text: sadā saṃtuṣṭamanaso bhaktā bhāgavatā matāḥ // SatvT_4.71
children.translated_text: Always of contented mind — these are considered <s>bhāgavata</s> devotees.
Supremely loving toward the good, pure, established in hearing, chanting, and uttering [the Lord's name],
Devoid of attachment and affection for worldly conversation about the three goals [of life],
Doers of the words of the good, with minds eager for the fame of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
These devotees, devoted to the love of <s>Hari</s>, are worshipped by the worlds.

children.text: bhaktānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ hy etat sāmānyena nirūpitam /
children.translated_text: This has been the characteristics of devotees described in general;

children.text: idānīm ātmajijñāsyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu // SatvT_4.74
children.translated_text: Now hear the threefold characteristics that you wish to know about the self.

children.text: sarvātmānaṃ hariṃ jñātvā sarveṣu prītimān naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Hari</s> as the self of all, a person who has love for all,

children.text: sevāparo dveṣahīno janeṣu sa ca sattamaḥ // SatvT_4.75
children.translated_text: Devoted to service, free from hatred toward people — he is the best.
Knowing <s>Viṣṇu</s> as all-pervading, yet having graduated love

children.text: śreṣṭhamadhyamanīceṣu hy ātmanaḥ sa tu madhyamaḥ // SatvT_4.76
children.translated_text: For the superior, middling, and inferior — he is the middle [type].

children.text: pratimādiṣv eva harau prītimān na tu sarvage /
children.translated_text: Having love for <s>Hari</s> only in images and the like, not in his all-pervading [form],

children.text: prāṇiprāṇavadhatyāgī prākṛtaḥ sa tu vaiṣṇavaḥ // SatvT_4.77
children.translated_text: Refraining from taking the life-breath of living beings — he is an ordinary (<s>prākṛta</s>) <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
One whose all senses [have] a natural attachment (<s>rati</s>) to <s>Hari</s> —

children.text: sa vai mahābhāgavato hy uttamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // SatvT_4.78
children.translated_text: He is declared to be the supreme, the great devotee (<s>mahābhāgavata</s>). // SatvT_4.78

children.text: yasya yatnenendriyāṇāṃ viṣṇau prītir hi jāyate /
children.translated_text: He by whose effort love for <s>Viṣṇu</s> arises in the senses —

children.text: sa vai bhāgavato vipraḥ madhyamaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ // SatvT_4.79
children.translated_text: that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is called the middling devotee (<s>bhāgavata</s>). // SatvT_4.79
He whose service to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> through the senses is performed without love —

children.text: sa prākṛto bhāgavato bhaktaḥ kāmavivarjitaḥ // SatvT_4.80
children.translated_text: he is the ordinary (<s>prākṛta</s>) devotee (<s>bhāgavata</s>), a devotee free from [selfish] desire. // SatvT_4.80
He who always, with love, utters what has been heard of <s>Hari</s>'s divine play (<s>līlā</s>) —

children.text: sa vai mahābhāgavato hy uttamo lokapāvanaḥ // SatvT_4.81
children.translated_text: he is the supreme great devotee (<s>mahābhāgavata</s>), a purifier of the world. // SatvT_4.81

children.text: śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ viṣṇau prītyāyāsau tu yo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: The man who, with love and effort,

children.text: kuryād aharahaḥ śaśvat prītimān sa ca madhyamaḥ // SatvT_4.82
children.translated_text: performs hearing and chanting of <s>Viṣṇu</s> day after day, constantly — he is the middling, endowed with love. // SatvT_4.82

children.text: yāmaikamātraṃ yaḥ kuryāc chravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ hareḥ /
children.translated_text: He who performs hearing and chanting of <s>Hari</s> for even a single watch (<s>yāma</s>)
with love, free from hatred toward the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — he is called ordinary (<s>prākṛta</s>). // SatvT_4.83
If the characteristics of another [grade] are observed in a devotee by the virtuous,

children.text: tathāpi niṣṭhām ālakṣya taṃ taṃ jānīhi sattama // SatvT_4.84
children.translated_text: even so, discerning his [primary] allegiance (<s>niṣṭhā</s>), know him accordingly, O best one. // SatvT_4.84
Those devotees who are steadfast in their respective <s>dharma</s>, O best of the twice-born —
the practice arising from association with them is the supreme cause of love [for the Lord]. // SatvT_4.85

children.text: tathāpi nirguṇā ye ca ye ca bhāgavatā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, those who are beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>nirguṇa</s>) and those who are regarded as <s>bhāgavatas</s> —

children.text: teṣu prītir mahābhāga duṣkareti mayocyate // SatvT_4.86
children.translated_text: love for them, O greatly blessed one, is said by me to be difficult [to attain]. // SatvT_4.86
You should constantly cultivate love toward those devoted to hearing and serving <s>Hari</s>'s divine play,

children.text: kāryā prītis tava harer yathā bhaktir na naśyati // SatvT_4.87
children.translated_text: so that your devotion to <s>Hari</s> does not perish. // SatvT_4.87

children.text: ity etat kathitaṃ vipra sādhūnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Thus has been told to you, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the characteristics of the virtuous, separately;
cultivating love toward devotees is the cause of liberation for all people. // SatvT_4.88
Through [this] means, O child, the distinctions of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) have been set forth by me;
this [path] is applicable to all castes (<s>varṇas</s>), pure, and removes the impurities of all stages of life (<s>āśramas</s>). // SatvT_4.89
It exists at all times, is eternal, and bestows perfection in all regions;
it is approved in all four <s>yugas</s> and accomplishes what is dear to the Lord. // SatvT_4.90
<s>Sātvatatantra</s>, Fifth Chapter (<s>Pañcama Paṭala</s>)
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
You have told me, O teacher of the gods, the characteristics of devotion to the Lord,
which is approved in all four <s>yugas</s> and brings happiness to all the worlds. // SatvT_5.1
Now tell me, O Lord of the gods, for the welfare of all beings,
the means of liberation through service to <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>, suited to each <s>yuga</s>. // SatvT_5.2

children.text: prajānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ viṣṇor bhūtir liṅgaṃ pṛthagvidham /
children.translated_text: The characteristics of the people, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s manifestation (<s>bhūti</s>), the various marks (<s>liṅga</s>),

children.text: dharmaṃ ca nāmasaṃkhyā ca samāsena sureśvara // SatvT_5.3
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s>, and the number of names — [tell me these] in brief, O Lord of the gods. // SatvT_5.3
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: kṛte yuge prajāḥ sarvāḥ śuddhā rāgādivarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>, all beings are pure, free from passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like,

children.text: autpattikena yogena śāntāḥ śamadṛśo matāḥ // SatvT_5.4
children.translated_text: tranquil by innate disposition (<s>autpattika yoga</s>), with vision of peace (<s>śama</s>) — so it is held. // SatvT_5.4
For them, meditation on the Lord (<s>bhagavad-dhyāna</s>) is what carries [them] across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: tad eva paramo dharmas tadyugasya mahāmate // SatvT_5.5
children.translated_text: that alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of that <s>yuga</s>, O great-minded one. // SatvT_5.5

children.text: taddhyānaṃ trividhaṃ proktaṃ daśabhir nāmabhir yutam /
children.translated_text: That meditation is declared to be threefold, endowed with ten names:
<s>nirālamba</s> (supportless), <s>sāvalamba</s> (with support), and <s>sarvāntaryāmi-dhāraṇa</s> (contemplation of the all-pervading inner controller). // SatvT_5.6
One should perform that [meditation] endowed with six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>), culminating in the supreme <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: duḥkhagrahaṃ nirālambaṃ prathamaṃ śṛṇu sattama // SatvT_5.7
children.translated_text: hear first about the supportless (<s>nirālamba</s>) [meditation], which is difficult to grasp, O best one. // SatvT_5.7

children.text: ahiṃsā brahmacaryaṃ ca satyaṃ lajjā hy akāryataḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), modesty (<s>lajjā</s>) from wrongdoing,

children.text: asteyo 'saṃcayo maunam asaṅgam abhayaṃ dayā // SatvT_5.8
children.translated_text: non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), non-accumulation (<s>asaṃcaya</s>), silence (<s>mauna</s>), non-attachment (<s>asaṅga</s>), fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>), compassion (<s>dayā</s>), // SatvT_5.8

children.text: dharme sthairyaṃ ca viśvāso yamā dvādaśa sattama /
children.translated_text: steadfastness in <s>dharma</s>, and faith (<s>viśvāsa</s>) — [these are] the twelve restraints (<s>yamas</s>), O best one.

children.text: yamādyam aṅgaṃ prathamaṃ kuryād dhyātā hy atandritaḥ // SatvT_5.9
children.translated_text: The meditator should perform the <s>yamas</s> as the first limb, without sloth. // SatvT_5.9

children.text: dehaśaucaṃ manaḥśaucaṃ jāpyaṃ homaṃ tapo vratam /
children.translated_text: Bodily purity (<s>deha-śauca</s>), mental purity (<s>manaḥ-śauca</s>), chanting (<s>jāpya</s>), fire-offering (<s>homa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), vows (<s>vrata</s>),
ancestral rites (<s>śrāddha</s>), hospitality to guests (<s>atithi-śuśrūṣā</s>), pilgrimage (<s>tīrtha-sevā</s>) that bestows satisfaction, // SatvT_5.10
effort for the benefit of others (<s>parārthehā</s>), service to the teacher (<s>guru-sevā</s>) — [these] twelve are called observances (<s>niyamas</s>).

children.text: kuryād dhyānaṃ dvitīyāṅgaṃ tṛtīyāṅgaṃ ca me śṛṇu // SatvT_5.11
children.translated_text: [The practitioner] should perform [these]; meditation is the second limb; hear from me the third limb. // SatvT_5.11
With the tips of the feet touching one's own knees, placing the shins in between,

children.text: utsaṅgamadhye hastau dvau tat sthānam āsanaṃ smṛtam // SatvT_5.12
children.translated_text: both hands in the middle of the lap — that posture is known as the seat (<s>āsana</s>). // SatvT_5.12
With the mantra of <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) alone, through inhalation (<s>pūraka</s>), retention (<s>kumbhaka</s>), and exhalation (<s>recaka</s>),

children.text: viparyayeṇa vā kuryāt turyāṅgaṃ prāṇasaṃyamam // SatvT_5.13
children.translated_text: or in reverse order, one should perform breath-control (<s>prāṇa-saṃyama</s>) as the fourth limb. // SatvT_5.13

children.text: viṣayebhyas tv indriyāṇāṃ saṃyamaṃ manasā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: The withdrawal of the senses from their objects, [directing them] with the mind into the heart —

children.text: kuryād atandrito yogī pratyāhāraṃ tu pañcamam // SatvT_5.14
children.translated_text: the diligent <s>yogī</s> should perform <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense-withdrawal) as the fifth [limb]. // SatvT_5.14

children.text: prāṇena manasaḥ sākṣāt sthairyaṃ dhyānāṅgam uttamam /
children.translated_text: The steadying of the mind directly through <s>prāṇa</s> — [this is] the supreme limb of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>);
the concentrated <s>yogī</s> should perform it while gazing at the tip of his own nose. // SatvT_5.15
That which is radiant (<s>tejomaya</s>), self-luminous, beyond the range of speech and mind —

children.text: lakṣīkṛtya dhiyā tiṣṭhed yāvan naiva prakāśate // SatvT_5.16
children.translated_text: having fixed it with the intellect, one should remain [in contemplation] until it does not manifest [i.e., until it fully manifests]. // SatvT_5.16
Thus practicing day after day, the <s>yogī</s>, purified of all sins,

children.text: cirāt prāpnoti paramāṃ samādhiṃ brahmaṇaḥ padam // SatvT_5.17
children.translated_text: after a long time attains the supreme <s>samādhi</s>, the state of <s>Brahman</s>. // SatvT_5.17

children.text: sāvaśeṣaṃ harer dhyānaṃ śṛṇu vipra samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: Hear in brief about meditation on <s>Hari</s> with support (<s>sāvaśeṣa</s>), O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: tenaiva vidhinā yukto manasā cintayed yathā // SatvT_5.18
children.translated_text: equipped with that same method, one should meditate with the mind as follows: // SatvT_5.18
In the middle of the pericarp of the heart-lotus, [one should contemplate] <s>Hari</s> in a body of pure <s>sattva</s> (<s>śuddha-sattva</s>);
one should meditate on the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) with four arms, resembling pure crystal, // SatvT_5.19
wearing matted locks (<s>jaṭā</s>), clad in bark (<s>valkala</s>), with an upper garment of black antelope skin (<s>kṛṣṇa-sāra-ajina</s>),
bearing a rosary (<s>akṣamālā</s>), a sacred thread (<s>yajña-sūtra</s>), and also a staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) and water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>), // SatvT_5.20
bearing [these], worshipped in both <s>yugas</s>, a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), imperishable;
with a lotus-like face, a beautiful nose, beautiful brows, and a beautiful forehead; // SatvT_5.21
shining like a piece of gold, with beautiful teeth, and a conch-like neck;
with long and extended four arms, adorned with sprout-like hands; // SatvT_5.22
with beautiful eyes, a beautiful heart, a beautiful belly marked with [three] folds (<s>vali</s>);
with a deep navel, and beautiful, charming thighs, knees, shanks, and feet, auspicious; // SatvT_5.23
with beautiful petal-shaped fingers, radiant with the luster of crescent-moon nails —

children.text: evaṃ cintayato rūpaṃ viṣṇor lokamanoharam // SatvT_5.24
children.translated_text: thus, for one who contemplates this form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, captivating to the world, // SatvT_5.24
supreme bliss and prosperity will swiftly come to him;
and from this, the contemplation of the all-pervading inner controller (<s>sarvāntaryāmi-dhāraṇa</s>), which quickly bestows perfection — // SatvT_5.25
hear attentively, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, free from pride and arrogance:
all this [world], moving and unmoving, is pervaded by the form of the Lord. // SatvT_5.26
One should contemplate [this] with body, speech, and mind free from hatred, O twice-born;

children.text: uttamān mānayed bhaktyā samān mitratayā dvija // SatvT_5.27
children.translated_text: one should honor the superior with devotion, and regard equals as friends, O twice-born. // SatvT_5.27
One should treat the inferior with compassion, and ignore enemies with compassion;

children.text: evaṃ bhāvayatas tasya yāvat sarvātmadarśanam // SatvT_5.28
children.translated_text: thus, for one who contemplates in this way, until the vision of the Self in all [arises], // SatvT_5.28
he shall soon attain with the mind the flood of supreme bliss.
In the <s>Tretā Yuga</s>, all beings are devoted to chanting (<s>japa</s>) and fire-offering (<s>homa</s>), // SatvT_5.29
well-disciplined, of happy conduct, of great households, and great-souled.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu bhagavadyāgo hy añjasā muktisādhakaḥ // SatvT_5.30
children.translated_text: For them, sacrifice to the Lord (<s>bhagavad-yāga</s>) is the direct means of liberation. // SatvT_5.30

children.text: sa eva paramo dharmas tretāyāṃ dvijasattama /
children.translated_text: That alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s> in <s>Tretā</s>, O best of the twice-born.

children.text: tasmin yajanti raktābhaṃ yajñamūrtiṃ jagadgurum // SatvT_5.31
children.translated_text: In that [<s>yuga</s>], they worship [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] in a red-hued form, the embodiment of sacrifice (<s>yajña-mūrti</s>), the teacher of the world, // SatvT_5.31
with regular and occasional sessions (<s>sattras</s>) and sacrifices (<s>yāgas</s>) accompanied by the eight names,

children.text: traividyena vidhānena yānti muktiṃ tadā janāḥ // SatvT_5.32
children.translated_text: through the threefold Vedic procedure — thus do people attain liberation. // SatvT_5.32

children.text: dvāpare tu janā hṛṣṭāḥ puṣṭāḥ karmakṛtikṣamāḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>Dvāpara</s>, the people are joyful, nourished, and capable of performing rites,
[but] with minds attached to enjoyments, enveloped in [the duality of] happiness and sorrow. // SatvT_5.33
For them, worship of the Lord (<s>bhagavat-pūjana</s>) is the supreme means of liberation;

children.text: sāṅgopāṅgaṃ kevalaṃ ca dvividhaṃ pūjanaṃ smṛtam // SatvT_5.34
children.translated_text: worship is held to be of two kinds: with ancillary parts (<s>sāṅgopāṅga</s>) and simple (<s>kevala</s>). // SatvT_5.34

children.text: tad eva paramo dharmo dvāparasya yugasya vai /
children.translated_text: That alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Dvāpara Yuga</s> indeed;
in that [<s>yuga</s>], men worship [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] bearing the characteristics described by the great king, // SatvT_5.35
of yellow color, with Vedic mantras, along with the twelve names.

children.text: kalau prajā mandabhāgyā alasā duḥkhasaṃyutāḥ // SatvT_5.36
children.translated_text: In <s>Kali</s>, the people are of meager fortune, lazy, and afflicted with suffering; // SatvT_5.36
devoted to the belly and the genitals, petty, wretched, and of impure mind.

children.text: teṣām ekavidhaṃ proktam añjasā muktikāraṇam // SatvT_5.37
children.translated_text: For them, one single means is declared as the direct cause of liberation — // SatvT_5.37
the chanting of the names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>kṛṣṇa-nāma-anukīrtana</s>), which bestows all happiness;
for at the beginning of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>, the Lord, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), // SatvT_5.38
having descended, spread his pure fame that destroys the stain of <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: dhyānayogakriyāḥ sarvāḥ sa saṃhatya dayāparaḥ // SatvT_5.39
children.translated_text: Having gathered together all the practices of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), <s>yoga</s>, and ritual (<s>kriyā</s>), he, full of compassion, // SatvT_5.39

children.text: svakīye yaśasi sthāpya gato vaikuṇṭham uttamam /
children.translated_text: established [them all] in his own fame and departed to the supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.

children.text: sa tāta paramo devo devakīdevinandanaḥ // SatvT_5.40
children.translated_text: He, O dear one, the Supreme God, the son of <s>Devakī Devī</s>, // SatvT_5.40
dark-blue like an indigo gem (<s>indranīla</s>) — it is he who is worshipped with <s>tantras</s> and <s>mantras</s>.

children.text: tasmin kaliyuge vipra śrutvā hariyaśo 'malāḥ // SatvT_5.41
children.translated_text: In that <s>Kali Yuga</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having heard the pure fame of <s>Hari</s>, // SatvT_5.41

children.text: prāyo bhaktā bhaviṣyanti tasmāc chreṣṭhayugaḥ kaliḥ /
children.translated_text: most [people] will become devotees; therefore <s>Kali</s> is the best of <s>yugas</s>.

children.text: ataḥ kṛtādiṣu prajāḥ kalau sambhavam ātmanaḥ // SatvT_5.42
children.translated_text: Hence, people in <s>Kṛta</s> and other [<s>yugas</s>] desire their own birth in <s>Kali</s>, // SatvT_5.42
being devoted to <s>dharma</s>, for the sake of devotion to the Lord.

children.text: dhyāneneṣṭayā pūjanena yat phalaṃ labhyate janaiḥ // SatvT_5.43
children.translated_text: The fruit that is obtained by people through meditation, sacrifice, and worship // SatvT_5.43

children.text: kṛtādiṣu kalau tad vai kīrtanādiṣu labhyate /
children.translated_text: in <s>Kṛta</s> and other [<s>yugas</s>] — that very [fruit] is obtained in <s>Kali</s> through chanting (<s>kīrtana</s>) and the like.

children.text: na deśakālakartṇāṃ niyamaḥ kīrtane smṛtaḥ // SatvT_5.44
children.translated_text: No restriction of place, time, or agent is prescribed for chanting; // SatvT_5.44

children.text: tasmāt kalau paro dharmo harikīrteḥ sukīrtanam /
children.translated_text: therefore, in <s>Kali</s>, the supreme <s>dharma</s> is the proper chanting of <s>Hari</s>'s glory.
For the learned ones dwelling in the [other] three <s>yugas</s> praise <s>Kali</s>, // SatvT_5.45
where by mere chanting one attains the supreme abode.

children.text: kṛtādāv api ye jīvā na muktā nijadharmataḥ // SatvT_5.46
children.translated_text: Even those beings in <s>Kṛta</s> and other [<s>yugas</s>] who were not liberated by their own <s>dharma</s> // SatvT_5.46
shall also attain liberation in <s>Kali</s> by mere chanting.

children.text: kaler doṣasamudrasya guṇa eko mahān yataḥ // SatvT_5.47
children.translated_text: For the one great virtue of <s>Kali</s>, which is an ocean of faults, is this: // SatvT_5.47
by the congregational chanting of the names alone (<s>nāma-saṃkīrtana</s>), a person obtains the four goals of life (<s>caturvarga</s>).
Even in <s>Kṛta</s> and other [<s>yugas</s>], O chief of the twice-born, the chanting of <s>Hari</s>'s names, // SatvT_5.48

children.text: tapādisādhyaṃ tad bhūyaḥ kalāv ubhayatāṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: achievable through austerity and the like, has in <s>Kali</s> attained a twofold status [as both means and goal].

children.text: tasmāt kaliyuge viṣṇor nāmakīrtanam uttamam // SatvT_5.49
children.translated_text: Therefore, in <s>Kali Yuga</s>, the chanting of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s names is the supreme // SatvT_5.49
means for those established in devotion (<s>bhakti-niṣṭha</s>), and is also proclaimed as the goal itself.

children.text: yena kenāpi bhāvena kīrtayan satataṃ harim // SatvT_5.50
children.translated_text: He who constantly chants <s>Hari</s> with whatever disposition (<s>bhāva</s>), // SatvT_5.50

children.text: hitvā pāpaṃ gatiṃ yānti kim utacchraddhayā gṛṇan /
children.translated_text: casting off sin, attains the [supreme] destination — how much more so one who chants with faith!

children.text: kalau nāmaparā eva satataṃ dvijasattama // SatvT_5.51
children.translated_text: In <s>Kali</s>, those who are exclusively devoted to the Name (<s>nāma-para</s>), O best of the twice-born, // SatvT_5.51
are called great devotees (<s>mahābhāgavatas</s>), who act in ways dear to the Lord.

children.text: tasmāt sarvātmanā vipra kuru śrīkṛṣṇakīrtanam // SatvT_5.52
children.translated_text: Therefore, with your entire being, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, perform the chanting of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>; // SatvT_5.52

body.text: śraddhayā satataṃ yukta etad eva mahāphalam // SatvT_5.53
body.translated_text: always endowed with faith — this alone bears the greatest fruit. // SatvT_5.53

children.translated_text: <s>Sātvatatantra</s>, Sixth Chapter (<s>Ṣaṣṭha Paṭala</s>)
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
You have told me, O Lord, about the chanting of <s>Hari</s>'s names,
which destroys sins, bestows great happiness, and is the cause of devotion to the Lord. // SatvT_6.1
Among those names which I chant, O best of the gods,

children.text: tāny ahaṃ jñātum icchāmi sākalyena kutūhalāt // SatvT_6.2
children.translated_text: I wish to know them in their entirety, out of curiosity. // SatvT_6.2
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: bhūmyambutejasāṃ ye vai paramāṇūn api dvija /
children.translated_text: Even the atoms of earth, water, and fire, O twice-born,

children.text: śakyante gaṇituṃ bhūyo janmabhir na harer guṇān // SatvT_6.3
children.translated_text: can be counted, but not the qualities of <s>Hari</s>, even in many births. // SatvT_6.3
Nevertheless, I shall speak the principal and supremely wonderful

children.text: nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ pārvatyai yadi hoktaṃ kṛpālunā // SatvT_6.4
children.translated_text: thousand names of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>, as once told by the compassionate one to <s>Pārvatī</s>. // SatvT_6.4
Seeing me established in <s>samādhi</s>, the fair-complexioned <s>Pārvatī</s>

children.text: apṛcchat paramaṃ devaṃ bhagavantaṃ jagadgurum // SatvT_6.5
children.translated_text: asked the supreme Lord, the blessed teacher of the world. // SatvT_6.5

children.text: tadā tasyai mayā prokto matparo jagadīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the thousand names were told by me to her — [names of] the Lord of the universe, who is devoted to me,

children.text: nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ ca tathā guṇakarmānusārataḥ // SatvT_6.6
children.translated_text: in accordance with his qualities and deeds. // SatvT_6.6
I shall now tell them to you, for you are a great devotee (<s>mahābhāgavata</s>);
[these names], by the mere remembrance of a single one of which, a person attains perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). // SatvT_6.7
[I meditate upon him] resembling a rising fresh rain-cloud, whose abode is unobstructed, clad in captivating yellow garments blazing with fire-like radiance,
adorned with a crown, armlets, and garlands of brilliant rays, resplendent with a girdle, bracelets, and rings; // SatvT_6.8
whose lotus-feet are worshipped by the hosts of gods led by <s>Brahmā</s>, who is attended by <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), whose entire appearance is beautiful,

children.text: gogopavanitāmunivṛndajuṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ purāṇapuruṣaṃ manasā smarāmi // SatvT_6.9
children.translated_text: who is frequented by cows, cowherds, women, and multitudes of sages — I meditate with the mind on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>. // SatvT_6.9
<s>Oṃ</s> — salutation to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>).
To the destroyer of the afflictions of those who bow, to the bestower of supreme bliss.

children.text: oṃ śrīkṛṣṇaḥ śrīpatiḥ śrīmān śrīdharaḥ śrīsukhāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Oṃ. <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, the glorious, Bearer of <s>Śrī</s>, Abode of <s>Śrī</s>'s happiness,

children.text: śrīdātā śrīkaraḥ śrīśaḥ śrīsevyaḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ // SatvT_6.11
children.translated_text: Giver of <s>Śrī</s>, Maker of <s>Śrī</s>, Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, Served by <s>Śrī</s>, Manifester of <s>Śrī</s>.
The Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Controller,
Supreme Bliss, the Supreme Abode, the Bestower of Supreme Bliss.
Without support, without modification, without attachment, without obstruction,
Eternally blissful, eternally liberated, without desire, dear to the desireless.
Sweet-spoken, doer of what is dear, giver of what is dear, creator of what is dear,

children.text: priyānugaḥ priyālambī priyakīrtiḥ priyāt priyaḥ // SatvT_6.14
children.translated_text: Follower of the dear, attached to the dear, of dear fame, dearer than the dearest.
The great renouncer, the great enjoyer, the great yogin, of great austerity,

children.text: mahātmā mahatāṃ śreṣṭho mahālokapatir mahān // SatvT_6.15
children.translated_text: The great-souled, the best of the great, the great lord of the worlds, the great one.
Of accomplished purpose, of accomplished resolve, bestower of accomplishments, the means of accomplishment,
Lord of the accomplished, foremost on the path of accomplishment, the sole protector of the world of the perfected.

children.text: iṣṭo viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭo mahiṣṭho jiṣṇur uttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The desired, the most distinguished, desired by the virtuous, the greatest, victorious <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, the supreme,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaś ca sarveṣṭo viṣṇur bhrājiṣṇur avyayaḥ // SatvT_6.17
children.translated_text: The eldest, the best, desired by all, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the radiant, the imperishable.

children.text: vibhuḥ śambhuḥ prabhur bhūmā svabhūḥ svānandamūrtimān /
children.translated_text: The all-pervading, the auspicious, the lord, the infinite, the self-existent, of the form of self-bliss,

children.text: prītimān prītidātā ca prītidaḥ prītivardhanaḥ // SatvT_6.18
children.translated_text: The loving, the giver of love, the bestower of love, the increaser of love.
The Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, attainable through <s>Yoga</s>, the Master of <s>Yogins</s>, one who has crossed beyond <s>Yoga</s>,
The giver of <s>Yoga</s>, the Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, the bestower of the attainments of <s>Yoga</s>.
Of truthful vows, devoted to truth, the thrice-true, the cause of truth,
The refuge of truth, the seizer of truth, the protector of the good, the increaser of truth.
The bliss of all, the remover of all, the all-pervading, the subduer of all,
The protector of all, the happiness of all, the ocean of all assemblies of Vedic hymns.
<s>Janārdana</s> (the agitator of people), the Lord of the universe, the protector of the universe, the father of the universe,
The creator of the universe, the sustainer of the universe, the embodiment of universal bliss.
Lord of the earth, lord of the worlds, lord of heaven, lord of the living,
Lord of knowledge, lord of wealth, lord of the good, lord of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>).
Of fourfold self, four-armed, bestower of the fruits of the four aims of life,
Of fourfold emanation (<s>caturvyūha</s>), of four abodes, the ordainer of the four ages (<s>yugas</s>).
The primordial god, the god of gods, the lord of gods, the sustainer of gods,
The maker of gods, the supporter of gods, the god whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods.
The lord of the universe, of universal form, the universal self, facing all directions,
The creator of the universe, the giver of universal fruits, the all-pervading, the leader of the universe.
The creator of beings, the sustainer of beings, existence itself, the self of beings, the nourisher of beings,
The giver of prosperity, the expanse of prosperity, prosperity itself, the protector of prosperity.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, resting on the waters, the creator from the waters, the life of the waters,
The sole bestower of fruits to the waters, the liberator of the waters, the leader of the waters.
Of a thousand forms, of a thousand names, of a thousand bodies,
Of a thousand heads, possessing a thousand feet, eyes, arms, and heads.
Lotus-naveled, lotus-wombed, bearing a lotus, with lotus-like eyes,
Reclining on a lotus, garlanded with lotuses, with the mark of lotuses on both feet.

children.text: vīryavān sthairyavān vāgmī śauryavān dhairyavān kṣamī /
children.translated_text: Valorous, steadfast, eloquent, courageous, patient, forgiving,

children.text: dhīmān dharmaparo bhogī bhagavān bhayanāśanaḥ // SatvT_6.31
children.translated_text: Wise, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, enjoying, the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), the destroyer of fear.
The ever-victorious, the triumphant, the conqueror, the giver of victory, the increaser of victory,

children.text: amāno mānado mānyo mahimāvān mahābalaḥ // SatvT_6.32
children.translated_text: Without pride, the giver of honor, the honorable, of great majesty, of great strength.
Content, giver of contentment, the giver, the tamer, compassionate toward the humble,
Wise, glorious, steadfast, the abode of endurance, vigor, and strength.
<s>Hayagrīva</s> (the horse-headed), of great radiance, the sportsman in the great ocean,
The destroyer of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, the creator of the <s>Vedas</s>, the protector of the <s>Vedas</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, and <s>Sanātana</s>,
Of unbroken vow of celibate <s>Brahman</s>-realization, the Self, the discriminator of <s>Yoga</s>.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s>, the divine sage, the initiator of [the distinction between] action and non-action,
The author of the <s>Sātvata Āgama</s>, the indicator of what is beneficial and harmful to the world.
The primordial Time, the essence of sacrifice, born from the nostril of <s>Brahmā</s>,
Bearing the globe of the earth on the tip of his tusk, the destroyer of the strength of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
The lord of the earth, of swift speed, containing the ocean within his hair-pores,
Whose breath shakes the golden mountain, praised by <s>Prajāpati</s>.
<s>Ananta</s> (the Infinite), the supporter of the earth, dwelling on the floor of the netherworld,
Swift as the fire of desire, the king of <s>Nāga</s> kings, of great splendor.
The great Tortoise (<s>Mahākūrma</s>), whose body is the universe, the bearer of <s>Śeṣa</s>, the protector of all,
The lord of the hosts of the world's ancestors, whose great abode is praised by the ancestors.
Full of compassion, self-manifest, the increaser of <s>Dhruva</s>'s love,
Whose feet are praised by <s>Dhruva</s>, the giver of the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshipped by the worlds.
The Pure One (<s>Śukla</s>), gratified by <s>Kardama</s>'s austerity, whose mind is pleased by austerity,
The granter of the mind's desires, who made the lake dance with drops of joy.
<s>Yajña</s> (Sacrifice), the lord of the hosts of gods, the slayer of <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>,
The protector of <s>Manu</s>, the guardian of the world, the creator of the birth of the world-protectors.
Named <s>Kapila</s>, the propounder of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, born from the body of <s>Kardama</s>,
The lord of all hosts of <s>Siddhas</s>, the giver of the final goal to <s>Devahūti</s>.
<s>Datta</s> (<s>Dattātreya</s>), the son of <s>Atri</s>, the <s>Yogin</s>, the shower of the path of <s>Yoga</s>,
The giver of joy to <s>Anasūyā</s>, praised by all <s>Yoga</s>-practitioners.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the sage <s>Nara</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, of great mind,
The tamer of the trident of <s>Maheśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the sole bestower of boons to <s>Maheśa</s>.
Of steadfast austerity lasting until the end of the cosmic cycle, the remover of the pride of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) and others,
Who conquered <s>Anaṅga</s> (Bodiless Love) by creating <s>Ūrvaśī</s>, the bestower of [what is] dear to <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.
<s>Ṛbhu</s>, the giver of happiness to <s>Nābhi</s>, the beloved son of <s>Merudevī</s>,
The creator of the king of <s>Yogins</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the demonstrator of the practice of <s>Yoga</s>.
Eight-armed, the purifier of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, honored by all,
The pacifier of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s lord's anger, the bestower of knowledge to <s>Dakṣa</s>.
Born in the lineage of <s>Priyavrata</s>, named <s>Gaya</s>, of great fame,
Of noble deeds, of abundant [knowledge], an ocean of hosts of great virtues.
In the form of a swan (<s>Haṃsa</s>), the speaker of truth, the discriminator of qualities and non-qualities,
The pacifier of <s>Brahmā</s>'s shame, dear to the celibate community.
The <s>Vaiśya</s> (<s>farmer-king</s>) <s>Pṛthu</s>, the milker of the earth, who caused the milking of sustenance for all living beings,
The first king, the maker of human habitations, the leveler of the earth.
Whose feet are praised by <s>Pracetas</s>, of peaceful form, beautiful to behold,
The lord of the hosts of days and nights, the banner-bearer, the refuge of the unborn.
<s>Śrī Kāmadeva</s>, the sporting lover of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
The giver of delight in his own feet, the bestower of desired happiness, the destroyer of sorrow.
The all-pervading, the foremost of upholders of <s>dharma</s>, the crown of the <s>Vedas</s>, the son of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
The teacher of eighty-eight thousand sages.
<s>Satyasena</s>, the burner of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, the protector of the humble,
The friend of <s>Indra</s>, the slayer of enemies of the gods, the son of <s>Sūnṛtā</s> and <s>Dharma</s>.
<s>Hari</s>, the rescuer of the best of elephants, the destroyer of the crocodile's snare,
Who delights in the forest on <s>Trikūṭa</s> mountain, who seeks the welfare of all worlds.
The bestower of the bright happiness of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the son of the beautiful <s>Vikuṇṭhā</s>,
The doer of what is dear to <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the glorious, the revealer of his own world.
The remover of the distress of the gods afflicted by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s curse,
The churner of the milk-ocean, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Virāja</s>, the unconquered.
The bearer of Mount <s>Mandāra</s>, the Tortoise, the benefactor of gods and <s>Dānavas</s>,
Equal to the <s>Jambū</s> continent, the creator, the cause of the production of nectar.
<s>Dhanvantari</s>, the curer of disease, the milker of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), the healer of disease,
The originator of <s>Āyurveda</s>, the king of physicians, the bestower of knowledge.
The giver of fearlessness to the gods, the enchantress (<s>Mohinī</s>) of the <s>Daityas</s>, of any form desired,
The drinker of nectar for the gods, the deceiver of the wicked <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>.
The great Fish (<s>Mahāmatsya</s>), of great body, containing the ocean within his scales,
The subduer of the <s>Daitya</s> enemy of the <s>Vedas</s>, the protector of the rice-seeds.
Whose tail-blow agitates the ocean, the bestower of [what is] dear to <s>Satyavrata</s>,
The rescuer of the devoted <s>Satyavrata</s>, the demonstrator of the threefold <s>Yoga</s>.
<s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion), the tongue of the world, with conch-like ears, with claws as weapons,
Whose mane shakes the clouds, whose teeth's luster outshines [all] radiance.
The destroyer of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the remover of the pride of many <s>Dānavas</s>,
Whose lotus feet are praised by <s>Prahlāda</s>, the remover of the torment of <s>saṃsāra</s> for devotees.
The destroyer of the fear of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>, the accomplisher of the gods' purposes,
Resembling a blazing fire, the destroyer of all fears.
The destroyer of great impurity, the bestower of all desired boons,
The destroyer of the assault of Time, the destroyer of the afflictions caused by planets.
The pacifier of all diseases, the punisher of fierce enemies,
The remover of the distress of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) terrified by the fierce <s>Bhairava</s>.
Whose head is covered with the skin of <s>Brahman</s>, who has <s>Śiva</s>'s head as his sole anklet,
Having the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> as a single jewel on his head, adorned with the world-guardians.
<s>Vāmana</s> (the Dwarf), the destroyer of <s>Aditi</s>'s fear, the ornament of the community of twice-born,
Who obtained the wealth of the three worlds from <s>Bali</s> through the pretext of three steps.
Whose toenail scratched the shell of the cosmic egg, of immeasurable valor,
The originator of the sacred <s>Gaṅgā</s>, worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>, the remover of fear.
Whose foot-water destroys heaps of sin, who shows the universal form as one [vision],
The doer of what is dear to <s>Bali</s>, the milker of heaven for devotees, the wielder of the mace.
<s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), of great valor, bearing the axe, the conqueror of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>,
The destroyer of <s>Sahasrārjuna</s>, the ender of all <s>Kṣatriya</s> lineages.
The maker of an earth without <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, the conqueror of heroes, the giver of sovereignty to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
The teacher of weapons and <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Droṇa</s>, the giver of fame to the teacher <s>Maheśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>).
The sun in the lotus of the Solar dynasty, the glorious son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
<s>Śrī Rāma</s>, <s>Rāmacandra</s>, <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, of immeasurable radiance.
Resembling a dark-blue [gem], the very life and breath of <s>Kausalyā</s>,
Lotus-eyed, lotus-faced, with the mark of lotuses on his feet.
With long arms, of beautiful limbs, adorned with jeweled ornaments,
Wearing divine garments, bearing a divine bow, master of divinely ordained celestial weapons.
With sword in hand, lord of heroes, of immeasurable prowess,
Having <s>Viśvāmitra</s> as teacher, the archer, the supreme knower of archery.
Who struck <s>Tāḍakā</s>, hitting the marks on the straight path,
<s>Subāhu</s>'s [slayer], the slayer of many <s>Rākṣasas</s> endowed with great arm-strength.
The breaker of the fierce bow of the Lord of <s>Caṇḍī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), grasped by his mighty arm,
The giver of joy to <s>Janaka</s>, the beloved lord of <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>).
The destroyer of the pride of the enemy's clan, who overcame the valor of <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>),
Whose mind was attached to the kingdom [only] by his father's word, who made a festival of forest-dwelling.
The subduer of <s>Virādha</s>, whose abode was <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain,
The performer of deeds in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, made desolate by a sage's curse.
The slayer of fourteen thousand fierce <s>Rākṣasas</s>, the destroyer of <s>Khara</s>,
The pacifier of the life of <s>Triśiras</s>, the punisher of the wicked <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>.
The slayer of the disguised <s>Mārīca</s>, the remover of the anguish of separation from <s>Jānakī</s>,
The performer of the funeral rites for <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, skilled in the slaying of <s>Kabandha</s>.
The dweller in the cave of <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, who made friendship with the five monkeys,
Who hurled the great mountain [that was] the skeleton of <s>Dundubhi</s> with the tip of his left foot.
The piercer of the seven <s>Tāla</s> palm trees together with thorns, impenetrable [to others],
The slayer of <s>Vāli</s>, the lord of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, the giver of the kingdom to his friend <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Whose greatness is [shown in] the burning of <s>Laṅkā</s> by the tail of <s>Āñjaneya</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>),
Who agitated the ocean with the fury of his wrath manifest through separation from <s>Sītā</s>.
The wondrous builder of a bridge across the ocean by hurling mountain-peaks,
The remover of the fear of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> terrified by the blow of his foot.
The conqueror of the terrible army of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, distressed by the words of <s>Aṅgada</s>,
The slayer of heroes such as <s>Nikumbha</s>, <s>Kumbha</s>, <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, and others,
The severer of the heads of the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), maddened by lifting <s>Kailāsa</s>.
He who is eager to embrace <s>Sītā</s>, purified by the touch of fire,
He whose kingdom was obtained through the monkey [<s>Hanumān</s>] and the limbs of the demon king, whose refuge is his own sovereignty,
The lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the crest-jewel among all royal assemblies,
He of inconceivable deeds, the king who attained the glory of the throne,
The crusher of the wicked and evil-minded, the sole protector of the lowly and destitute,
The generator of all prosperity, the discerner of justice even for animals,
He who restored life to the son of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> consumed by the terrible austerity of a <s>śūdra</s>,
He whose heart was pained by harsh words, the one who caused the exile of <s>Sītā</s>,
The performer of the <s>Turaṅgamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), the glorious father of <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>,
He who abandoned <s>Saumitri</s> [<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>] for the sake of truth, the gatherer of righteous people,
He whose auspicious fame fills the ears, he whose glory's light destroys darkness,
<s>Bharata</s>, who renounced the royal throne out of devotion to the lotus feet of his elder brother,
Endowed with all noble qualities, the destroyer of a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) of <s>Gandharvas</s>,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, devoted to his elder brother, the destroyer of hosts of enemies of the gods,
The extinguisher of the life of <s>Indrajit</s>, the brotherly one who renounced [his own] body,
<s>Śatrughna</s>, the subduer of foes, the slayer of <s>Lavaṇa</s>,
Praiseworthy among noble brothers, a mine of qualities praised by the good,
He who reclines on a banyan leaf, the glorious <s>Mukunda</s>, the refuge of all,
He who placed the universe within his slender belly, the son of <s>Mṛkaṇḍa</s> [i.e., <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>]'s [vision], the bird [<s>Garuḍa</s>-mounted],
The first, the foremost among the hosts of gods, delighting in measured praise and obeisance,
He who accomplished the sacred counsel of the gods terrified by the dreadful body of <s>Vṛtra</s>,
Devoted to the <s>Veda</s>, praising <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, affectionate toward pious people,
He who sheltered the <s>Vālakhilya</s> sages whose bodies were sinking in water in a cow's hoofprint,
The dispeller of misfortune, the best among sacrificers, the cause of wonder to kings,
The performer of many horse sacrifices, the crest-jewel among the generous,
The son of <s>Vāsavī</s> [<s>Satyavatī</s>], <s>Vyāsa</s>, the classifier of the branches of the <s>Vedas</s>,
The teacher of the <s>Purāṇas</s> and the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, desirous of the welfare of the people in the age of <s>Kali</s>,
The delight of <s>Rohiṇī</s>'s heart, <s>Balabhadra</s>, whose refuge is strength,
<s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, the plough-handed one, whose weapon is the pestle, of spotless radiance,
He whose body is white like a conch, jasmine, and moon, the splitter of the <s>Tāla</s> [palm tree], the destroyer of <s>Dhenuka</s>,
The slayer of <s>Muṣṭika</s> and <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, he who dragged the <s>Yamunā</s> with a plough,
The taker of <s>Pralamba</s>'s life, the crusher of <s>Rukmī</s>, the destroyer of <s>Dvivida</s>,
The giver of joy to <s>Revatī</s>, the husband of <s>Rāmā</s> [<s>Revatī</s>], the slayer of <s>Balvala</s>,
He who dragged [the city of] <s>Hastināpura</s>, he whose lotus feet are worshipped by the <s>Kauravas</s>,
He whose lotus feet are praised by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, the protector of gods and <s>Yādavas</s>,
The lord of <s>Māyā</s>, the great <s>Māyā</s> himself, the commander of the great <s>Māyā</s>,
The full moon in the ocean of the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty, the beloved younger brother of <s>Baladeva</s>,
He who has a human form yet is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the completely full one, the cause of supreme exaltation,
He who is complete with all knowledge and other [perfections], of perfect bliss, the most ancient one,
The wearer of yellow garments, he who sleeps on yellow [bedding], he of great austerity in the yellow abode,
He of a great chest and mighty arms, wearing ear-ornaments of precious gems,
Adorned with a garland of golden diadems upon his radiant cheeks,
He of beautiful ears, with brilliantly shining ear-ornaments in the shape of <s>makara</s> (sea-creatures),
He of dark, curly, smooth locks of hair, with a face like moonlight,
He of a beautiful nose, with teeth like jasmine buds, with shining red lips like the <s>kokanada</s> (red lotus),
He of a gentle smile, with a gaze graced by beautiful curved eyebrows,
He with a conch-like neck, the great <s>Brahman</s>, adorned with bracelets and armlets,
The wearer of the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem] and the forest garland, the bearer of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
He whose body is marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who is characterized by all [auspicious] marks,
He of a slender belly and deep navel, faultless and without dependence [on another],
Adorned with a girdle of tinkling bells that embrace the roundness of his hips,
He of symmetrical calves and pair of knees, shining with beautiful splendor,
He whose lotus feet are marked with the signs of a banner, thunderbolt, goad, lotus, and arrow,
He whose lotus-feet nectar is drunk by swarms of bee-like devotees,
He of great mind illumined by the moonlight-radiance of his toenail-gems,
Resplendent with tinkling anklets placed upon both lotus feet,
He who is the expansive lotus shining in the sky of his own devotees' hearts,
The delight of all living beings, dear to the praise of <s>Vasudeva</s>,
The son who delights <s>Devakī</s>, the maker of joy for the world, the dispeller of devotees' fear,
He who is attended by <s>Śeṣa</s>, who reclines on <s>Śeṣa</s>, the giver of boundless honor to <s>Yaśodā</s>,
The maker of bliss for <s>Nanda</s>, the kinsman of the cowherds, cowherdesses, and the cattle-settlement,
He who delights all the people of <s>Vraja</s>, the beloved of the beloved devotees,
He whose body shines with youthful charm, he who dwells in the arms of the cowherd women,
He who drank the milk of <s>Pūtanā</s>'s purified breast, the drainer of <s>Pūtanā</s>'s life-breath,
He who stood upon <s>Pūtanā</s>'s chest, the bestower of liberation to <s>Pūtanā</s>,
He who delights all who approach him, the one who overturned the cart,
The intelligent lord who received the blessings of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the possessor of qualities such as <s>laghimā</s> (supernatural lightness),
He who seized the throat of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, the slayer of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>,
The one who generates joy for his mother, he who revealed the universe within his mouth to his mother,
Delighting in childhood play, rejoicing in childish prattle and sportive deeds,
The pleaser of cowherds and cowherdesses, the imitator of songs and dances,
He whose body is smeared with fresh butter, fond of morsels of fresh butter,
The stealer of pieces of fresh butter, the thief of fresh butter,
<s>Dāmodara</s> (bound by a rope around the belly), the uprooter of the <s>Arjuna</s> trees, the unifier of the cowherds' minds,
He who sports in the forests of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, skilled in various kinds of play,
He who dragged calves by their tails, the slayer of <s>Vatsāsura</s>,
The enemy of <s>Baka</s>, the destroyer of <s>Agha</s> [<s>Aghāsura</s>], the annihilator of the demon who kills children [<s>Bālāsura</s>],
He who delights in the smooth sandy banks caressed by the breeze of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
He who stays amidst the multitude of cowherd boys, partaking of rich food with curds,
He who brings joy to cows, cowherds, and cowherdesses, the possessor of wealth, the destroyer of delusion,
The one who generated delusion in <s>Brahmā</s>, the displayer of most wondrous sovereignty,
He whose lotus feet were praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, the breaker of the intellect [i.e., pride] of the cowherd boys,
The crusher of the pride of <s>Kālīya</s>, he who delights in the praise of the <s>Nāga</s> women,
The quencher of forest fires, the sustainer of all <s>Vraja</s>, the life of the people,
He who overcame the terrible forest fire encountered upon entering the <s>Muñja</s> forest,
He who sports happily at all times, adorned with a peacock-feather crest,
The very life of the milkmaids, skilled in the playing of the flute,
He who hid the garments of the <s>gopīs</s>, the granter of boons regarding the <s>gopīs</s>' vow,
The subduer of the pride of the [ritualist] <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the bestower of grace upon the wives of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
The destroyer of the sacrificial rite of <s>Śatakratu</s> [<s>Indra</s>], the remover of the pride and arrogance of <s>Śakra</s> [<s>Indra</s>],
The lifter of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, the bestower of fearlessness to the people of <s>Vraja</s>,
He whose fame outshines that of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, the festival of <s>Gokula</s>,
The rescuer of <s>Nanda</s>, he whose sacred narrative is heard by <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of waters,
Praised by the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s>, the revealer of his own divine abode,
He who sports with the <s>gopīs</s> maddened by the intoxicating sound of his flute,
The remover of the pride of the milkmaids, he who celebrates the singing of his own glory,
He who delights in the women of <s>Vraja</s>, the beloved of the beauties of <s>Vraja</s>,
Delighting in the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, the ornament of the great circle of the <s>Rāsa</s>,
He who fills <s>Vṛndāvana</s> forest with fragrance, he who sports on the banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
He who is sung about in the songs of the <s>gopīs</s>, the one who seized the head of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>,
The liberator of the terrified <s>Nanda</s> who was swallowed by a great serpent's mouth,
He whose feet are worshipped by <s>Sudarśana</s> [the discus], the destroyer of the wicked <s>Ariṣṭa</s>,
The enemy of <s>Keśī</s>, the slayer of <s>Vyoma</s> [<s>Vyomāsura</s>], he who heard the hymns of <s>Nārada</s>,
The pleaser of <s>Akrūra</s>, the slayer of the cruel washerman, the bestower of fine garments,
Adorned with the garland given by <s>Sudāman</s>, anointed with sandalwood paste by <s>Kubjā</s>,
He who delighted the people of <s>Mathurā</s>, the breaker of the mighty bow [of <s>Śiva</s>],
The annihilator of the army of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, worshipped by assemblies of merchants and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
The slayer of the great elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, the crusher of <s>Cāṇūra</s>,
He who created a festival for the countless men and women who came to the wrestling arena,
The destroyer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the bestower of a state of identity [liberation] upon <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s sisters,
He who made <s>Ugrasena</s> king, the maker of happiness for all the <s>Yādavas</s>,
He who brought joy to his father and mother, the bestower of grace upon <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd,
He who took refuge with the guru <s>Sāndīpani</s>, who traversed the ocean of all knowledge,
The destroyer of the demon <s>Pañcajana</s>, dear to the conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>,
He who restored the dead son of <s>Sāndīpani</s>, worshipped by <s>Kāla</s> [Death] and <s>Yama</s>,
The pacifier of the passionate anguish of <s>Sairandhrī</s> [<s>Kubjā</s>], the giver of joy to <s>Akrūra</s>,
The bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, expert in stringing various arrows,
He of impenetrable divine armor, having the glorious <s>Dāruka</s> as his charioteer,
He whose banner bears the emblem of <s>Garuḍa</s>, the lord of birds, the discus-handed one, the wielder of the mace,
He who possesses a <s>Yādava</s> army equipped with the sword <s>Nandaka</s>, bearing an inexhaustible quiver of arrows,
Unconquerable in battle by gods and demons alike, the vanquisher of the lord of the <s>Māgadha</s> army,
The destroyer of the army of <s>Māgadha</s> [<s>Jarāsandha</s>], the protector of the city of <s>Mathurā</s>,
The builder of the city of <s>Dvārakā</s>, the regulator of the stability of the world,
The generator of all prosperity, the maker of bliss for his own people,
He whose earth is touched by wish-fulfilling trees, he who brought [the assembly hall] <s>Sudharmā</s> to the earthly realm,
The destroyer of the <s>Yavana</s> demon, the fulfiller of the desires of <s>Mucukunda</s>,
He who went alone by chariot to <s>Kuṇḍina</s> at the secret counsel of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s messenger <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
The abductor of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, the one who shaved the head of <s>Rukmī</s>,
The pleaser of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, directly the husband of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>,
He who is like a bee drinking honey from the lotus-face of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>,
He who, for the sake of the <s>Syamantaka</s> [gem], conquered the bear-chief [<s>Jāmbavān</s>], his own devotee — the pure one,
He whose lotus feet were worshipped by <s>Jāmbavān</s>, directly the husband of <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
He who took the hand of <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, dear to the beautiful <s>Kālindī</s>,
The conqueror of seven sharp-horned bulls, the breaker of the host of kings,
<s>Nagnajit</s>'s daughter <s>Satyā</s> [<s>Nāgnajitī</s>]'s bridegroom, the best among leaders,
The lord of <s>Bhadrā</s>, the beloved of <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, the dear lord of <s>Mitravindā</s>,
The slayer of <s>Mura</s>, the destroyer of the general <s>Pīṭha</s>, the slayer of <s>Naraka</s> [<s>Narakāsura</s>],
He whose lotus feet are worshipped by the Earth goddess, the remover of the fear of <s>Bhagadatta</s>,
The lord of the divine women, jewels, and vehicles taken from <s>Naraka</s>,
He who enjoyed the company of sixteen thousand one hundred and eight women,
He who stole the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree at the words of the powerful <s>Satyabhāmā</s>,
The vanquisher of the strength of <s>Devendra</s>, delighting in various sports born of [his] wives,
The remover of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>'s wounded pride, undeluded by the amorous charms of women,
The father of <s>Kāmadeva</s> [i.e., <s>Pradyumna</s>], the father of <s>Sāmba</s>, having innumerable sons and grandsons,
He who severed the arms of <s>Bāṇa</s> for the sake of his grandson [<s>Aniruddha</s>] who had gone to <s>Uśā</s>,
The destroyer of <s>Nandī</s> and other <s>Pramatha</s> attendants, he who playfully conquered the great lord [<s>Śiva</s>],
He whose feet are praised by <s>Mahādeva</s>, the liberator of <s>Nṛga</s> from his suffering,
He who protected his own people by narrating the tale of the misery caused by stealing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s property,
The enemy of <s>Pauṇḍraka</s>, the taker of the head of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, ever victorious,
The destroyer of the fire-missile of <s>Śiva</s> created through the rites of <s>Sudakṣiṇā</s>'s vow,
The burner of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, he whose glory was witnessed by <s>Nārada</s>,
He of wondrous majestic sovereignty, the promulgator of all <s>dharma</s>,
He whose sacred narrative was recited by kings for the purpose of besieging <s>Jarāsandha</s>,
He who accomplished the weighty task of a true friend prompted by <s>Nārada</s>,
He who is accompanied by his wife, sons, true friends, good servants, and household,
The planner of the slaying of <s>Jarāsandha</s>, the bestower of peace upon kings,
He who acts upon the counsel of a true friend, the initiator of the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice,
He who is praised by all assemblies of sages, the cutter of the life of <s>Caidya</s> [<s>Śiśupāla</s>],
Worshipped by the people of <s>Indraprastha</s>, the deluder of <s>Duryodhana</s>,
The destroyer of the city whose fortune was given by <s>Maheśa</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] [i.e., <s>Śālva</s>'s <s>Saubha</s>], the slayer of enemies,
The cutter of the enemy <s>Dantavakra</s>, the bestower of [a high] destiny upon <s>Dantavakra</s>,
The crusher of <s>Vidūratha</s>, he who incarnated to lighten the heavy burden of the earth,
The messenger of <s>Pārtha</s> [<s>Arjuna</s>], the benefactor of <s>Pārtha</s>, devoted to <s>Pārtha</s>'s cause, the charioteer of <s>Pārtha</s>,
The dispeller of <s>Pārtha</s>'s delusion, the revealer of the <s>Gītā</s> scripture,
The bestower of liberation in its solitary form (<s>kaivalya</s>) upon the heroes whose lives departed through <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows; // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.173
The fire that consumed the wicked such as <s>Duryodhana</s> and others; the bestower of liberation upon <s>Bhīṣma</s>;
The one who received [the horse in] <s>Arjuna</s>'s horse-sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>); the one who established <s>Arjuna</s>'s kingdom. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.174
The fulfiller of <s>Pṛthā</s>'s (<s>Kuntī</s>'s) desires; the bestower of victory upon <s>Bhīma</s>; the granter of triumph to <s>Vijaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>);
The bestower of desired boons upon <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>; the one who brought joy to <s>Draupadī</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.175
The one whose feet were extolled by <s>Sahadeva</s>; the one whose form was worshipped by <s>Nakula</s>;
The one who restored the lineage of <s>Puru</s>, [whose heir] was in the womb burned by the <s>Brahmāstra</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.176
The one whose arrival in <s>Dvārakā</s> was a festival for the women of the city of the lord of the people;
The one whose great deeds were extolled by the citizens dwelling in the <s>Ānarta</s> region. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.177
The one who brings delight to the beloved; the destroyer of the poverty of his friend, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [<s>Sudāmā</s>];
The one who performs dear [deeds] for the true friend under the pretext of pilgrimage; the son of <s>Nanda</s> (<s>Nanda-nandana</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.178
The bestower of knowledge upon the <s>Gopī</s> women; the one who created a festival through the rites performed for his father;
The speaker of righteous conduct, the performer of righteous conduct, the protector of righteous conduct. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.179
The bestower of self-knowledge upon his father; the one who restored <s>Devakī</s>'s dead sons;
The one who brought joy to <s>Śrutadeva</s>; the one who increased the bliss of [the king of] <s>Mithilā</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.180
The one who subdued <s>Arjuna</s>'s pride; the one who restored the dead sons of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
The one who delights in the multitude of jewel-like women; the one whose festivity is the play of people. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.181
More blissful than ten million moons; equal in radiance to ten million suns;
Unapproachable by ten million Deaths (<s>Kṛtānta</s>); more enchanting than ten million <s>Kāmas</s> (gods of love). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.182
Wealthier than ten million <s>Kuberas</s> (kings of <s>Yakṣas</s>); more valorous than ten million <s>Maruts</s> (wind-gods);
Deeper than ten million oceans; more unshakable than ten million <s>Himālayas</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.183
Richer than ten million horse-sacrifices (<s>aśvamedha</s>); surpassing in name ten million sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>);

The destroyer of death more [potent] than ten million [draughts of] nectar (<s>pīyūṣa</s>); the fulfiller of desires more [generous] than ten million wish-fulfilling cows (<s>kāmadhuk</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.184
Richer in splendor than ten million <s>Indras</s>; the lord of ten million universes (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>);
He whose every effort is unfailing; of endless fame and boundless prowess. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.185
He whose fame fulfills all desires; whose hearing and glorification are meritorious;
He whose deeds, sung by <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, transcend all human endeavor. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.186
Without beginning, middle, or end; free from growth and decay;
The sole bestower of knowledge upon his chief devotee <s>Uddhava</s>; he whose very form is knowledge. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.187
He of fierce valor who, under the pretext of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s curse, destroyed the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty;
The bestower of heaven in bodily form, free from old age and disease; praised by the celestials. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.188
He whose fame brings bliss to those who have renounced sense-objects, the seekers of liberation, and [all] people;
He whose fame destroys the impurities of the <s>Kali</s> age; he whose hearing is auspicious. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.189
Dear to his devotees; beneficent to his devotees; the lotus [that draws] the bee-like devotees;
The protector of all merely by being remembered; the destroyer of [all binding] <s>yantras</s> and <s>mantras</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.190
He whose very name causes all prosperity to flow; the beloved of the <s>Tulasī</s> garland;
He of immeasurable form; adorned with brilliant, priceless ornaments. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.191
The sole bestower of happiness to the universe; the protector and delighter of all good people in the world;
The crest-jewel of all the gods; possessed of wondrous and infinite enjoyments. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.192
<s>Adhokṣaja</s> (beyond the reach of the senses); the life of all people; the refuge of all virtuous beings;
He whose very name shatters all fear; the destroyer of suffering merely by being remembered. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.193
He who delights in people joyful at hearing his fame; an ocean of virtues;
He of indescribable form; the refuge of the afflicted; the life of all lives. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.194
The Supreme Reality; the Supreme Object of Knowledge; the Supreme Light; the Supreme Goal;
Knowable through <s>Vedānta</s>; the Blessed Lord; an infinite ocean of bliss. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.195
He whose fame destroys the bondage of the world; the refuge of all living beings in the world;
The sole lord of the world of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>; the beloved of the people of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.196
<s>Pradyumna</s>, son of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>; the slayer of <s>Śambara</s>; dear to <s>Rati</s>;
The bearer of the flower-bow; the conqueror of the universe; the slayer of <s>Dyumat</s>'s life-breath. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.197
<s>Aniruddha</s>, the son of <s>Kāma</s> (<s>Pradyumna</s>); the source of the Word (<s>śabda-yoni</s>); of great strides;
The husband of <s>Uṣā</s>; the lord of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>; <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (lord of the senses); the lord of the mind. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.198
The illustrious teacher of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>; the ocean of all <s>Vedānta</s>;
<s>Śuka</s>, the knower of all <s>dharma</s>; honored by King <s>Parīkṣit</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.199
<s>Śrī Buddha</s>, the destroyer of wicked intellects; the one who expelled the demons from the <s>Vedas</s>;
The proclaimer of the heterodox path; the conqueror of the world without weapons. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.200
<s>Kalki</s>, the dispeller of the <s>Kali</s> age; the re-establisher of the age of truth (<s>Satya</s>);
The offspring of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>; the re-establisher of lost <s>dharma</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.201
<s>Sārasvata</s> [avatāra]; <s>Sārvabhauma</s>; the one who secured the three worlds for <s>Bali</s>;
The speaker of true <s>dharma</s> through the eighth interval [<s>Manvantara</s>]; dear to the son of <s>Virocana</s> (<s>Bali</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.202
The one who makes [creation] of waters (<s>Āpaḥkara</s>); the lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); the annihilator of the lineage of enemies of the gods;
The benefactor of <s>Śrutendra</s>; the bestower of strength and liberation upon steady heroes. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.203
<s>Viṣvaksena</s>; the friend of <s>Śambhu</s>; the protector of the tenth interval [<s>Manvantara</s>];
The benefactor of the ocean-born lineage of <s>Brahma-Sāvarṇi</s>; the promoter of the universe. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.204
<s>Dharmasetu</s> (bridge of <s>dharma</s>); the destroyer of <s>adharma</s>; the bestower of the station of medical science;
The slayer of demons; the son of <s>Arthaka</s>; of excellent speech. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.205
<s>Svadhāman</s> (self-luminous); the son of <s>Sunṛtā</s>; of true radiance; born of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
The protector of the twelfth <s>Manu</s>-age; the destroyer of the cities of the netherworld. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.206
<s>Daivahotra</s> (son of <s>Devahotra</s>); <s>Vārhata</s> [born at <s>Bṛhatī</s>]; the friend of the lord of the day;
The protector of the thirteenth interval [<s>Manvantara</s>]; the lord of yogins and those devoted to yoga. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.207
<s>Satrāyaṇa</s> (born of <s>Satrāyaṇa</s>); of mighty arms; the son of <s>Vinatā</s>'s [lineage]; the most excellent of the wise;
The sole proclaimer of the ritual portion (<s>karma-kāṇḍa</s>); the establisher of Vedic doctrine (<s>veda-tantra</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.208
<s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme); the eldest of the gods; <s>Brahmā</s>; the lord of the creators of the universe;
Born from the lotus (<s>abja-yoni</s>); riding the swan (<s>haṃsa-vāha</s>); the grandfather of all worlds. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.209
