<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the protector of the entire world; tranquil; pure; eternal;
Worthy of worship by the twice-born; an ocean of compassion; a refuge; tender-hearted toward his devotees. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.210

children.text: rudro mūḍhaḥ śivaḥ śāstā śambhuḥ sarvaharo haraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>; <s>Mūḍha</s> [bewilderer]; <s>Śiva</s>; the Ruler; <s>Śambhu</s>; the remover of all; <s>Hara</s>;

children.text: kapardī śaṃkaraḥ śūlī tryakṣo 'bhedyo maheśvaraḥ // SatvT_6.211
children.translated_text: <s>Kapardī</s> (matted-haired); <s>Śaṃkara</s> (bestower of welfare); the Trident-bearer; the Three-eyed; the Indivisible; <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.211
The overseer of all; all-powerful; the meaning of all; facing all directions;
The abode of all; the form of all; the cause of all causes. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.212

children.text: ity etat kathitaṃ vipra viṣṇor nāmasahasrakam /
children.translated_text: Thus has been recounted to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the Thousand Names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
Which pacifies all sins and bestows the fruit of all desires. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.213
It quickly purifies the mind and increases devotion to the Blessed Lord;
It removes all obstacles and bestows wondrous sovereignty. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.214
It pacifies all suffering and bestows the fruits of the four goals of human life (<s>cāturvargya</s>).

children.text: śraddhayā parayā bhaktyā śravaṇāt paṭhanāj japāt // SatvT_6.215
children.translated_text: Through hearing, reciting, and chanting with supreme faith and devotion— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.215
Daily, for people of all classes (<s>varṇa</s>) who have taken refuge at the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—

children.text: etat paṭhan dvijo vidyāṃ kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīm imām // SatvT_6.216
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> reciting this obtains learning; a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, this earth; // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.216

children.text: vaiśyo mahānidhiṃ śūdro vāñchitāṃ siddhim āpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s>, a great treasury; a <s>Śūdra</s>, the desired <s>siddhi</s> (spiritual attainment).
The thirty-two offenses that one may commit, knowingly or unknowingly, against <s>Hari</s>— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.217

children.text: nāmnā daśāparādhāṃś ca pramādād ācared yadi /
children.translated_text: And the ten offenses against the Name, if committed through negligence—

children.text: samāhitamanā hy etat paṭhed vā śrāvayej japet // SatvT_6.218
children.translated_text: If one recites this with a collected mind, or causes others to hear it, or chants it— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.218

children.text: smared vā śṛṇuyād vāpi tebhyaḥ sadyaḥ pramucyate /
children.translated_text: Or remembers it, or listens to it—one is immediately freed from all of those [offenses].

children.text: nātaḥ parataraṃ puṇyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vidyate // SatvT_6.219
children.translated_text: There is no merit (<s>puṇya</s>) greater than this in the three worlds— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.219
By the single glorification of which one is freed from the bondage of existence.

children.text: atas tvaṃ satataṃ bhaktyā śraddhayā kīrtanaṃ kuru // SatvT_6.220
children.translated_text: Therefore, constantly, with devotion and faith, perform the glorification— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.220
Of the Thousand Names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which is the cause of the Blessed Lord's delight.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
I am blessed; I have been graced by you, O one of supreme compassion,

children.text: yataḥ kṛṣṇasya paramaṃ sahasraṃ nāmakīrtitam // SatvT_6.221
children.translated_text: Since the supreme Thousand Names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has been proclaimed. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.221

children.text: yady ālasyāt pramādād vā sarvaṃ paṭhitum anvaham /
children.translated_text: If through laziness or negligence, I am unable to recite all of it every day,

children.text: na śaknomi tadā deva kiṃ karomi vada prabho // SatvT_6.222
children.translated_text: Then, O Lord, what should I do? Tell me, O Master. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.222
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: yadi sarvaṃ na śaknosi pratyahaṃ paṭhituṃ dvija /
children.translated_text: If you are unable to recite all of it every day, O twice-born,

children.text: tadā kṛṣṇeti kṛṣṇeti kṛṣṇeti pratyahaṃ vada // SatvT_6.223
children.translated_text: Then say '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' every day. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.223

children.text: etena tava viprarṣe sarvaṃ sampadyate sakṛt /
children.translated_text: By this alone, O sage among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, everything is accomplished at once;

children.text: kiṃ punar bhagavannāmnāṃ sahasrasya prakīrtanāt // SatvT_6.224
children.translated_text: How much more then by the proclamation of the Thousand Names of the Blessed Lord! // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.224
By the mere glorification of whose Name, a person crosses the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) completely—

children.text: taraty addhā prapadye taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ gopālarūpiṇam // SatvT_6.225
children.translated_text: I take refuge in that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has the form of a cowherd (<s>gopāla</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 6.225
<s>Sātvata Tantra</s>, Seventh Chapter (<s>Paṭala</s>).
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇvanti pratyahaṃ ye vai viṣṇor nāmasahasrakam /
children.translated_text: Those who every day hear the Thousand Names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: kīrtayanty athavā vipra saṃsmaranty ādareṇa vā // SatvT_7.1
children.translated_text: Or glorify them, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or remember them with reverence— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.1

children.text: vā śataṃ vā viṃśatiṃ vāpi daśa vā pañca vā dvija /
children.translated_text: Whether a hundred, or twenty, or even ten, or five, O twice-born,

children.text: ekaṃ vā kāmato bhaktyā viṣṇupādāmbujāśrayāḥ // SatvT_7.2
children.translated_text: Or even one [name], out of desire or devotion, having taken refuge at the lotus feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.2

children.text: teṣāṃ phalasya puṇyānāṃ nāntaṃ paśyāmi nārada /
children.translated_text: I cannot see the end of the meritorious fruit of those [devotees], O <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: yatas tair bhagavān eva parānando vaśīkṛtaḥ // SatvT_7.3
children.translated_text: Since by them the Blessed Lord himself, of supreme bliss, is won over. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.3

children.text: yato nāmaiva paramaṃ tīrthaṃ kṣetraṃ ca puṇyadam /
children.translated_text: For the Name alone is the supreme <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), the merit-bestowing sacred ground (<s>kṣetra</s>);

children.text: nāmaiva paramaṃ daivaṃ nāmaiva paramaṃ tapaḥ // SatvT_7.4
children.translated_text: The Name alone is the supreme deity; the Name alone is the supreme austerity. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.4

children.text: nāmaiva paramaṃ dānaṃ nāmaiva paramā kriyā /
children.translated_text: The Name alone is the supreme gift; the Name alone is the supreme ritual act;

children.text: nāmaiva paramo dharmo nāmaivārthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // SatvT_7.5
children.translated_text: The Name alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s>; the Name alone is declared the supreme wealth. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.5

children.text: nāmaiva kāmo bhaktānāṃ mokṣo 'pi nāma kevalam /
children.translated_text: The Name alone is the [fulfillment of] desire for devotees; liberation too is the Name alone;

children.text: eṣāṃ ca sādhanaṃ nāma kāmināṃ dvijasattama // SatvT_7.6
children.translated_text: And the Name is the means [to all these] for those who have desires, O best of the twice-born. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.6

children.text: nāmaiva paramā bhaktir nāmaiva paramā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: The Name alone is supreme devotion (<s>bhakti</s>); the Name alone is the supreme goal;

children.text: nāmaiva paramaṃ jāpyaṃ nāmaiva prārthanaṃ param // SatvT_7.7
children.translated_text: The Name alone is the supreme object of recitation (<s>jāpya</s>); the Name alone is the supreme prayer. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.7
For the desireless, the Name is wealth, possessing the value of liberation and enjoyment alike;

children.text: nāma syāt paramaṃ saukhyaṃ nāmaiva vairāgyakāraṇam // SatvT_7.8
children.translated_text: The Name is the supreme happiness; the Name alone is the cause of detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.8
The Name purifies the <s>sattva</s> (being); the Name is remembered as the bestower of knowledge;
For those seeking liberation, it is the abode of liberation; for the desirous, it grants all desires. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.9

children.text: vaiṣṇavānāṃ phalaṃ nāma tasmān nāma sadā smaret /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, the Name is the [supreme] fruit; therefore, one should always remember the Name.
Whether uttered accidentally, in jest, in contempt, or in fever and suffering— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.10
The Name of the Blessed Lord, when glorified, is remembered as the destroyer of all sins.

children.text: yāvatī pāpanirhāre śaktir nāmni hareḥ sthitā // SatvT_7.11
children.translated_text: Whatever power resides in the Name of <s>Hari</s> for the removal of sin— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.11

children.text: tāvat pāpijanaḥ pāpaṃ kartuṃ śaknoti naiva hi /
children.translated_text: A sinful person can never commit that much sin [as the Name can destroy].

children.text: jñānājñānād dharer nāmakīrtanāt puruṣasya hi // SatvT_7.12
children.translated_text: Whether knowingly or unknowingly, through the glorification of <s>Hari</s>'s Name— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.12

children.text: pāparāśiṃ dahaty āśu yathā tūlaṃ vibhāvasuḥ /
children.translated_text: It burns the mountain of sins instantly, just as fire [burns] cotton.

children.text: saṃkīrtitaṃ harer nāma śraddhayā puruṣeṇa vai // SatvT_7.13
children.translated_text: The Name of <s>Hari</s>, glorified by a person with faith— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.13
Bestows its true fruit upon that person gradually, O best of the twice-born:

children.text: pāpanāśaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ vairāgyaṃ ca caturvidham // SatvT_7.14
children.translated_text: Destruction of sin, great merit, and the fourfold detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>); // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.14
Service to the teacher, self-realization, the destruction of delusion, and then—

children.text: sampūrṇānandabodhaṃ ca tatas tasmin labhet sthiram // SatvT_7.15
children.translated_text: The stable attainment of perfect bliss-consciousness (<s>sampūrṇānanda-bodha</s>). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.15
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
The fourfold detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>) has been mentioned by you, O best of the gods;

children.text: etad varṇaya lokasya hitāya jñānakāraṇam // SatvT_7.16
children.translated_text: Describe this for the welfare of the world—the cause of knowledge. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.16
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:
When a person engages in the enjoyment of sense-objects free from attachment—
That, O best of the twice-born, is called '<s>amāna</s>' (absence of pride/indifference). // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.17
When one's activity is carried on even though the enjoyable is devoid of relish—

children.text: dvitīyo vyatirekākhyas tad vijānīhi sattama // SatvT_7.18
children.translated_text: That second [type], called '<s>vyatireka</s>' (discrimination/detachment), know it, O noble one. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.18
When there is no delight in the mind, yet the senses alone partake of enjoyment—

children.text: bhogas tṛtīyaḥ puruṣair indriyākhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // SatvT_7.19
children.translated_text: That third [type] is called '<s>indriya</s>' (sense-based [detachment]) by [the wise]. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.19
The supreme absence of attachment in both mind and senses,
The withdrawal from sense-objects, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—that fourth [type] is proclaimed. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.20

children.text: eṣa nāma paraś cāśu jāyate dvijasattama /
children.translated_text: This supreme [detachment] arises quickly, O best of the twice-born,

children.text: jñānaṃ ca paramaṃ śuddhaṃ brahmānandapradāyakam // SatvT_7.21
children.translated_text: Along with supreme, pure knowledge that bestows the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.21

children.text: tīrthair dānais tapobhiś ca homair jātyair vratamaikhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through sacred fords, gifts, austerities, fire-oblations, births, vows, and fasts,

children.text: yogaiś ca vividhair vipra yad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // SatvT_7.22
children.translated_text: And through various forms of yoga, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>— // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.22

children.text: na yānti mānavās tad vai nāmakīrtanamātrataḥ /
children.translated_text: People do not attain it; but through the mere glorification of the Name,

children.text: saṃyānty eva na saṃdehaṃ kuru vipra haripriyam // SatvT_7.23
children.translated_text: They certainly do attain it—there is no doubt. Practice what is dear to <s>Hari</s>, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! // <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> 7.23
Even one burdened with great sins, having glorified the Teacher of the World (<s>Jagadguru</s>)—

children.text: taraty eva na saṃdehaḥ satyam eva vadāmy aham // SatvT_7.24
children.translated_text: he crosses over [saṃsāra] without a doubt — I speak the truth. // SatvT_7.24
And casting off the impurity of the age of <s>Kali</s> and all sins,

children.text: hitvā nāmaparo vipra viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati // SatvT_7.25
children.translated_text: one who is devoted to the Name, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // SatvT_7.25
Therefore, by the Name alone, a person crosses the ocean of worldly existence;

children.text: pumān atra na saṃdeho vinā nāmāparādhataḥ // SatvT_7.26
children.translated_text: there is no doubt about this — except through offenses against the Name (<s>nāmāparādha</s>). // SatvT_7.26
Therefore, a person who desires his own welfare, O best of the twice-born,

children.text: viṣṇor na kuryān nāmnas tu daśapāpān kathaṃcana // SatvT_7.27
children.translated_text: should never commit the ten offenses against the Name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by any means. // SatvT_7.27
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
I have heard from the mouth of the Lord about the twenty-two offenses [against <s>Viṣṇu</s>];

children.text: viṣṇor nāmnā daśa tathā etad varṇaya no prabho // SatvT_7.28
children.translated_text: now describe for us the ten [offenses] against <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s Name, O Lord. // SatvT_7.28
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: śrūyatām aparādhān vai viṣṇor vakṣyāmi nārada /
children.translated_text: Listen — I shall speak of the offenses against <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: yān kṛtvā narakaṃ yānti mānavāḥ satataṃ mune // SatvT_7.29
children.translated_text: committing which, human beings go to hell perpetually, O sage. // SatvT_7.29

children.text: asnātvā sparśanaṃ viṣṇor vinā śaṅkhena snāpanam /
children.translated_text: Touching <s>Viṣṇu</s> [the deity] without bathing; bathing [the deity] without a conch;

children.text: aśauce sparśanaṃ sākṣād bhuktā pādodakagrahaḥ vā // SatvT_7.30
children.translated_text: touching [the deity] during a period of impurity (<s>aśauca</s>); receiving the foot-water (<s>pādodaka</s>) after eating; // SatvT_7.30

children.text: vinā śabdena pūjā ca vinā naivedyapūjanam /
children.translated_text: worship without sound [i.e., in silence when sound is required]; worship without food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>);
worship while seated on a high seat; and fanning [the deity] in the cold; // SatvT_7.31
allowing a menstruating woman to see [the deity]; and placing the bell on the ground;

children.text: pauṣe ca candanasparśo grīṣme cāsparśanaṃ tathā // SatvT_7.32
children.translated_text: applying sandalwood paste in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s> [winter]; and not applying it in summer; // SatvT_7.32

children.text: puṣpaṃ toyena saṃsparśaṃ vinā homaṃ mahotsavaḥ /
children.translated_text: touching flowers with water [that has been offered]; a great festival without a fire-offering (<s>homa</s>);

children.text: pūjāṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭhadarśam agre ca bhramaṇaṃ tathā // SatvT_7.33
children.translated_text: after performing worship, turning one's back [to the deity]; and walking in front [of the deity]; // SatvT_7.33
eating at the Lord's doorway; and being sorrowful without having eaten [the Lord's prasāda];
wearing footwear [in the temple]; and wearing a blanket in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s house; // SatvT_7.34
entering with the left foot; jumping; eating cooked food [not offered];
and spitting mucus; and cleaning the teeth with [sacrificial] grass; // SatvT_7.35
mounting a vehicle before the deity; regarding the offering (<s>naivedya</s>) as a mere material commodity;

children.text: śālagrāme sthirāyāṃ ca śileti pratimeti ca // SatvT_7.36
children.translated_text: regarding a <s>Śālagrāma</s> [stone], a permanently installed [deity], as 'a stone' or 'an image' [i.e., a mere object]; // SatvT_7.36
not praising the chanting of <s>Hari</s>; treating a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> as an ordinary person;
equating <s>Viṣṇu</s> with other deities; and offering [what is meant for <s>Viṣṇu</s>] to another [deity]. // SatvT_7.37

children.text: ete 'parādhā dvātriṃśad viṣṇor nāmnām atha śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: These are the thirty-two offenses against <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Now hear about those against the Name:

children.text: satāṃ nāmnā śive viṣṇau bhidācāryāvamānatā // SatvT_7.38
children.translated_text: perceiving a difference between <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> regarding the names of the virtuous; disrespecting the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher); // SatvT_7.38
blaspheming the <s>Vedas</s>; disputation regarding the Name; desiring sin on the strength of the Name;

children.text: nāmno dharmaiḥ sāmyabuddhir dānaṃ śraddhāvivarjitaiḥ // SatvT_7.39
children.translated_text: regarding the Name as equal to [other] religious duties; giving [the Name] to those devoid of faith; // SatvT_7.39
lack of faith even after hearing [the Name]; and egoistic attitude in chanting —

children.text: ete nāmnāṃ dvijaśreṣṭha hy aparādhā mayeritāḥ // SatvT_7.40
children.translated_text: these are the offenses against the Names, O best of the twice-born, declared by me. // SatvT_7.40
They should be avoided with effort by men, since they are causes of hell.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said: // SatvT_7.41
For ordinary (<s>prākṛta</s>) people whose minds are attached to sense objects, O Lord,

children.text: aparādhā harer āśu varjyā naiva bhavanti hi // SatvT_7.42
children.translated_text: the offenses against <s>Hari</s> cannot quickly be abandoned. // SatvT_7.42

children.text: ato yena prakāreṇa taranti prākṛtā api /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by whatever means even ordinary people can cross over

children.text: aparādhān kṛtān deva tan mamākhyātum arhasi // SatvT_7.43
children.translated_text: the offenses they have committed — please tell me that, O Lord. // SatvT_7.43
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:
Having performed a hundred circumambulations (<s>pradakṣiṇas</s>) and bowing prostrate on the ground,

children.text: aparādhaśataṃ tasya kṣamate svasya keśavaḥ // SatvT_7.44
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> forgives a hundred offenses of that person. // SatvT_7.44

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ sakṛt kṛtvā yo na jānuśiraṃ namet /
children.translated_text: He who, having performed a single circumambulation, does not bow with knees and head —

children.text: niṣphalaṃ tad bhavet tasya tasmāt pratyekaśo namet // SatvT_7.45
children.translated_text: that [circumambulation] becomes fruitless for him; therefore, he should bow after each one. // SatvT_7.45

children.text: jagannātheti te nāma vyāhariṣyanti te yadi /
children.translated_text: If they utter your name as '<s>Jagannātha</s>' (Lord of the World),

children.text: aparādhaśataṃ teṣāṃ kṣamate nātra saṃśayaḥ // SatvT_7.46
children.translated_text: a hundred offenses of theirs are forgiven — there is no doubt about this. // SatvT_7.46

children.text: nāmno 'parādhās tarati nāmna eva sadā japāt /
children.translated_text: One crosses over offenses against the Name by constant chanting of the Name itself,
except for offenses against a devotee — [for one guilty of that], the Lord's grace is withheld. // SatvT_7.47
One who takes shelter at <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s lotus feet crosses over all offenses;

children.text: viṣṇor apy aparādhān vai nāmasaṃkīrtanāt taret // SatvT_7.48
children.translated_text: even offenses against <s>Viṣṇu</s> [himself], one can cross over through <s>nāma-saṃkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting). // SatvT_7.48
But for offenses against the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, there is simply no other remedy.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:

children.text: bhaktāparādhān me brūhi yathā teṣāṃ pratikriyā /
children.translated_text: Tell me the offenses against devotees and their remedy,

children.text: anugrahāya lokānāṃ bhagavan mama cāpi hi // SatvT_7.49
children.translated_text: for the benefit of the world and for my own sake as well, O blessed one. // SatvT_7.49
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:
Seizing all the possessions of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of the twice-born;

children.text: bhartsanaṃ cottame bhakte svapne cāpi prahāraṇam // SatvT_7.50
children.translated_text: reviling a great devotee; and striking [a devotee] even in a dream — // SatvT_7.50
these are the offenses against devotees. Hear their remedy:

children.text: taddhanaṃ dviguṇaṃ dattvā kṛtvā pādābhivandanam // SatvT_7.51
children.translated_text: having given back twice the wealth and performed obeisance at his feet, // SatvT_7.51
one should say, 'Forgive me' — this [remedies] the offense of seizing wealth.

children.text: yāvat tadbhartsanaṃ kṛtvā tāvan māsān samāhitaḥ // SatvT_7.52
children.translated_text: For the reviling one has done, for that many months, with concentrated mind, // SatvT_7.52
free from envy, one should serve [that devotee]; by his grace, one is purified.

children.text: yāvaj jīvaṃ prahāre tu paricaryed atandritaḥ // SatvT_7.53
children.translated_text: In the case of striking, one should serve [that devotee] diligently for the rest of one's life; // SatvT_7.53
by his grace alone is there atonement for that sin — not otherwise.

children.text: akṛtvā niṣkṛtīn etān narakān nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ // SatvT_7.54
children.translated_text: Without performing these atonements, there is no escape from hell. // SatvT_7.54
When done unknowingly, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, it is destroyed by his [the devotee's] grace;

children.text: jñānāt tu dviguṇaṃ kuryād eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ // SatvT_7.55
children.translated_text: but when done knowingly, one should perform double [the atonement] — this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>. // SatvT_7.55

children.text: putre śiṣye ca jāyāyāṃ śāsane nāsti dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: In disciplining a son, disciple, or wife, there is no fault;

children.text: anyayā tu kṛte doṣo bhavaty eva na saṃśayaḥ // SatvT_7.56
children.translated_text: but when done toward another, fault certainly arises — there is no doubt. // SatvT_7.56

children.text: keśākarṣe padāghāte mukhe ca carpaṭe kṛte /
children.translated_text: In the case of pulling hair, kicking with the foot, or slapping on the face —

children.text: na niṣkṛtiṃ prapaśyāmi tasmāt tān na samācaret // SatvT_7.57
children.translated_text: I see no atonement; therefore, one should never engage in these. // SatvT_7.57
<s>Sātvatatantra</s>, Eighth Chapter (<s>Aṣṭama Paṭala</s>)
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: atha te sampravakṣyāmi rahasyaṃ hy etad uttamam /
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell you this supreme secret,

children.text: yac chraddhayā tu tiṣṭhan vai harau bhaktir dṛḍhā bhavet // SatvT_8.1
children.translated_text: by abiding in which with faith, firm devotion to <s>Hari</s> comes about: // SatvT_8.1

children.text: deve tīrthe ca dharme ca viśvāsaṃ tāpatāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: faith in deity, pilgrimage, and <s>dharma</s>, arising from the crossing of afflictions (<s>tāpa</s>) —
abandoning these, one should joyfully enter the shelter of the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. // SatvT_8.2
'<s>Jagannātha</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s> — he is my refuge' —

children.text: tannāmni svagurau caiva brūyād etat samāhitaḥ // SatvT_8.3
children.translated_text: one should declare this with concentrated mind regarding his Name and one's own <s>guru</s>. // SatvT_8.3
Abandoning the worship of other deities through offerings (<s>bali</s>) and the like, O twice-born,

children.text: ekam eva yajet kṛṣṇaṃ sarvadevamayaṃ dhiyā // SatvT_8.4
children.translated_text: one should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone with the understanding that he encompasses all gods. // SatvT_8.4

children.text: nityaṃ naimitakaṃ kāryaṃ tathāvaśyakam eva ca /
children.translated_text: The regular (<s>nitya</s>), occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), and obligatory (<s>āvaśyaka</s>) duties

children.text: gṛhāśramī viṣṇubhaktaḥ kuryāt kṛṣṇaṃ dhiyā smaran // SatvT_8.5
children.translated_text: a householder who is a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> should perform while remembering <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with the mind. // SatvT_8.5

children.text: eteṣu cānyadevānāṃ yā pūjā vidhinā smṛtā /
children.translated_text: In these [duties], whatever worship of other deities is prescribed by rule,

children.text: sāpi kṛṣṇārcanāt paścāt kriyeta hṛdi taṃ smaran // SatvT_8.6
children.translated_text: that too should be performed after the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, while remembering him in the heart. // SatvT_8.6

children.text: anyadā tv anyadevānāṃ pṛthakpūjāṃ na ca smaret /
children.translated_text: At other times, one should not even think of separate worship of other deities;

children.text: kāmyaṃ niṣiddhaṃ ca tathā naiva kuryāt kadācana // SatvT_8.7
children.translated_text: and one should never perform desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) or prohibited (<s>niṣiddha</s>) rites. // SatvT_8.7
Those who, abandoning wife, children, friends, and the like, have taken refuge in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: harikīrtiratā ye ca teṣāṃ kṛtyaṃ na vidyate // SatvT_8.8
children.translated_text: and are devoted to the chanting of <s>Hari</s>'s glory — for them there is no [other] duty. // SatvT_8.8
One who performs the worship of other deities with offerings, motivated by desire, O twice-born,

children.text: bhaktibhraṣṭo bhaved āśu saṃsārān na nivartate // SatvT_8.9
children.translated_text: quickly falls from devotion and does not turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s>. // SatvT_8.9
One who is driven by desire, devoid of compassion, and engages in the slaughter of animals —
he is cooked in hell for as many years as there are hairs on that animal. // SatvT_8.10

children.text: yajñe paśor ālabhane naiva doṣo 'sti yad vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: The statement that 'there is no fault in the slaughtering of an animal in sacrifice' —

children.text: api pravṛttī rāgiṇāṃ nivṛttis tu garīyasī // SatvT_8.11
children.translated_text: that is [a concession to] the inclination of the passionate; but renunciation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) is indeed superior. // SatvT_8.11
Having performed the worship of other deities and sacrificed an animal — [if] such worst of men

children.text: yadi te svargatiṃ yānti narakaṃ yānti ke tadā // SatvT_8.12
children.translated_text: go to heaven, then who goes to hell? // SatvT_8.12

children.text: sa māṃ punar bhakṣayitā yasya māṃsam adāmy aham /
children.translated_text: 'He will eat me in turn, whose flesh I eat' —

children.text: iti māṃsaniruktaṃ vai varṇayanti manīṣiṇaḥ // SatvT_8.13
children.translated_text: thus the wise explain the etymology of 'meat' (<s>māṃsa</s>). // SatvT_8.13
Having taken refuge in devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and yet engaging in the slaughter of animals,
and performing the worship of other deities — one certainly falls [from devotion]. // SatvT_8.14

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ prāpya ye jīvā na bhajanti hareḥ padam /
children.translated_text: Those beings who, having obtained a human birth, do not worship the feet of <s>Hari</s> —

children.text: te śocyā sthāvarādīnām apy ekaśaraṇā yadi // SatvT_8.15
children.translated_text: they are pitiable; even plants and the like are [better off] if they are devoted to the One Refuge. // SatvT_8.15

children.text: ahaṃ brahmā surendrāś ca ye bhajāmo divāniśam /
children.translated_text: I, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the lords of the gods — we worship [him] day and night;

children.text: tato 'dhiko 'sti ko devaḥ śrīkṛṣṇāt puruṣottamāt // SatvT_8.16
children.translated_text: what god is greater than <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>)? // SatvT_8.16
All the worlds with their guardians await his grace;

children.text: sāpi lakṣmīr yac caraṇaṃ sevate tadanādṛtā // SatvT_8.17
children.translated_text: and even <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) herself, disregarded [by others], serves his feet. // SatvT_8.17
What god is greater than <s>Janārdana</s>, the beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,

children.text: yan nāmni ke na saṃyānti puruṣāḥ paramaṃ padam // SatvT_8.18
children.translated_text: by whose Name persons do attain the supreme abode? // SatvT_8.18
The worship of whose feet is the root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> —

children.text: tato 'dhiko 'sti ko devaḥ kṛpāsindhor mahātmanaḥ // SatvT_8.19
children.translated_text: what god is greater than that great-souled ocean of compassion? // SatvT_8.19
He who always considers even a small amount of worship as great —

children.text: tato 'dhiko 'sti ko devaḥ sukhārādhyāj jagadguroḥ // SatvT_8.20
children.translated_text: what god is greater than that easily worshipped teacher of the world? // SatvT_8.20

children.text: yena kenāpi bhāvena yo 'pi ko 'pi bhajan janaḥ /
children.translated_text: Any person at all, worshipping with whatever disposition,

children.text: labhate 'bhīpsitāṃ siddhiṃ mokṣaṃ cāpy akutobhayam // SatvT_8.21
children.translated_text: attains the desired perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) and also fearless liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). // SatvT_8.21
What god is greater than the son of <s>Devakī Devī</s>,

children.text: yo jaganmuktaye kīrtim avatīrya tatāna ha // SatvT_8.22
children.translated_text: who, having descended, spread his fame for the liberation of the world? // SatvT_8.22
Therefore, abandoning the worship of other deities through offerings and the like,
by the instruction of a true <s>guru</s>, one should worship the two feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. // SatvT_8.23
One should hear daily the supremely auspicious fame of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: uccārayen mukhenaiva nāma cittena saṃsmaret // SatvT_8.24
children.translated_text: one should utter the Name with the mouth and remember [it] with the mind. // SatvT_8.24
One should cultivate love toward <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> and avoid non-devotees;

children.text: daivopalabdhaṃ bhuñjāno nātiyatnaṃ caret sukhe // SatvT_8.25
children.translated_text: enjoying what is obtained by providence, one should not exert excessively for comfort. // SatvT_8.25

children.text: gṛheṣv atithivat tiṣṭhed yady etān naiva bādhate /
children.translated_text: One should dwell in the household like a guest, as long as it does not obstruct these [practices];

children.text: eṣāṃ bādhe pṛthak tiṣṭhed vaiṣṇaveṣu ca saṅgavān // SatvT_8.26
children.translated_text: if these [practices] are obstructed, one should dwell separately, in the company of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>. // SatvT_8.26

children.text: brahmacārī gṛhī vāpi vānaprastho yatiś ca vā /
children.translated_text: Whether a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>), a householder (<s>gṛhī</s>), a forest-dweller (<s>vānaprastha</s>), or a renunciant (<s>yati</s>) —

children.text: vinā vaiṣṇavasaṅgena naiva siddhiṃ labhej janaḥ // SatvT_8.27
children.translated_text: without the association of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, no person attains perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). // SatvT_8.27

children.text: bhaktasaṅgaṃ vinā bhaktir naiva jāyeta kasyacit /
children.translated_text: Without the association of devotees, devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) is never born in anyone;

children.text: bhaktiṃ vinā na vairāgyaṃ na jñānaṃ mokṣam aśnute // SatvT_8.28
children.translated_text: without devotion, neither dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) nor knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) attains liberation. // SatvT_8.28

children.text: ata āśramaliṅgāṃś ca hitvā bhakteḥ samaṃ vaset /
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning the external marks of the <s>āśramas</s>, one should dwell in the company of devotees,

children.text: yatsaṅgāc chrutikīrtibhyāṃ harau bhaktiḥ prajāyate // SatvT_8.29
children.translated_text: by whose association, through hearing and chanting, devotion to <s>Hari</s> is born. // SatvT_8.29
Even a moment's association with a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: svargāpavargau na sāmyaṃ kim utānyasukhādibhiḥ // SatvT_8.30
children.translated_text: cannot be equaled by heaven or liberation — how much less by other pleasures! // SatvT_8.30

children.text: ato yatnena puruṣaḥ kuryāt saṅgaṃ harer janaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, a person should make every effort to associate with the people of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: tiryañco 'pi yato muktiṃ labhante kimu mānuṣāḥ // SatvT_8.31
children.translated_text: since even animals attain liberation [thereby] — how much more so humans! // SatvT_8.31
By that association alone, a person certainly attains <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: vinā vairāgyajñānābhyāṃ yato viṣṇus tadantike // SatvT_8.32
children.translated_text: without [need for] dispassion or knowledge, since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is near those [devotees]. // SatvT_8.32

children.text: yeṣāṃ saṅgāddhareḥ saṅgaṃ sakṛd ākarṇya mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: By their association, having once heard of association with <s>Hari</s>, a person

children.text: parityaktuṃ na śaknoti yadi bhadrasarid bhavet // SatvT_8.33
children.translated_text: is unable to abandon it — if he is one of auspicious flow. // SatvT_8.33
Even one who is devoid of taste (<s>arasa-jña</s>), if he somehow enters into that association,

children.text: bhūtvā rasajño 'pi mahān karmabandhād vimucyate // SatvT_8.34
children.translated_text: having become one of great taste, he is freed from the bondage of <s>karma</s>. // SatvT_8.34
Then, devoted to that <s>dharma</s>, toward the Lord of immaculate nature,
he attains the supreme devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) that fulfills all desires. // SatvT_8.35

children.text: bhaktiṃ viditvā puruṣo muktiṃ necchati kaścana /
children.translated_text: Having known devotion, no person desires liberation,

children.text: sālokyādipadaṃ cāpi kimu cānyasukhaṃ dvija // SatvT_8.36
children.translated_text: nor even the states of <s>sālokya</s> (residing in the Lord's world) and the like — how much less other pleasures, O twice-born! // SatvT_8.36

children.text: phalaṃ vinā viṣṇubhaktā muktiṃ yānti dvijottama /
children.translated_text: Devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> attain liberation without [seeking] its fruit, O best of the twice-born;

children.text: tata eva vidur nānya ānandamayam uttamam // SatvT_8.37
children.translated_text: from that [devotion] alone they know the supreme [state] full of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>), and from nothing else. // SatvT_8.37

children.text: yato harir likhitavat hṛdaye vartate sadā /
children.translated_text: For <s>Hari</s> ever abides in their hearts as if inscribed;
bound by the creeper of their love, he who is the embodiment of supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda-vigraha</s>). // SatvT_8.38
<s>Sātvatatantra</s>, Ninth Chapter (<s>Navama Paṭala</s>)
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:
Such great virtue there is, O Lord of the gods, in serving the feet of the Lord;

children.text: kuto bhajanti manujo anyadevaṃ kim icchayā // SatvT_9.1
children.translated_text: why then do people worship another deity? With what desire? // SatvT_9.1
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:
When in the primordial <s>Satya</s> [Yuga], O chief of the twice-born, the people were devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: na yajanti vinā viṣṇum anyadevaṃ kathaṃcana // SatvT_9.2
children.translated_text: they did not worship any other deity besides <s>Viṣṇu</s> at all. // SatvT_9.2
Then, for the purpose of obtaining worship for ourselves, [recognizing him as] encompassing all gods,
we worship <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> with body, speech, and mind, O twice-born. // SatvT_9.3

children.text: tadā tuṣṭo vibhuḥ prāha devadevo rameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the all-pervading Lord, pleased — the God of gods, the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — said:

children.text: avatīrya yajiṣyāmi yuṣmāṃl lokāṃś ca yājayan // SatvT_9.4
children.translated_text: 'Having descended, I shall cause you to be worshipped, and I shall also cause the worlds to worship [you].' // SatvT_9.4

children.text: tataḥ sarve janā yuṣmān yajiṣyanti samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thereafter, all people will worship you with concentrated minds;

children.text: anena pūjā yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyati sukhāvahā // SatvT_9.5
children.translated_text: by this means, worship of you will come about, bringing happiness.' // SatvT_9.5

children.text: ahaṃ coktaḥ pṛthak tena śrīnivāsena brāhmaṇa /
children.translated_text: And I was told separately by <s>Śrīnivāsa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>:

children.text: kalpitair āgamair nityaṃ māṃ gopāya maheśvara // SatvT_9.6
children.translated_text: 'Through fabricated <s>āgamas</s>, always conceal me, O <s>Maheśvara</s>. // SatvT_9.6
The supreme thousand names that destroy the sin of disrespecting me —

children.text: paṭhiṣyasi sadā bhadraṃ prārthitena mayā punaḥ // SatvT_9.7
children.translated_text: you shall always recite [them]; for your welfare, I have again been entreated [to grant this].' // SatvT_9.7

children.text: tato me hy āgamaiḥ kṛṣṇam ācchādya na tu devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, by me, through the <s>āgamas</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was concealed — but not the [other] deities;

children.text: yantrair mantraiś ca tantraiś ca darśitāḥ phaladā dvija // SatvT_9.8
children.translated_text: through <s>yantras</s>, <s>mantras</s>, and <s>tantras</s>, [the other deities] were shown as fruit-givers, O twice-born. // SatvT_9.8

children.text: tair āgamair mandadhiyā hitvā kṛṣṇaṃ jagadgurum /
children.translated_text: By those <s>āgamas</s>, people of dull intellect, abandoning <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the teacher of the world,

children.text: bhajanti devatā anyā balidānena nityaśaḥ // SatvT_9.9
children.translated_text: worship other deities constantly through offerings (<s>bali</s>). // SatvT_9.9
Having worshipped various deities with the desire for various pleasures,

children.text: bhogāvasāne te yānti narakaṃ svatamomayam // SatvT_9.10
children.translated_text: when those enjoyments are exhausted, they go to their own darkness-filled hell. // SatvT_9.10
Seeing the people in such a state, with a mind apprehensive of sin,

children.text: gato 'haṃ vāsudevasya caraṇe śaraṇaṃ dvija // SatvT_9.11
children.translated_text: I went to the feet of <s>Vāsudeva</s> for refuge, O twice-born. // SatvT_9.11
And bowing, with neck humbly inclined,
with concentrated mind, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, with palms joined, I praised <s>Puruṣottama</s>: // SatvT_9.12
'<s>Oṃ</s>, salutation to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the creator of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the friend of all beings who take shelter in the play of your feet,
who is ever self-fulfilled, the cause of the highest purpose, the treasury of knowledge and wisdom, the self-born! // SatvT_9.13

children.text: eko 'si sṛṣṭeḥ purato laye tathā yugādikāle ca vidāṃ samakṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: You are one before creation and at dissolution, and at the beginning of the <s>yugas</s>, in the sight of the wise;

children.text: anyatra nānātanubhir virājate tasmā anantācaritāya te namaḥ // SatvT_9.14
children.translated_text: elsewhere you shine forth in manifold forms — salutation to you, of infinite deeds! // SatvT_9.14
To the witness of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), time, disposition, and <s>karma</s>; to the one who acts in the sport of gathering and releasing them;

children.text: kṛṣṇāya nānātanum īyuṣe same kṛtānurāgāya namo namas te // SatvT_9.15
children.translated_text: to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has assumed manifold forms yet remains the same, to whom love has been offered — repeated salutation to you! // SatvT_9.15

children.text: śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti ye yaśo jagatpavitraṃ jagadīśitus tava /
children.translated_text: Those who hear, sing, and recite your fame, which purifies the world, O Lord of the universe —

children.text: te 'nyaṃ na paśyanti sukhāya hy ātmano vinā bhavatpādaniṣevaṇād bahiḥ // SatvT_9.16
children.translated_text: they see no other [source] for their own happiness, apart from the service of your feet. // SatvT_9.16

children.text: niṣkiṃcanā ye tava pādasaṃśrayāḥ puṣṇanti te tat sukham ātmasambhavam /
children.translated_text: Those who possess nothing and take shelter at your feet nourish that self-born happiness;

children.text: jānanti tattvena vidus tataḥ parāḥ kāmaiḥ samākṛṣṭadhiyo vicakṣaṇāḥ // SatvT_9.17
children.translated_text: they know the truth and are beyond it [worldly concerns]; the discerning ones, whose minds are drawn by [transcendental] desires, know [you]. // SatvT_9.17

children.text: ahaṃ tu sākṣāt tava pādapaṅkajaṃ nityaṃ bhajāno 'pi pṛthaṅmatir vibho /
children.translated_text: I, however, though always directly worshipping your lotus feet, O all-pervading one, with a separate [self-interested] mentality,

children.text: purātmamānaṃ pracikīrṣur ātmanaḥ sakāśato 'py adya malaṃ nikṛntayan // SatvT_9.18
children.translated_text: formerly wishing to increase my own honor, am now cutting away the impurity from myself. // SatvT_9.18

children.text: athāpi te deva padāmbujadvayaṃ nikāmalābhāya sadāstu me hareḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, may the pair of your lotus feet, O <s>Hari</s>, ever be [present] for me, for the attainment of desireless [devotion];

children.text: yac cintanāt sarvamano'nukūlāt siddhir bhavaty eva kimu prakīrtanāt // SatvT_9.19
children.translated_text: by whose contemplation — pleasing to all minds — perfection arises, how much more so by its proclamation!' // SatvT_9.19

children.text: iti me saṃstutiṃ jñātvā bhagavān praṇatārtihā /
children.translated_text: Knowing my hymn of praise, the Lord, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow,

children.text: mamākṣigocaraṃ rūpam akarot sa dayāparaḥ // SatvT_9.20
children.translated_text: made his form visible to my eyes — he who is full of compassion. // SatvT_9.20

[I beheld him] like a great <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) gem of dense bliss, with golden [ornaments] gleaming from his body, with crowns, a pair of garland-and-earrings, armlets, girdle, and bracelets,

children.text: mañjīrair vilasatpiśaṅgavalayaṃ lakṣmyāṅkitaṃ śāśvatam sarveśaṃ karuṇākaraṃ suravarair bhaktaiḥ samāsevitam // SatvT_9.21
children.translated_text: with anklets and resplendent tawny bangles, marked with <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), eternal, the Lord of all, the ocean of compassion, attended by the best of gods and by devotees. // SatvT_9.21

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tatpadapaṅkajaṃ hṛdi dadhe govindadāmodaraśrīkṛṣṇeti mukhair vadan trijagato bhartur mudāhaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: Having beheld [him], I placed those lotus feet in my heart, uttering with my mouth '<s>Govinda</s>! <s>Dāmodara</s>! <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>!' — the Lord of the three worlds — with joy;

children.text: netrair nirjharavāripūram iva me gātre ca harṣas tato vāṇyāṃ gadgadatāṃ vilokya bhagavān mām āha bhaktapriyaḥ // SatvT_9.22
children.translated_text: from my eyes flowed a torrent like a waterfall, and horripilation [arose] on my body; then, seeing the stammering in my speech, the Lord, the lover of devotees, spoke to me: // SatvT_9.22

children.text: jñatāṃ me suravarya vāñchitatarāṃ madbhaktasaṅgāvaliṃ tat te 'haṃ pravadāmi te karuṇayā bhaktāya sākaṃ varaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Know, O best of gods, the most desired [thing]: the succession of association with my devotees. I shall tell you this, out of compassion, along with boons to the devotee.

children.text: mallīlāṃ gadato bhaviṣyati bhavatsarve janā vaiṣṇavāḥ /
children.translated_text: When you narrate my divine play, all people shall become <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>;

children.text: bhāryā cāpi tayānukūlasukhadā bhaktāgraṇīr me bhavān // SatvT_9.23
children.translated_text: and your wife too, pleasing and favorable to her — you shall be the foremost of my devotees.' // SatvT_9.23

children.text: etāvad uktvā bhagavān gato lokam alaukikam /
children.translated_text: Having said this much, the Lord departed to that world beyond the worldly;

children.text: ahaṃ ca tān varāṃl labdhvā kṛtārtho 'smi dvijarṣabha // SatvT_9.24
children.translated_text: and I, having obtained those boons, became fulfilled, O bull among the twice-born. // SatvT_9.24

children.text: atas tad dinam ārabhya pārvatī bhuvaneśvarī /
children.translated_text: From that day onward, <s>Pārvatī</s>, the sovereign of the worlds,

children.text: matsaṅgād vaiṣṇavī bhūtvā mām āpṛcchat sureśvarī // SatvT_9.25
children.translated_text: having become a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> through my association, asked me, the sovereign of the gods. // SatvT_9.25
You, the great devotee, <s>Kumāra</s> and the other <s>Maheśvaras</s>,

children.text: kuberādyā devatāś ca nandīśādyāś ca me gaṇāḥ // SatvT_9.26
children.translated_text: <s>Kubera</s> and the other deities, and <s>Nandiśa</s> and the other [members of] my retinue (<s>gaṇa</s>) — // SatvT_9.26
each separately asked me, having taken refuge at the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the supremely auspicious stories that purify all the worlds. // SatvT_9.27

children.text: atha māṃ pṛcchatī vākyaṃ madvākyaṃ ca dvijottama /
children.translated_text: And while she questioned me, her words and my words, O best of the twice-born —
<s>Gaṇeśa</s>, my son, attentively records them nearby. // SatvT_9.28

children.text: mama teṣāṃ ca saṃvādaṃ kalā lokamanoharāḥ /
children.translated_text: My dialogues with them — those arts captivating to the world —

children.text: abhavaṃs tatra śāstrāṇi sarvalokahitāni vai // SatvT_9.29
children.translated_text: became the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), beneficial to all the worlds. // SatvT_9.29
Those <s>tantras</s>, the listeners shall bring to the surface of the earth

children.text: sthāne sthāne muniśreṣṭha kathayiṣyanti bhūriśaḥ // SatvT_9.30
children.translated_text: and narrate abundantly in place after place, O best of sages. // SatvT_9.30

children.text: tvam apy enaṃ sātvatākhyaṃ tantraṃ bhagavataḥ priyam /
children.translated_text: You too shall narrate this <s>tantra</s> called <s>Sātvata</s>, dear to the Lord,
before <s>Śaunaka</s> and others at <s>Naimiṣa</s> [forest]. // SatvT_9.31
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:

children.text: śrutaṃ bhagavato vaktrāt tantraṃ sātvatam uttamam /
children.translated_text: I have heard from the mouth of the Lord this supreme <s>Sātvata Tantra</s>;

children.text: tasmin hiṃsāniṣedhaṃ ca śrutvā me saṃśayo 'bhavat // SatvT_9.32
children.translated_text: having heard the prohibition of violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) therein, a doubt has arisen in me. // SatvT_9.32
Violence toward animals is enjoined by the <s>Veda</s> in sacrificial rites;

children.text: yajñe vadho 'vadhaś caiva vedavidbhir nirūpitaḥ // SatvT_9.33
children.translated_text: killing in sacrifice is [said to be] non-killing — so it has been determined by the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>. // SatvT_9.33

children.text: tanniṣedhe kathaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ karma maheśvara /
children.translated_text: If that [violence] is prohibited, how shall the <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) and <s>smārta</s> (traditional) rites
continue for all people, which bear fruit in this world and the next, O <s>Maheśvara</s>? // SatvT_9.34
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttaṃ ca dvividhaṃ karma varṇitam /
children.translated_text: Two kinds of <s>karma</s> have been described: that of engagement (<s>pravṛtta</s>) and that of withdrawal (<s>nivṛtta</s>),

children.text: śrutyā smṛtyā ca viprendra kāmyaṃ kāmijanāya vai // SatvT_9.35
children.translated_text: by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, O chief of the twice-born — the desire-motivated is for those who have desires. // SatvT_9.35

children.text: pravṛttam avirodhena kurvan svar yāti mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: A person who performs the path of engagement without transgression goes to heaven;
[but] when the merit is exhausted, he is born on the surface of the earth among those bound by <s>karma</s>. // SatvT_9.36
A <s>yogī</s> who follows the path of withdrawal, with a mind that has abandoned the desire for enjoyments,

children.text: prayāti paramāṃ siddhiṃ yato nāvartate gataḥ // SatvT_9.37
children.translated_text: attains the supreme perfection, from which one does not return once gone. // SatvT_9.37
Therefore, for one who is established in the path of engagement, attached to various desires,
only a permission (<s>abhyanujñā</s>) has been shown by the six kinds of regulations, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // SatvT_9.38

children.text: vidhir naivāsti hiṃsāyām abhyanujñā yataḥ kṛtā /
children.translated_text: There is no injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) for violence; only a permission has been made;

children.text: ato nivṛttihiṃsāyāṃ yajñe 'pi kathitā budhaiḥ // SatvT_9.39
children.translated_text: therefore, the cessation of violence even in sacrifice has been taught by the wise. // SatvT_9.39
Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is the supreme <s>dharma</s>, surpassing all <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>;

children.text: sa ca ācārato nṇām abhīṣṭaphalado bhavet // SatvT_9.40
children.translated_text: and that, when practiced by people, bestows the desired fruit. // SatvT_9.40
Especially, devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> abandon the act of violence;

children.text: ahiṃsayā hi bhūtānāṃ bhagavān āśu tuṣyati // SatvT_9.41
children.translated_text: for the Lord is quickly pleased by non-violence toward all beings. // SatvT_9.41
For the Lord, the ruler of all,
having entered into all beings, is perceived in various forms — stationary and moving. // SatvT_9.42

children.text: mayāpi hy āgame hiṃsā vihitā yā vidhānataḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the violence that has been prescribed by me in the <s>āgamas</s> according to rule —
that too is for the fulfillment of desired fruits for worldly people who are driven by desires.

children.text: viṣṇubhaktā na vāñchanti matto 'pi kiyad eva hi /
children.translated_text: Devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> do not desire [anything] even from me — how much [less from others]!

children.text: atas teṣāṃ vidhāne 'pi hiṃsā nindyā prakīrtitā // SatvT_9.43
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in their ritual system, violence is declared as censured. // SatvT_9.43
Therefore, abandoning desire-motivated rites (<s>kāmya-karman</s>) especially,
you should hear the sacred stories of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which bestow the attainment desired by all worlds. // SatvT_9.44

children.text: pravṛttaśāstraṃ śṛṇuyād yac chrutvā tatparo bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should hear the scriptures of engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) such that, having heard, one becomes devoted to that [the Lord];

children.text: nivṛtte 'pi harer bhaktiyutaṃ mukhyaṃ prakīrtitam // SatvT_9.45
children.translated_text: in the path of withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>) too, that which is accompanied by devotion to <s>Hari</s> is proclaimed as principal. // SatvT_9.45
Especially, the stories of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s divine play (<s>līlā</s>), which bring supreme auspiciousness to the world —

children.text: kīrtayasva dvijaśreṣṭha śrūyāś caiva nirantaram // SatvT_9.46
children.translated_text: proclaim [them] and hear [them] continuously, O best of the twice-born. // SatvT_9.46
Abandoning the refuge of other deities and their worship especially,

children.text: ye bhajanti hareḥ pādaṃ kṛṣṇaikaśaraṇaṃ narāḥ // SatvT_9.47
children.translated_text: those men who worship the feet of <s>Hari</s>, taking sole refuge in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — // SatvT_9.47
they are ever fulfilled in this world and the next, dear to the Lord,
and they attain the flood of supreme bliss continuously. // SatvT_9.48
But those who are without such knowledge, unpeaceful, foolish yet thinking themselves learned,

children.text: yajanty avirataṃ devān paśūn hatvā sukhecchayā // SatvT_9.49
children.translated_text: who worship gods incessantly, having slaughtered animals, out of desire for pleasure — // SatvT_9.49
when the enjoyment of their desires is exhausted, they shall certainly fall.

children.text: ity etat kathitaṃ vipra tantraṃ sātvatam uttamam // SatvT_9.50
children.translated_text: Thus has been told to you, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the supreme <s>Sātvata Tantra</s>, // SatvT_9.50
the life-sustenance of devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which bestows all perfections.

children.text: śravaṇāt kīrtanād asya kṛṣṇe bhaktir hi jāyate // SatvT_9.51
children.translated_text: By hearing and chanting of it, devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is born. // SatvT_9.51

children.text: bhaktiṃ labdhavataḥ sādho kim anyad avaśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: For a person who has obtained devotion, O virtuous one, what else remains?

children.text: yato bhagavatā proktaṃ tasya bhaktivivardhanam // SatvT_9.52
children.translated_text: For the Lord has declared that this [tantra] increases one's devotion. // SatvT_9.52
In this <s>tantra</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, has been told the supreme origin of the universe,

children.text: avatārāś ca śrīviṣṇoḥ sampūrṇāṃśakalā bhidā // SatvT_9.53
children.translated_text: and the <s>avatāras</s> of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> — the distinctions of complete, partial, and fractional [incarnations]; // SatvT_9.53

children.text: bhaktibhedāś ca bhedānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham /
children.translated_text: the varieties of devotion, the various characteristics of each [grade],
the means of liberation through service to <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> suited to each <s>yuga</s>; // SatvT_9.54
the thousand names of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the supreme greatness of the Name;

children.text: viṣṇor nāmnā vaiṣṇavānām aparādhasya ca niṣkṛtiḥ // SatvT_9.55
children.translated_text: the offenses against <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s Name and against <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, and their atonement; // SatvT_9.55
the secret essence of all, and the cause of the origin of the <s>tantras</s>;
and the injunction and prohibition regarding violence — in accordance with your questions. // SatvT_9.56

children.text: yan nāmaikaṃ karṇamūlaṃ praviṣṭaṃ vācānviṣṭaṃ cetanāsu smṛtaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: That single Name which, having entered the root of the ear, or being sought out by speech, or being remembered in consciousness,

children.text: dagdhvā pāpaṃ śuddhasattvāt taddehaṃ kṛtvā sākṣāt saṃvidhatte 'navadyam /
children.translated_text: having burnt away sin, from [the state of] pure <s>sattva</s>, directly renders the body [of the one who chants] faultless;
therefore, to the infinite one, to <s>Janārdana</s>, to the inexhaustible ocean of qualities proclaimed by the <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: mahānubhāvāya nirañjanāya nityātmalābhāya namo namas te // SatvT_9.57
children.translated_text: to the one of great glory, to the stainless one, to the one whose attainment is the eternal Self — repeated salutation to you! // SatvT_9.57
